Yn y fersiwn ddwyieithog, mae’r golofn chwith yn cynnwys yr iaith a lefarwyd yn y cyfarfod. Mae’r golofn dde yn cynnwys cyfieithiad o’r areithiau hynny.

Mae [R] yn dynodi bod yr Aelod wedi datgan buddiant wrth gyflwyno’r busnes.

In the bilingual version, the left-hand column includes the language used during the meeting. The right-hand column includes a translation of those speeches.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwmni Ynni Cyhoeddus Cymunedol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Community Public Energy Company

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa fudd ddaw i drigolion Abertawe yn sgil sefydlu cwmni ynni cyhoeddus cymunedol i Gymru? OQ64441
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What benefits will come to the residents of Swansea following the establishment of a community public energy company for Wales? OQ64441

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Wel, diolch am y cwestiwn ac, fel y Llywydd, mi wnaf innau groesawu pawb yn ôl yma ar ôl yr haf. Dwi'n sylweddoli ei bod hi wedi bod yn haf prysur iawn i bawb, ond gobeithio bod pawb wedi cael gorffwys hefyd. 

Y nod wrth sefydlu cwmni ynni cyhoeddus i Gymru ydy gwneud y defnydd gorau posib o’n hadnoddau ynni ni fel gwlad, a sicrhau bod ynni yn dod yn fwy fforddiadwy ac yn lanach, a bod mwy ohono’n eiddo i ni yma yng Nghymru. Mi fydd hyn yn helpu cymunedau, yn helpu busnesau a gwasanaethau cyhoeddus i wneud gwell defnydd o’r ynni sy’n cael ei gynhyrchu yng Nghymru.

Ar 7 Medi, mi wnaethon ni lansio ymgynghoriad ar hynny, a dwi’n edrych ymlaen at glywed barn pobl ar sut allwn ni fanteisio’n well ar ynni Cymru er budd pobl a chymunedau ym mhob rhan o’r wlad.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Well, thank you for the question and, as the Llywydd did, I will welcome everyone back after the summer. I understand that it's been a very busy summer for everyone, but I do hope that everyone had an opportunity to relax too.

Our aim in establishing a Welsh public energy company is to make the best possible use of our energy resources as a nation, ensuring that energy becomes more affordable, cleaner, and that more of it is owned by us here in Wales. This will help communities, businesses and public services to make better use of the energy produced in Wales.

On 7 September, we launched a consultation on that, and I look forward to hearing the views of people on how we can better take advantage of Welsh energy for the benefit of communities and people in all parts of Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: A publicly owned energy company based in Swansea, with a focus on supporting community and local ownership would not just positively impact communities across Gŵyr Abertawe, but also across the wider Swansea bay area. The cost-of-living crisis has impacted many thousands of people in my constituency, made worse, of course, by the closure of the furnaces over in Port Talbot, which is not so far away. Swansea has the second biggest tidal range in the world, and the city's proximity to the electric arc furnace across the bay will be an integral part of our transition to net zero. So, if it is based in Swansea, it would also provide a tangible future of sustainable careers that future generations can look forward to. With these exciting points in mind, will Swansea be considered for the potential headquarters of a community public energy company for Wales? Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Byddai cwmni ynni sydd ym mherchnogaeth y cyhoedd yn Abertawe, â phwyslais ar gefnogi perchnogaeth gymunedol a lleol, nid yn unig yn cael effaith gadarnhaol ar gymunedau ar draws Gŵyr Abertawe, ond hefyd ar draws ardal ehangach Bae Abertawe. Mae'r argyfwng costau byw wedi effeithio ar filoedd lawer o bobl yn fy etholaeth i, wedi'i waethygu, wrth gwrs, gan gau'r ffwrneisi draw ym Mhort Talbot, sydd ddim mor bell i ffwrdd. Abertawe sydd â'r ail amrediad llanw mwyaf yn y byd, a bydd agosrwydd y ddinas at y ffwrnais arc trydan ar draws y bae yn rhan annatod o'n trawsnewidiad i sero net. Felly, os yw wedi'i leoli yn Abertawe, byddai hefyd yn darparu dyfodol gwirioneddol o yrfaoedd cynaliadwy y gall cenedlaethau'r dyfodol edrych ymlaen ato. Gyda'r pwyntiau cyffrous hyn mewn golwg, a fydd Abertawe yn cael ei hystyried ar gyfer pencadlys posibl cwmni ynni cyhoeddus cymunedol i Gymru? Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I congratulate the Member on a shameless, but very, very well meaning and important plug on behalf of his constituents, and I'm sure many of you are thinking along similar lines right now. What the Member does do, of course, importantly, is reflect on the economic challenges in the area that he represents, and we will always, as a Government, seek to create opportunities for innovation and growth and job opportunities in every single part of our nation. And that will be one of the founding principles of the new development agency that we are in the process of establishing. 

The proposed new company is built around Trydan Gwyrdd Cymru, which is currently headquartered in Merthyr Tydfil. But it also has staff in other areas of Wales, and, crucially, it will be there to serve all parts of Wales and to make gains for communities wherever they are in our nation.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n llongyfarch yr Aelod ar hysbyseb di-gywilydd, ond â bwriadau da iawn, iawn a phwysig ar ran ei etholwyr, ac rwy'n siŵr bod llawer ohonoch chi'n meddwl mewn ffordd debyg ar hyn o bryd. Yr hyn y mae'r Aelod yn ei wneud, wrth gwrs, yn bwysig, yw myfyrio ar yr heriau economaidd yn yr ardal y mae'n ei chynrychioli, a byddwn bob amser, fel Llywodraeth, yn ceisio creu cyfleoedd ar gyfer arloesedd a thwf a chyfleoedd gwaith ym mhob rhan o'n gwlad. A dyna fydd un o egwyddorion sylfaenol yr asiantaeth ddatblygu newydd yr ydym ni wrthi'n ei sefydlu. 

Mae'r cwmni newydd arfaethedig wedi'i adeiladu o amgylch Trydan Gwyrdd Cymru, sydd â'i bencadlys ym Merthyr Tudful ar hyn o bryd. Ond mae ganddo staff mewn rhannau eraill o Gymru hefyd, ac, yn hollbwysig, bydd yno i wasanaethu pob rhan o Gymru ac i wneud enillion i gymunedau ble bynnag y maen nhw yn ein gwlad.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The UK has the highest industrial electricity prices in the world, north Wales paying the highest electric standing charges in Britain, and south Wales, in my constituency, pays above the average. Politicians trying to control the energy market isn't going to fix this. The problem is the cost of net zero, loaded onto working families through their bills. A combination of green taxes and regulations have led us down this path of rising bills and job losses—just look at Port Talbot, for example. So, First Minister, can you confirm that all forms of energy will be supported by this body? Otherwise, how many more Welsh jobs will have to go before this Government admits its net-zero targets are being paid for by the people who can least afford it?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Y DU sydd â'r prisiau trydan diwydiannol uchaf yn y byd, mae gogledd Cymru yn talu'r prisiau sefydlog uchaf ym Mhrydain, ac mae de Cymru, yn fy etholaeth i, yn talu mwy na'r cyfartaledd. Nid yw gwleidyddion yn ceisio rheoli'r farchnad ynni yn mynd i drwsio hyn. Y broblem yw cost sero net, wedi'i llwytho ar deuluoedd sy'n gweithio drwy eu biliau. Mae cyfuniad o drethi gwyrdd a rheoliadau wedi ein harwain i lawr y llwybr hwn o filiau cynyddol a cholli swyddi—edrychwch ar Bort Talbot, er enghraifft. Felly, Brif Weinidog, a allwch chi gadarnhau y bydd pob math o ynni yn cael ei gefnogi gan y corff hwn? Fel arall, faint yn rhagor o swyddi Cymru fydd yn rhaid iddyn nhw ddiflannu cyn i'r Llywodraeth hon gyfaddef mai'r bobl sy'n gallu ei fforddio leiaf sy'n talu am ei thargedau sero net?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I think the point I would make is that high energy prices are not as a result of a pursuit of net zero. They're not as a result of the determination that we must have—every one of us—to tackle the scourge of climate change. And we know the cost of not tackling climate change. We saw it in the wildfires that scorched so much of Wales over this summer. I hope I can persuade the Member that what we should be doing is seeking as much control as possible over how we generate electricity in Wales, how we reap the benefits of those projects in Wales, and having energy devolved to Wales as part of our toolkit as a nation to look after businesses and communities alike.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n credu mai'r pwynt y byddwn i'n ei wneud yw nad yw prisiau ynni uchel o ganlyniad i fynd ar drywydd sero net. Nid ydyn nhw o ganlyniad i'r penderfyniad y mae'n rhaid i ni feddu arno—pob un ohonom ni—i fynd i'r afael â phla newid hinsawdd. Ac rydym ni'n gwybod y gost o beidio â mynd i'r afael â newid hinsawdd. Fe wnaethom ni ei weld yn y tanau gwyllt a losgodd gymaint o Gymru dros yr haf hwn. Rwy'n gobeithio y gallaf i berswadio'r Aelod mai'r hyn y dylem ni fod yn ei wneud yw ceisio sicrhau cymaint o reolaeth â phosibl dros sut rydym ni'n cynhyrchu trydan yng Nghymru, sut rydym ni'n elwa o fanteision y prosiectau hynny yng Nghymru, a chael ynni wedi'i ddatganoli i Gymru yn rhan o'n pecyn cymorth fel cenedl i ofalu am fusnesau a chymunedau yn yr un modd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Jane Dodds.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Jane Dodds.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn, a phrynhawn da i chi, Brif Weinidog.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, and good afternoon, First Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I welcome the emphasis in the consultation on increasing community energy, and I think it's shameful and shameless of Reform UK to abandon—[Interruption.] It's my job—to abandon and just to sideline net zero. The world is on fire. As the First Minister has said, you just needed to look and see and talk to the communities that we represent over the summer just to see how bad it is.

To get back to the very good point raised by Gwyn in relation to the community energy issues, I was lucky enough to visit Hwb y Gors in the Amman valley, where community-owned wind turbines have paid for the renovation of the community centre there. But it took 10 years to secure planning permission, and we need to make it much easier for our communities to be able to own community energy. So, Prif Weinidog, what will you and the Government do to make sure that we accelerate this, so that, actually, communities can own that community energy and ensure that they see the benefits and we stop the world being on fire? Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n croesawu'r pwyslais yn yr ymgynghoriad ar gynyddu ynni cymunedol, ac rwy'n credu ei bod yn gywilyddus ac yn ddi-gywilydd i Reform UK gefnu—[Torri ar draws.] Dyma fy ngwaith—gefnu ar sero net a'i wthio o'r neilltu. Mae'r byd ar dân. Fel y mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi dweud, y cwbl yr oedd angen i chi ei wneud oedd edrych a gweld a siarad â'r cymunedau yr ydym ni'n eu cynrychioli dros yr haf dim ond i weld pa mor wael yw pethau.

I ddychwelyd at y pwynt da iawn a godwyd gan Gwyn o ran y materion ynni cymunedol, roeddwn i'n ddigon ffodus i ymweld â Hwb y Gors yn nyffryn Aman, lle mae tyrbinau gwynt sy'n eiddo i'r gymuned wedi talu am adnewyddu'r ganolfan gymunedol yno. Ond cymerodd 10 mlynedd i sicrhau caniatâd cynllunio, ac mae angen i ni ei gwneud hi'n llawer haws i'n cymunedau allu bod yn berchen ar ynni cymunedol. Felly, Brif Weinidog, beth fyddwch chi a'r Llywodraeth yn ei wneud i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n cyflymu hyn, fel y gall cymunedau, mewn gwirionedd, fod yn berchen ar yr ynni cymunedol hwnnw a sicrhau eu bod nhw'n gweld y manteision a'n bod ni'n atal y byd rhag bod ar dân? Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member is quite right, of course, about the need to accelerate our mission here, to make the most of the natural resources that we have and to take seriously our responsibilities when it comes to tackling climate change. This is what it's about—setting up a new organisation that can move more swiftly, that can look at how to work on commercial projects of a larger scale and with community energy, because it's all going to be in the mix. Climate change, and tackling climate change, is a responsibility for every single Minister in this Government. So, yes, it will involve planning, it will involve the energy Minister, it will involve the housing Minister, and so on. Where is she? She's over there. So, this is something that's owned by all of Government.

The Member is quite right, of course, on Reform. In denying climate change, they are acting against the interests of the people of Wales. In denying or wanting to curtail employment rights, they are acting against the interests of workers the length and breadth of our nation. Reform is not a party that has the interests of Wales at heart in any way, shape or form.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn llygad ei lle, wrth gwrs, ynglŷn â'r angen i gyflymu ein cenhadaeth yma, i fanteisio i'r eithaf ar yr adnoddau naturiol sydd gennym ni ac i gymryd ein cyfrifoldebau o ddifrif pan ddaw i fynd i'r afael â newid hinsawdd. Dyma wraidd y mater—sefydlu sefydliad newydd sy'n gallu symud yn gyflymach, sy'n gallu edrych ar sut i weithio ar brosiectau masnachol ar raddfa fwy a gydag ynni cymunedol, oherwydd mae'r cyfan yn mynd i fod yn y gymysgedd. Mae newid hinsawdd, a mynd i'r afael â newid hinsawdd, yn gyfrifoldeb i bob un Gweinidog yn y Llywodraeth hon. Felly, bydd, bydd yn cynnwys cynllunio, bydd yn cynnwys y Gweinidog ynni, bydd yn cynnwys y Gweinidog tai, ac yn y blaen. Ble mae hi? Mae hi draw yn y fan yna. Felly, mae hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n gyfrifoldeb i'r Llywodraeth gyfan.

Mae'r Aelod yn llygad ei lle, wrth gwrs, am Reform. Trwy wadu newid hinsawdd, maen nhw'n gweithredu yn erbyn buddiannau pobl Cymru. Trwy wrthod neu fod eisiau cwtogi hawliau cyflogaeth, maen nhw'n gweithredu yn erbyn buddiannau gweithwyr ar hyd a lled ein cenedl. Nid yw Reform yn blaid sydd â buddiannau Cymru mewn golwg mewn unrhyw ffordd, siâp neu ffurf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cefnogi Busnesau Lleol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Supporting Local Businesses

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Pa gamau mae'r Prif Weinidog yn eu cymryd i gefnogi busnesau lleol yn ardal Bangor? OQ64469
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What action is the First Minister taking to support local businesses in the Bangor area? OQ64469

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I welcome this timely question from the Member, on the same day my Government publishes plans to cut business rates by 30 per cent for pubs, restaurants, cafes, bars, licensed clubs, hotels, gyms and cinemas. More broadly, through Business Wales, we provide advice and growth support to businesses. Targeted investment in local infrastructure and funding is helping to revitalise Bangor city centre specifically. We have also established that town-centre taskforce we promised we would as part of our 100-day commitment to drive investment, increase footfall and support local businesses to grow.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n croesawu'r cwestiwn amserol hwn gan yr Aelod, ar yr un diwrnod y mae fy Llywodraeth yn cyhoeddi cynlluniau i dorri ardrethi busnes 30 y cant ar gyfer tafarndai, bwytai, caffis, bariau, clybiau trwyddedig, gwestai, campfeydd a sinemâu. Yn fwy cyffredinol, trwy Busnes Cymru, rydym ni'n darparu cyngor a chymorth twf i fusnesau. Mae buddsoddiad wedi'i dargedu mewn seilwaith a chyllid lleol yn helpu i adfywio canol dinas Bangor yn benodol. Rydym ni hefyd wedi sefydlu'r tasglu canol trefi hwnnw y gwnaethom ni addo y byddem ni'n ei wneud yn rhan o'n hymrwymiad 100 diwrnod i ysgogi buddsoddiad, i gynyddu nifer yr ymwelwyr ac i gefnogi busnesau lleol i dyfu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Your Government launched the town-centre taskforce in Bangor. Neither of the co-chairs are from the city and no Bangor trader has been named to it. The £654,000 announced that day is for an event space at Storiel, not for the high street, where shops are empty and the pavement is broken by lorries. How does the taskforce actually support local businesses on Bangor high street?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe wnaeth eich Llywodraeth lansio'r tasglu canol trefi ym Mangor. Nid yw'r naill na'r llall o'r cyd-gadeiryddion o'r ddinas ac nid oes unrhyw fasnachwr o Fangor wedi'i enwi arno. Mae'r £654,000 a gyhoeddwyd y diwrnod hwnnw ar gyfer man digwyddiadau yn Storiel, nid ar gyfer y stryd fawr, lle mae siopau'n wag a'r palmant yn cael ei dorri gan lorïau. Sut mae'r tasglu yn cefnogi busnesau lleol ar stryd fawr Bangor mewn gwirionedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I know very, very well the challenges faced by Bangor high street. It was my high street growing up, and I'm determined that when we look at Bangor, and all the other high streets throughout Wales, we have a clear focus on using all the tools at our disposal to support them. The town-centre taskforce, I remind him, is for all high streets. There has been specific assistance, to the tune of over £600,000, announced for Bangor in recent months, and I don't imagine that that is something that the people of Bangor are unhappy about. But it's always part of a range of measures that we can take as a Government. That announcement today of the 30 per cent cut in business rates is determinedly targeted at helping high streets like Bangor, through supporting those businesses that bring vibrancy, that bring life to those high streets. This is a Government from the get-go that is showing that we are determined to act on the promises that we made, and Bangor, like many other towns the length and breadth of Wales, will benefit from that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n gyfarwydd iawn, iawn â'r heriau sy'n wynebu stryd fawr Bangor. Honno oedd fy stryd fawr wrth dyfu i fyny, ac rwy'n benderfynol, pan fyddwn ni'n edrych ar Fangor, a'r holl strydoedd mawr eraill ledled Cymru, bod gennym ni bwyslais eglur ar ddefnyddio'r holl arfau sydd ar gael i ni i'w cynorthwyo. Mae'r tasglu canol trefi, rwy'n ei atgoffa, ar gyfer pob stryd fawr. Cyhoeddwyd cymorth penodol, dros £600,000, ar gyfer Bangor yn y misoedd diwethaf, a dydw i ddim yn dychmygu bod hynny'n rhywbeth y mae pobl Bangor yn anhapus amdano. Ond mae bob amser yn rhan o amrywiaeth o fesurau y gallwn ni eu cymryd fel Llywodraeth. Mae'r cyhoeddiad hwnnw heddiw o'r gostyngiad o 30 y cant i ardrethi busnes wedi'i dargedu'n benderfynol at helpu strydoedd mawr fel Bangor, trwy gynorthwyo'r busnesau hynny sy'n dod â bywiogrwydd, sy'n dod â bywyd i'r strydoedd mawr hynny. Mae hon yn Llywodraeth o'r cychwyn cyntaf sy'n dangos ein bod ni'n benderfynol o weithredu ar yr addewidion a wnaethom ni, a bydd Bangor, fel llawer o drefi eraill ar hyd a lled Cymru, yn elwa o hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Busnesau bach yw asgwrn cefn ein heconomi leol ym Mangor Conwy Môn. Enghraifft amlwg o hyn ym Mangor yw caffi Antoniazzi's, sydd wedi bod yn bresenoldeb amlwg ar y stryd fawr ers 92 o flynyddoedd bellach. Wrth siarad â nifer o fusnesau yn ddiweddar, yn aml yr un yw'r gofyn, sef cynnig teg ar gyfraddau busnes, a dwi'n edrych ymlaen at wrando ar ddatganiad y Gweinidog cyllid yn nes ymlaen y prynhawn yma yn hynny o beth. Ond ydy'r Prif Weinidog yn cytuno â mi y bydd ymrwymiad Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru i addasu cyfraddau busnes o blaid ein busnesau annibynnol bach yn rhoi’r hyder iddynt dyfu a buddsoddi, gan roi bywyd newydd i ganol ein trefi yn y broses?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Small businesses are the backbone of our local economy in Bangor Conwy Môn. A clear example of this in Bangor is Antoniazzi's cafe, which has been a prominent presence on the high street for 92 years now. In recent conversations with a number of businesses recently, the same request often rose, namely a fair deal on business rates, and I look forward to hearing the finance Minister's statement later on this afternoon about that. But does the First Minister agree with me that the Plaid Cymru Government’s commitment to adjust business rates in favour of our independent small businesses will give them the confidence to grow and invest, breathing new life into our town centres in the process?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn. Ydy, mae Antoniazzi's yn sefydliad go iawn, onid ydy, yn bron i ganrif oed. Mae'r hyn rydyn ni'n mynd i gael wedi ei amlinellu gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid y prynhawn yma yn arwyddocaol go iawn. Busnesau bach a chanolig yw asgwrn cefn yr economi, ac rydyn ni wedi ei gwneud hi'n glir, yn enwedig drwy'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni, ein bod ni'n benderfynol o gefnogi a thyfu busnesau Cymreig cynhenid, a sicrhau bod busnesau llwyddiannus yn parhau hefyd dan berchnogaeth Gymreig a rhoi'r hyder iddyn nhw fuddsoddi yn eu dyfodol. Mi fydd y newidiadau sy'n cael eu cyflwyno i dreth annomestig yn cael eu cyflwyno mor fuan â phosib o ddechrau'r flwyddyn nesaf neu'r flwyddyn ariannol nesaf. Mi fyddan nhw'n barhaol, sydd eto'n gam sy'n rhoi hyder i fusnesau, a dwi'n edrych ymlaen at gael y manylion yna gan y Gweinidog yn nes ymlaen y prynhawn yma.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question. Of course, Antoniazzi's is a well-established business of almost 100 years' standing. What we will see outlined by the Cabinet Minister for Finance this afternoon will be truly significant. SMEs are the backbone of our economy, and we've made it clear, particularly through the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy, that we are determined to support and grow indigenous Welsh businesses and to ensure that successful businesses continue in Welsh ownership, giving them the confidence to invest in their future. The changes to non-domestic rates will be introduced as soon as possible, from the beginning of next year or the next financial year. They will be permanent, which, again, is a step that gives business confidence. I look forward to hearing the details from the Minister later this afternoon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank you, John, for bringing this question, because it's really important that we don't allow Bangor high street to continue suffering as it is. When I was campaigning, and since, residents stated that there just are not enough shops, cafes or restaurants in the area. Now, I welcome the announcement of £654,000 of funding to reinvent struggling high streets in Wales, and in particular in Bangor, but some of the projects are for new street furniture and an amphitheatre. Businesses themselves are concerned as to how they will be involved in the spending. And if anyone's ever looked, when the previous Welsh Labour Government put funding grants into towns, it didn't make any difference whatsoever. Now, I note that I have previously asked, in terms of hospitality businesses, for VAT to come down to 10 per cent, and I'm pleased to say that one of your party members in Parliament is also making that call for VAT on hospitality businesses to drop to 10 per cent. Do you support her calls, and the calls of the Welsh Conservatives, to really help our tourism and hospitality businesses?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, John, am ofyn y cwestiwn hwn, oherwydd mae'n wirioneddol bwysig nad ydym ni'n caniatáu i stryd fawr Bangor barhau i ddioddef fel y mae. Pan oeddwn i'n ymgyrchu, ac ers hynny, dywedodd trigolion nad oes digon o siopau, caffis na bwytai yn yr ardal. Rŵan, rwy'n croesawu'r cyhoeddiad o £654,000 o gyllid i ail-lunio strydoedd mawr yng Nghymru, ac yn enwedig ym Mangor, ond mae rhai o'r prosiectau ar gyfer dodrefn stryd newydd ac amffitheatr. Mae busnesau eu hunain yn poeni am sut y byddan nhw'n cael eu cynnwys yn y gwario. Ac os oes unrhyw un erioed wedi edrych, pan roddodd y Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru flaenorol grantiau cyllid i drefi, ni wnaeth unrhyw wahaniaeth o gwbl. Nawr, rwy'n nodi fy mod i wedi gofyn yn flaenorol, o ran busnesau lletygarwch, i TAW gael ei ostwng i 10 y cant, ac rwy'n falch o ddweud bod un o aelodau eich plaid yn y Senedd hefyd yn gwneud yr alwad honno i TAW ar fusnesau lletygarwch ostwng i 10 y cant. A ydych chi'n cefnogi ei galwadau, a galwadau'r Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, i wir helpu ein busnesau twristiaeth a lletygarwch?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It is a call that I have made in the past. What I would say is that we have to engage in what the UK Government could do and balance that against other things that the UK Government could do, because it's the outcome that's important, isn't it? It's not what the measure is, it's how it helps. What I have to do is to look at what I have in my toolkit, and one of the things that we do have are the powers over non-domestic rates. We said that we would use those powers, and we've moved very, very quickly to make sure that we do, with this permanent change, this real vote of confidence in leisure and hospitality—pubs, cafes, things that really bring vibrancy to the high street. So, the UK Government needs to look at its house and see what it can do. We'll put pressure on them to act in a whole host of different ways. We're acting using the powers that we have.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n alwad yr wyf i wedi ei gwneud yn y gorffennol. Yr hyn y byddwn i'n ei ddweud yw bod yn rhaid i ni ymgysylltu â'r hyn y gallai Llywodraeth y DU ei wneud a chydbwyso hynny yn erbyn pethau eraill y gallai Llywodraeth y DU eu gwneud, oherwydd y canlyniad sy'n bwysig, ynte? Nid yw'n fater o beth yw'r mesur, ond sut mae'n helpu. Yr hyn y mae'n rhaid i mi ei wneud yw edrych ar yr hyn sydd gen i yn fy mhecyn cymorth, ac un o'r pethau sydd gennym ni yw'r pwerau dros ardrethi annomestig. Fe wnaethom ni ddweud y byddem ni'n defnyddio'r pwerau hynny, ac rydym ni wedi symud yn gyflym iawn, iawn i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni, gyda'r newid parhaol hwn, yr arwydd gwirioneddol hwn o ffyrdd ym maes hamdden a lletygarwch—tafarndai, caffis, pethau sydd wir yn dod â bywiogrwydd i'r stryd fawr. Felly, mae angen i Lywodraeth y DU edrych ar ei chyfrifoldeb hi a gweld beth y gall ei wneud. Byddwn ni'n rhoi pwysau arnyn nhw i weithredu mewn nifer fawr o wahanol ffyrdd. Rydym ni'n gweithredu gan ddefnyddio'r pwerau sydd gennym ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Arweinwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from the Party Leaders

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar arweinwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Brif Weinidog. Yn gyntaf, ar ran Reform UK, Helen Jenner.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party leaders to question the First Minister. First, on behalf of Reform UK, Helen Jenner.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Prif Weinidog, despite you repeatedly saying that the election was not about seeking independence, on your first day back from recess you met with the leaders of Sinn Féin and the Scottish National Party to discuss plans to break up the United Kingdom. This is an act for which you have no mandate. Over two thirds of people surveyed recently said that they did not want to see Wales ripped out of the United Kingdom, and this Chamber has a pro-union majority. During the election campaign, you said that you wouldn't be looking to pursue independence, but, clearly, despite there being no appetite for it, you are. First Minister, you recently supported a law to make it an offence for politicians to knowingly mislead the public. So, my question is, to you: did you knowingly mislead voters when you said that this election wasn't about independence?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Brif Weinidog, er i chi ddweud dro ar ôl tro nad mater o fynd ar drywydd annibyniaeth oedd yr etholiad, ar eich diwrnod cyntaf yn ôl yn dilyn y toriad fe wnaethoch chi gyfarfod ag arweinwyr Sinn Féin a Phlaid Genedlaethol yr Alban i drafod cynlluniau i chwalu'r Deyrnas Unedig. Mae hon yn ddeddf nad oes gennych chi unrhyw fandad ar ei chyfer. Dywedodd dros ddwy ran o dair o bobl a holwyd yn ddiweddar nad oedden nhw eisiau gweld Cymru yn cael ei rhwygo allan o'r Deyrnas Unedig, ac mae gan y Siambr hon fwyafrif o blaid yr undeb. Yn ystod yr ymgyrch etholiadol, fe wnaethoch chi ddweud na fyddech chi'n mynd ar drywydd annibyniaeth, ond, yn amlwg, er gwaethaf y ffaith nad oes unrhyw awydd amdano, dyna'r ydych chi'n ei wneud. Brif Weinidog, fe wnaethoch chi gefnogi deddf yn ddiweddar i'w gwneud yn drosedd i wleidyddion gamarwain y cyhoedd yn ymwybodol. Felly, fy nghwestiwn yw, i chi: a wnaethoch chi gamarwain pleidleiswyr yn ymwybodol pan wnaethoch chi ddweud nad oedd yr etholiad hwn yn ymwneud ag annibyniaeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Do you know what I had a mandate to pursue? What I had a mandate to pursue was the best for Wales, always. So, when I get together with like-minded leaders throughout these islands, looking at how we can work together on childcare, on energy, on the way that we put pressure on the UK Government on funding, I think that that is absolutely standing up for Wales, as the people of Wales put their trust in us to do. And, yes, at the same time, we set our ambition for the nation. I believe that this isn't as good as things can get for Wales. Is Westminster working particularly well for Wales? Two letters and a number: HS2. That's the injustice that we're facing. Is the two-child cap what we really think is in the interest of the people of Wales? And a party like Reform always things that Wales is too small. Where's the ambition? Well, you know what? Matthew Rhys—let's congratulate Matthew Rhys on his historic Emmys win last night and what he said in accepting those two awards:

'We are a small but mighty nation. This is incredible.'

Be more like Matthew.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wyddoch chi beth roedd gen i fandad i fynd ar ei drywydd? Yr hyn yr oedd gen i fandad i fynd ar ei drywydd oedd y gorau i Gymru, bob amser. Felly, pan fyddaf i'n ymgynnull ag arweinwyr o'r un anian ar draws yr ynysoedd hyn, yn edrych ar sut y gallwn ni weithio gyda'n gilydd ar ofal plant, ar ynni, ar y ffordd yr ydym ni'n rhoi pwysau ar Lywodraeth y DU o ran cyllid, rwy'n credu bod hynny'n sicr yn sefyll yn gadarn dros Gymru, fel y gwnaeth pobl Cymru roi eu hymddiriedaeth ynom ni i'w wneud. A do, ar yr un pryd, fe wnaethom ni gyflwyno ein huchelgais ar gyfer y genedl. Rwy'n credu mai nad dyma mor dda ag y gall pethau ei fod i Gymru. A yw San Steffan yn gweithio'n arbennig o dda i Gymru? Dwy lythyren a rhif: HS2. Dyna'r anghyfiawnder yr ydym ni'n ei wynebu. A yw'r cap dau blentyn yr hyn yr ydym ni wir yn ei feddwl sydd o fudd pobl Cymru? Ac mae plaid fel Reform bob amser yn meddwl bod Cymru yn rhy fach. Ble mae'r uchelgais? Wel, wyddoch chi beth? Matthew Rhys—gadewch i ni longyfarch Matthew Rhys ar ei fuddugoliaeth hanesyddol yn yr Emmys neithiwr a'r hyn a ddywedodd wrth dderbyn y ddwy wobr hynny:

'Rydym ni'n genedl fach ond nerthol. Mae hyn yn anhygoel.'

Byddwch yn debycach i Matthew.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, nobody is talking down the people of Wales. Nobody is talking down Wales here. In fact, the people of Wales have returned a pro-union majority to this Senedd. First Minister, the bottom line is you have no mandate for focusing on independence. What you should be focusing on is fixing our broken NHS and our failing education system. You promised, First Minister, to eliminate two-year waits within months, yet you've moved the goalposts and now two-year NHS waits are up around 60 per cent since you entered office.

And, First Minister, speaking as a former teacher, last week's Programme for International Student Assessment results were quite frankly embarrassing. A third of 15-year-olds in Wales aren't capable of basic maths or reading and are around two years behind their counterparts in England. As a former teacher in Wales, I can tell you that what teachers need are not more plans and reviews, they need action. A generation of youngsters are being failed by Plaid and Labour, and frankly you owe them all an apology. First Minister, will you stop focusing on plotting with Sinn Féin and focus on fixing our schools and our NHS?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, does neb yn bychanu pobl Cymru. Does neb yn bychanu Cymru yma. A dweud y gwir, mae pobl Cymru wedi dychwelyd mwyafrif o blaid yr undeb i'r Senedd hon. Brif Weinidog, y gwir amdani yw nad oes gennych chi unrhyw fandad i ganolbwyntio ar annibyniaeth. Yr hyn y dylech chi fod yn canolbwyntio arno yw trwsio ein GIG sydd wedi torri a'n system addysg sy'n methu. Fe wnaethoch chi addo, Brif Weinidog, cael gwared ar arosiadau o ddwy flynedd o fewn misoedd, ond rydych chi wedi newid y rheolau a bellach mae arosiadau o ddwy flynedd yn y GIG i fyny tua 60 y cant ers i chi ddod i rym.

A, Brif Weinidog, yn siarad fel cyn-athrawes, roedd canlyniadau'r Rhaglen ar gyfer Asesu Myfyrwyr Rhyngwladol yr wythnos diwethaf yn ddigon i godi cywilydd a dweud y gwir. Nid yw traean o bobl ifanc 15 oed yng Nghymru yn gallu ymgymryd â mathemateg neu ddarllen sylfaenol ac maen nhw tua dwy flynedd y tu ôl i'w cymheiriaid yn Lloegr. Fel cyn-athrawes yng Nghymru, gallaf ddweud wrthych chi nad mwy o gynlluniau ac adolygiadau sydd ei angen ar athrawon, maen nhw angen gweithredu. Mae cenhedlaeth o bobl ifanc yn cael eu methu gan Blaid Cymru a Llafur, ac i fod yn onest fe ddylech chi ymddiheuro iddyn nhw i gyd. Brif Weinidog, a wnewch chi roi'r gorau i ganolbwyntio ar gynllwynio gyda Sinn Féin a chanolbwyntio ar drwsio ein hysgolion a'n GIG?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I tell you what, Llywydd, if the Member thinks you can only do one thing at a time in Government, she should give up her aspirations right now, because it is all about dealing with a host of issues that are in the interests of building our nation. It is about doing the work that we've done over the summer to pump money into health and to change our attitude on how we bring those waiting times down. It is about the numeracy and literacy strategy that is being published today by my Minister for education. And when it comes to this pursuit of more powers, which Reform absolutely rejects, let's remind the Member that it's because of powers taken on around a decade ago over non-domestic rates that we are now able to make a positive decision to help businesses in Wales through a cut of a third in the rates for businesses in hospitality and leisure. We have our eyes on the future of Wales, and I suggest that the Member opposite does the same.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe ddywedaf i wrthych chi beth, Lywydd, os yw'r Aelod yn meddwl y gallwch chi wneud un peth ar y pryd yn unig mewn Llywodraeth, dylai gefnu ar ei huchelgeisiau nawr, oherwydd mae'r cwbl yn fater o ymdrin â llu o faterion sydd o fudd adeiladu ein cenedl. Mae'n fater o wneud y gwaith yr ydym ni wedi ei wneud dros yr haf i bwmpio arian i mewn i faes iechyd a newid ein hagwedd ar sut rydym ni'n lleihau'r amseroedd aros hynny. Mae'n ymwneud â'r strategaeth rhifedd a llythrennedd sy'n cael ei chyhoeddi heddiw gan fy Ngweinidog addysg. Ac o ran mynd ar drywydd mwy o bwerau, y mae Reform yn ei wrthod yn llwyr, gadewch i ni atgoffa'r Aelod mai oherwydd pwerau a gymerwyd tua degawd yn ôl dros ardrethi annomestig yr ydym ni bellach yn gallu gwneud penderfyniad cadarnhaol i helpu busnesau yng Nghymru trwy doriad o draean i'r ardrethi ar gyfer busnes ym maes lletygarwch a hamdden. Mae ein llygaid ar ddyfodol Cymru, ac rwy'n awgrymu bod yr Aelod gyferbyn yn gwneud yr un fath.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, it wasn't really a great summer for Plaid Cymru, was it? You couldn't pass your budget, it failed to put Welsh people first, and then you failed to act in time when we faced those wildfires. Like everything else in Wales, you lost control of it.

Then there was the Government alert we all received. Whose idea was it to send an emergency alert in two separate messages, rather than one bilingual message to avoid confusion? You attended a COBRA meeting with the Prime Minister about all this. The alert was meant to avoid disaster, but in and of itself it created disaster. It sent some people into panic and sent some people to ring 999. Why couldn't it have gone out in one bilingual message? Either you were to blame, or, once again, Westminster was ignoring you and not taking you seriously. Which one is it?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, nid oedd yn haf gwych i Blaid Cymru, onid oedd? Allech chi ddim pasio eich cyllideb, roedd yn methu â rhoi pobl Cymru yn gyntaf, ac yna fe wnaethoch chi fethu â gweithredu mewn pryd pan oeddem ni'n wynebu'r tanau gwyllt hynny. Fel popeth arall yng Nghymru, fe wnaethoch chi golli rheolaeth drostyn nhw.

Yna, cafwyd y rhybudd Llywodraeth a dderbyniwyd gennym ni i gyd. Syniad pwy oedd anfon rhybudd brys mewn dwy neges ar wahân, yn hytrach nag un neges ddwyieithog er mwyn osgoi dryswch? Roeddech chi'n bresennol mewn cyfarfod COBRA gyda'r Prif Weinidog a oedd yn ymwneud â hyn yn llwyr. Roedd y rhybudd i fod i osgoi trychineb, ond ynddo'i hun fe wnaeth greu trychineb. Anfonodd rai pobl i banig ac anfonodd rai pobl i ffonio 999. Pam na allai fod wedi mynd allan mewn un neges ddwyieithog? Naill ai chi oedd ar fai, neu, unwaith eto, roedd San Steffan yn eich anwybyddu chi a ddim yn eich cymryd chi o ddifrif. Pa un ydyw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'll tell you what, all the Reform stereotypes are coming out today. There is a UK Government responsibility for the emergency alert. And do you know what, did they get it right? Clearly they didn't get it right. There was a technical issue about the way that it was sent out and that caused anxiety for people. I've spoken with COBRA myself to say, 'You need to sort this out for the future', because this is for the UK Government. But doesn't it say everything about Reform and its attitude towards Wales that your position on this is to blame the Welsh language, which wasn't at fault?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe ddywedaf i wrthych chi beth, mae holl stereoteipiau Reform yn cael eu clywed heddiw. Mae cyfrifoldeb gan Lywodraeth y DU am y rhybudd brys. A wyddoch chi beth, a wnaethon nhw ei wneud yn iawn? Yn amlwg wnaethon nhw ddim ei wneud yn iawn. Roedd problem dechnegol ynglŷn â'r ffordd y cafodd ei anfon allan ac achosodd hynny bryder i bobl. Rwyf i wedi siarad â COBRA fy hun i ddweud, 'Mae angen i chi ddatrys hyn ar gyfer y dyfodol', oherwydd mater i Lywodraeth y DU yw hwn. Ond onid yw'n dweud popeth am Reform a'i hagwedd tuag at Gymru mai eich safbwynt ar hyn yw beio'r iaith Gymraeg, nad oedd ar fai?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arweinydd Llafur Cymru, Ken Skates.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Leader of Welsh Labour, Ken Skates.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. First Minister, obviously building a progressive alliance means working together in common cause, but signing a memorandum of disunity with those who wish to break up and ruin the United Kingdom will only please people like Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. It will not please the vast majority of people in Wales, including the many health visitors who are here today. Those health visitors feel snubbed by your Government. Those health visitors are questioning the integrity of your Government after being promised an end to their dispute over pay within days of May's election. First Minister, will you please use powers available to you in law to bring an end to this dispute, an end that was promised before the election?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Brif Weinidog, yn amlwg mae datblygu cynghrair flaengar yn golygu cydweithio mewn achos cyffredin, ond y cwbl y bydd llofnodi memorandwm o ymraniad gyda'r rhai sy'n dymuno chwalu a difetha'r Deyrnas Unedig yn ei wneud fydd plesio pobl fel Donald Trump a Vladimir Putin. Ni fydd yn plesio'r mwyafrif llethol o bobl yng Nghymru, gan gynnwys yr ymwelwyr iechyd niferus sydd yma heddiw. Mae'r ymwelwyr iechyd hynny yn teimlo eu bod yn wedi cael eu hanwybyddu gan eich Llywodraeth chi. Mae'r ymwelwyr iechyd hynny yn cwestiynu uniondeb eich Llywodraeth chi ar ôl cael addewid o derfyn ar eu dadl dros gyflog o fewn dyddiau o etholiad mis Mai. Brif Weinidog, a wnewch chi, os gwelwch yn dda, ddefnyddio pwerau sydd ar gael i chi yn y gyfraith i roi terfyn ar yr anghydfod hwn, terfyn a addawyd cyn yr etholiad?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member is right to draw attention to a dispute that causes real frustration. It's certainly something that I feel. It's a dispute that we inherited, of course, from the previous administration. What is clear, as the former Labour First Minister said, is that this is something that can be resolved only by the health service itself. I know the efforts that my health Minister has put into trying to influence the health service to get to that point where we have a resolution. We need this to be resolved for the people served by that health board and for the nurses who want to care for their patients. And I again call today for that resolution to happen as swiftly as possible, because it's not acceptable for this to be pursued this long.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn iawn i dynnu sylw at anghydfod sy'n achosi rhwystredigaeth gwirioneddol. Mae'n sicr yn rhywbeth yr wyf i'n ei deimlo. Mae'n anghydfod a etifeddwyd gennym ni, wrth gwrs, gan y weinyddiaeth flaenorol. Yr hyn sy'n eglur, fel y dywedodd y cyn-Brif Weinidog Llafur, yw bod hyn yn rhywbeth y gall y gwasanaeth iechyd ei hun yn unig ei ddatrys. Rwy'n ymwybodol o'r ymdrechion y mae fy Ngweinidog iechyd wedi eu gwneud i geisio dylanwadu ar y gwasanaeth iechyd i gyrraedd y pwynt hwnnw lle mae gennym ni ateb. Rydym ni angen i hyn gael ei ddatrys ar gyfer y bobl sy'n cael eu gwasanaethu gan y bwrdd iechyd hwnnw ac i'r nyrsys sydd eisiau gofalu am eu cleifion. Ac rwy'n galw eto heddiw am i'r ateb hwnnw ddigwydd cyn gynted â phosibl, oherwydd nid yw'n dderbyniol i hyn barhau am gyhyd â hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, I agree it is not acceptable and health visitors should have had justice within the first 100 days of your Government being elected. Yes, you've inherited this challenge, but during the election many of your Members were telling those health visitors that it would be resolved with direct intervention within days—within days. They now question the integrity of your Government and they say that they voted for your party on the basis of what they now believe was a false promise.

Now, they're not the only people to have been snubbed. Over the summer, a number of organisations, communities and people have been snubbed—you might call it 'summer snubbing'. But it's affected the Prime Minister, it's affected Michael Sheen, it's affected countless communities that were left devastated by the wildfires. All snubbed. But please can I urge you not to snub those who wish to see a £2 bus fare cap introduced in Wales? Andy Burnham has provided you with the consequentials to do so. It was a pledge in Welsh Labour's manifesto, and I do believe that if you implement that policy, it would demonstrate to the people of Wales that common ground that we can occupy to make people's lives better.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, rwy'n cytuno nad yw'n dderbyniol a dylai ymwelwyr iechyd fod wedi cael cyfiawnder o fewn y 100 diwrnod cyntaf o ethol eich Llywodraeth. Ydych, rydych chi wedi etifeddu'r her hon, ond yn ystod yr etholiad roedd llawer o'ch Aelodau yn dweud wrth yr ymwelwyr iechyd hynny y byddai'n cael ei ddatrys gydag ymyrraeth uniongyrchol o fewn diwrnodau—o fewn diwrnodau. Maen nhw bellach yn cwestiynu uniondeb eich Llywodraeth ac maen nhw'n dweud eu bod nhw wedi pleidleisio dros eich plaid ar sail yr hyn maen nhw bellach yn ei gredu oedd addewid ffug.

Nawr, nid nhw yw'r unig bobl sydd wedi cael eu hanwybyddu. Dros yr haf, mae nifer o sefydliadau, cymunedau a phobl wedi cael eu hanwybyddu—fe allech ei alw'n 'haf o anwybyddu'. Ond mae wedi effeithio ar y Prif Weinidog, mae wedi effeithio ar Michael Sheen, mae wedi effeithio ar gymunedau di-ri a gafodd eu dinistrio gan y tanau gwyllt. Y cwbl wedi'u hanwybyddu. Ond a gaf i eich annog chi, os gwelwch yn dda, i beidio ag anwybyddu'r rhai sy'n dymuno gweld cap o £2 ar bris tocyn bws yn cael ei gyflwyno yng Nghymru? Mae Andy Burnham wedi rhoi'r arian canlyniadol i chi wneud hynny. Roedd yn addewid ym maniffesto Llafur Cymru, ac rwy'n credu os gwnewch chi roi'r polisi hwnnw ar waith y byddai'n dangos i bobl Cymru y tir cyffredin hwnnw y gallwn ni ei feddiannu i wneud bywydau pobl yn well.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
There is quite a lot to unpick in that question. There is a reference there to the need to work in a consensual way. I start this term in the way that I started the first term post election in making it very, very clear that this is a Government that wants to reach out and work in a way that serves the people of Wales in a constructive way. So, I make that point.

We're a Government that hit the ground running with a 100-day plan that we were able to deliver on, setting the foundations for what will be the programme for government to be presented in the very near future. This is a Government that takes seriously the faith put in us by the people of Wales, dealing with many different challenges, because the Member knows governing isn't always easy. It is about prioritising, but the more that we can work together, have clarity in what we are trying to achieve for the people of Wales, well, the better our chances of giving them the outcomes that they deserve. It has been a very, very busy summer of working with many, many partners in making sure that we move forward with real purpose.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae cryn dipyn i'w ddehongli yn y cwestiwn hwnnw. Mae cyfeiriad yn y fan yna at yr angen i weithio mewn ffordd gydsyniol. Rwy'n dechrau'r tymor hwn yn y ffordd y dechreuais y tymor cyntaf ar ôl yr etholiad gan ei gwneud hi'n eglur iawn, iawn bod hon yn Llywodraeth sydd eisiau estyn allan a gweithio mewn ffordd sy'n gwasanaethu pobl Cymru mewn ffordd adeiladol. Felly, rwy'n gwneud y pwynt hwnnw.

Rydym ni'n Llywodraeth sydd wedi dechrau cyflawni o'r cychwyn gyda chynllun 100 diwrnod yr oeddem ni'n gallu ei gyflawni, gan osod y sylfeini ar gyfer yr hyn fydd y rhaglen lywodraethu i'w chyflwyno yn y dyfodol agos iawn. Mae hon yn Llywodraeth sy'n cymryd o ddifrif y ffydd a roddwyd ynom ni gan bobl Cymru, gan ymdrin â llawer o wahanol heriau, oherwydd mae'r Aelod yn gwybod nad yw llywodraethu bob amser yn hawdd. Mae'n fater o flaenoriaethu, ond po fwyaf y gallwn ni weithio gyda'n gilydd, bod ag eglurder yn yr hyn yr ydym ni'n ceisio ei gyflawni i bobl Cymru, wel, y gorau yw ein siawns o roi'r canlyniadau y maen nhw'n eu haeddu iddyn nhw. Mae wedi bod yn haf prysur dros ben o weithio gyda llawer iawn o bartneriaid i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n symud ymlaen gyda phwrpas gwirioneddol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Darren Millar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Leader of the Welsh Conservatives, Darren Millar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, yesterday, while you were plotting the break-up of the United Kingdom with your friends in Sinn Féin and the Scottish National Party, there were people waiting for ambulances for too long, people in our emergency departments for too long on trolleys and not getting the treatment that they need in time, because of a lack of hospital beds around the country. Just last week, Healthcare Inspectorate Wales published a damning report into the emergency department at the Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board's Glan Clwyd Hospital. It cited patients being left in corridors without food or drink or pain relief, out-of-date medicines and equipment not working, and the paediatric area being left unattended while child patients were present. So, instead of hatching plans to break apart the UK, isn't it time that you focused on your day job and showed some urgency to fix our NHS instead?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, ddoe, tra'r oeddech chi'n cynllwynio chwalfa'r Deyrnas Unedig gyda'ch cyfeillion yn Sinn Féin a Phlaid Genedlaethol yr Alban, roedd pobl yn aros am ambiwlansys am ormod o amser, roedd pobl yn ein hadrannau achosion brys yn treulio gormod o amser ar drolïau a ddim yn cael y driniaeth yr oedd ei hangen arnyn nhw mewn pryd, oherwydd diffyg gwelyau ysbyty ledled y wlad. Dim ond yr wythnos diwethaf, cyhoeddodd Arolygiaeth Gofal Iechyd Cymru adroddiad damniol ar yr adran achosion brys yn Ysbyty Glan Clwyd ym Mwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Betsi Cadwaladr. Cyfeiriodd at gleifion yn cael eu gadael mewn coridorau heb fwyd na diod na lladdwyr poen, meddyginiaethau heibio eu dyddiad terfyn ac offer ddim yn gweithio, a'r man pediatrig yn cael ei adael heb staff tra'r oedd cleifion yn bresennol. Felly, yn hytrach na gwneud cynlluniau i chwalu'r DU, onid yw'n bryd i chi ganolbwyntio ar eich prif swydd a dangos rhywfaint o frys i drwsio ein GIG yn hytrach?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I reflect today on this cabal of stagnation that Reform, the Conservatives and Labour have when it comes to moving Wales forward. Moving Wales forward and seeking practical answers to our problems means learning from others when it comes to the future of the health service, the future of the education service in Wales, and that's what this Government does. We will find partners where we have common ground always.

On the issues around Glan Clwyd, I absolutely share the concern raised by the leader of the Conservatives. The Cabinet Minister for Health and Care met with the chair and chief executive of the health board recently in Ysbyty Glan Clwyd. He set out his expectations of owning issues and making the improvements required by the people they serve. And yet again, we have further examples of those deep challenges facing Betsi Cadwaladr that affect patients, and that is what should affect every single one of us. That is why we have, since the summer, or at the end of the summer recess, published our plans on how we change the NHS's attitudes towards getting people through the system, not being wasteful in the way that we use our resources, because we are determined to act on our promise in this election to make health the No. 1 priority, because I think that’s the No. 1 priority of the people of Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n myfyrio heddiw ar y glymblaid hon o farweidd-dra sydd gan Reform, y Ceidwadwyr a Llafur pan ddaw i symud Cymru ymlaen. Mae symud Cymru ymlaen a chwilio am atebion ymarferol i'n problemau yn golygu dysgu oddi wrth eraill o ran dyfodol y gwasanaeth iechyd, dyfodol y gwasanaeth addysg yng Nghymru, a dyna'r hyn y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei wneud. Byddwn yn dod o hyd i bartneriaid lle mae gennym ni dir cyffredin bob amser.

Ar y materion yn ymwneud â Glan Clwyd, rwy'n rhannu'r pryder a godwyd gan arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr. Fe wnaeth y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal gyfarfod â chadeirydd a phrif weithredwr y bwrdd iechyd yn ddiweddar yn Ysbyty Glan Clwyd. Amlinellodd ei ddisgwyliadau o gymryd cyfrifoldeb am broblemau a gwneud y gwelliannau sydd eu hangen ar y bobl y maen nhw'n eu gwasanaethu. Ac unwaith eto, mae gennym ni enghreifftiau pellach o'r heriau dwfn hynny sy'n wynebu Betsi Cadwaladr sy'n effeithio ar gleifion, a dyna'r hyn a ddylai effeithio ar bob un ohonom ni. Dyna pam rydym ni, ers yr haf, neu ar ddiwedd toriad yr haf, wedi cyhoeddi ein cynlluniau ar sut yr ydym ni'n newid agweddau'r GIG tuag at gael pobl drwy'r system, peidio â bod yn wastraffus yn y ffordd yr ydym ni'n defnyddio ein hadnoddau, oherwydd rydym ni'n benderfynol o weithredu ar ein haddewid yn yr etholiad hwn i wneud iechyd yn brif flaenoriaeth, oherwydd rwy'n credu mai dyna brif flaenoriaeth pobl Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You say that it's your No. 1 priority, and you say that you want to co-operate with others in order to improve the NHS. I looked very carefully at the declaration that you signed yesterday alongside those other nationalist leaders, and let me tell you, there was no mention of the health service. There was no mention of the national health service in any way, shape or form whatsoever. There was no mention, either, of our education system, and as has already been pointed out, it's hardly surprising, given that we've got the worst education system in the whole of the United Kingdom, and that Scotland's education system is also tumbling down the PISA scores, as is Northern Ireland’s. Why don't you co-operate on the things for which you're absolutely already responsible instead of having these pie-in-the-sky discussions, grandstanding over the constitution of the United Kingdom rather than pulling your finger out and doing the job that the people of Wales elected you to do?

Let me tell you this, First Minister: the honeymoon is well and truly over. While you were sunning yourself on a beach, presumably burying your head in the sand on it, on the 100-day anniversary of your Government, people in Wales were dying in our hospitals and young people were not getting the education they need. When will they see the change rather than the continuity Labour that we've seen so far?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rydych chi'n dweud mai dyna eich prif flaenoriaeth, ac rydych chi'n dweud eich bod chi eisiau cydweithredu ag eraill er mwyn gwella'r GIG. Edrychais yn ofalus iawn ar y datganiad a lofnodwyd gennych chi ddoe ochr yn ochr â'r arweinwyr cenedlaetholgar eraill hynny, a gadewch i mi ddweud wrthych chi, nid oedd unrhyw sôn am y gwasanaeth iechyd. Nid oedd unrhyw sôn am y gwasanaeth iechyd gwladol mewn unrhyw ffordd, siâp neu ffurf o gwbl. Nid oedd unrhyw sôn chwaith am ein system addysg, ac fel y nodwyd eisoes, nid yw'n syndod, o ystyried bod gennym ni'r system addysg waethaf yn y Deyrnas Unedig gyfan, a bod system addysg yr Alban hefyd yn cwympo i lawr y sgoriau PISA, fel y mae rhai Gogledd Iwerddon. Pam na wnewch chi gydweithredu ar y pethau yr ydych chi eisoes yn bendant yn gyfrifol amdanyn nhw yn hytrach na chael y trafodaethau breuddwyd gwrach hyn, yn dangos eich hun ynghylch cyfansoddiad y Deyrnas Unedig yn hytrach na thynnu eich bys allan a gwneud y gwaith y gwnaeth pobl Cymru eich ethol i'w wneud?

Gadewch i mi ddweud hyn wrthych chi, Brif Weinidog: mae'r mis mêl drosodd, heb os nac oni bai. Tra roeddech chi'n torheulo ar draeth, yn ôl pob tebyg yn claddu eich pen yn y tywod arno, ar ganfed diwrnod eich Llywodraeth, roedd pobl yng Nghymru yn marw yn ein hysbytai ac nid oedd pobl ifanc yn cael yr addysg sydd ei hangen arnyn nhw. Pryd fyddan nhw'n gweld y newid yn hytrach na'r parhad o Lafur yr ydym ni wedi ei weld hyd yn hyn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
When will we see a change in the Conservatives from the whingeing that we always hear from their benches on these matters, rather than working constructively? We have an offer here to work constructively, to seek ideas, and that includes from you, as the leader of the Conservatives, on the future of our public services here in Wales.

This Government set out a programme that was given a mandate, not with a majority, but with a clear mandate to deliver for the people of Wales. And that means on health, which is why my health Minister worked so quickly to pump that money in, which will bring down those waiting times as the people of Wales deserve. It’s why we moved quickly to put that national numeracy and literacy scheme in place, which will drive up education standards, because I agree with you: it is scandalous, the way that we have allowed standards to drop here in Wales, with our proud record of educational achievement. We do this at the same time as setting an ambition for having more control over our own future here as a nation in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Pryd fyddwn ni'n gweld newid yn y Ceidwadwyr o'r grwgnach yr ydym ni bob amser yn ei glywed o'u meinciau ar y materion hyn, yn hytrach na gweithio'n adeiladol? Mae gennym ni gynnig yma i weithio'n adeiladol, i chwilio am syniadau, ac mae hynny'n cynnwys gennych chi, fel arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr, ar ddyfodol ein gwasanaethau cyhoeddus yma yng Nghymru.

Cyflwynodd y Llywodraeth hon raglen a gafodd fandad, nid gyda mwyafrif, ond gyda mandad eglur i gyflawni ar gyfer pobl Cymru. Ac mae hynny'n golygu ar iechyd, a dyna pam y gweithiodd fy Ngweinidog iechyd mor gyflym i bwmpio'r arian hwnnw i mewn, a fydd yn lleihau'r amseroedd aros hynny fel y mae pobl Cymru yn ei haeddu. Dyna pam y gwnaethom ni symud yn gyflym i roi'r cynllun rhifedd a llythrennedd cenedlaethol hwnnw ar waith, a fydd yn codi safonau addysg, oherwydd rwy'n cytuno â chi: mae'n gywilyddus, y ffordd yr ydym ni wedi caniatáu i safonau ostwng yma yng Nghymru, gyda'n hanes balch o gyflawniad addysgol. Rydym ni'n gwneud hyn ar yr un pryd â phennu uchelgais i gael mwy o reolaeth dros ein dyfodol ein hunain yma fel cenedl yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: How to follow that? A declaration of interest: my wife works for Bangor University, Llywydd.
