XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa asesiad mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi'i wneud o fforddiadwyedd ffioedd dysgu yng Nghymru? OQ64476
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What assessment has the First Minister made of the affordability of tuition fees in Wales? OQ64476

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tuition fees are set by higher education institutions, and eligible students receive loans to meet the full cost of their tuition. The Welsh Government will consider fees alongside the long-term sustainability of higher education itself in our independent review of higher education, and the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education will provide further details later this afternoon.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae ffioedd dysgu yn cael eu pennu gan sefydliadau addysg uwch, ac mae myfyrwyr cymwys yn derbyn benthyciadau i dalu cost lawn eu haddysg. Bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn ystyried ffioedd ochr yn ochr â chynaliadwyedd hirdymor addysg uwch ei hun yn ein hadolygiad annibynnol o addysg uwch, a bydd y Dirprwy Weinidog Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol yn darparu rhagor o fanylion yn ddiweddarach y prynhawn yma.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, First Minister. The figures are clear and unambiguous. England has already set its tuition fee cap at just over £10,000. At the same time, Welsh universities are under severe financial pressure. The sector recorded an underlying deficit of more than £79 million according to Medr, while Bangor University alone reported a deficit of nearly £19 million, alongside redundancies. And the number of Welsh students studying at Welsh universities has fallen by about 9 per cent since 2021, the largest percentage fall of any UK nation.

Universities need certainty if they’re to plan staffing, courses and investment responsibly. They are on their beam ends, quite frankly. So, will the First Minister give the sector some certainty today? Will the Welsh tuition fee cap remain in line with England for the rest of the Senedd term, yes or no, please?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Mae'r ffigurau yn eglur ac yn ddigamsyniol. Mae Lloegr eisoes wedi pennu ei chap ffioedd dysgu ar ychydig dros £10,000. Ar yr un pryd, mae prifysgolion Cymru o dan bwysau ariannol difrifol. Cofnododd y sector ddiffyg sylfaenol o fwy na £79 miliwn yn ôl Medr, ac adroddodd Prifysgol Bangor ar ei phen ei hun ddiffyg o bron i £19 miliwn, ochr yn ochr â diswyddiadau. Ac mae nifer y myfyrwyr o Gymru sy'n astudio mewn prifysgolion yng Nghymru wedi gostwng tua 9 y cant ers 2021, y gostyngiad canrannol mwyaf o unrhyw genedl yn y DU.

Mae angen sicrwydd ar brifysgolion os ydyn nhw'n mynd i gynllunio staffio, cyrsiau a buddsoddiad yn gyfrifol. Maen nhw wedi cyrraedd pen eu tennyn, i fod yn gwbl onest. Felly, a wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi rhywfaint o sicrwydd i'r sector heddiw? A fydd y cap ffioedd dysgu yng Nghymru yn parhau i fod yn unol â Lloegr am weddill tymor y Senedd, bydd neu na fydd, os gwelwch yn dda?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I genuinely appreciate the way that the question has been framed, because I align myself with that description of the fragility of the higher education sector in Wales. It's something that should worry us all for the future of education and learning itself, for the impact that that has on the Welsh economy and research, also on the jobs that are supported by our higher education sector. But of course, we also want to support the students who are the future of those jobs, and those jobs in the sector itself. It is a balance, and what we have said is that we need to find that balance, and I'll remind you what Plaid Cymru, the party I lead, has said throughout: this is something that we need consensus on. This is something that's far too important to be allowed to be used as some sort of political ding-dong, because I hope I'm looking at everybody in this Chamber and seeing fellow Members who want to see our students supported appropriately and our higher education institutions survive and prosper.

On the fees cap, no decision has been announced yet on Welsh tuition fee caps or fee loan support for 2027-28. We're considering how best to support students while maintaining the higher education sector in Wales. That is a balance that we all need to think carefully about.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwyf i wir yn gwerthfawrogi'r ffordd y mae'r cwestiwn wedi cael ei fframio, oherwydd rwy'n cysylltu fy hun â'r disgrifiad hwnnw o fregusrwydd y sector addysg uwch yng Nghymru. Mae'n rhywbeth a ddylai ein poeni ni i gyd am ddyfodol addysg a dysgu ei hun, am yr effaith y mae hynny'n ei chael ar economi ac ymchwil Cymru, a hefyd ar y swyddi sy'n cael eu cefnogi gan ein sector addysg uwch. Ond wrth gwrs, rydym ni hefyd eisiau cynorthwyo'r myfyrwyr, sef dyfodol y swyddi hynny, a'r swyddi hynny yn y sector ei hun. Mae'n gydbwysedd, a'r hyn yr ydym ni wedi ei ddweud yw bod angen i ni ddod o hyd i'r cydbwysedd hwnnw, ac fe wnaf i eich atgoffa o'r hyn y mae Plaid Cymru, y blaid rwy'n ei harwain, wedi ei ddweud o'r cychwyn: mae hyn yn rhywbeth yr ydym ni angen consensws yn ei gylch. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n llawer rhy bwysig i ganiatáu iddo gael ei ddefnyddio fel rhyw fath o nôl ac ymlaen gwleidyddol, oherwydd rwy'n gobeithio fy mod i'n edrych ar bawb yn y Siambr hon ac yn gweld cyd-Aelodau sydd eisiau gweld ein myfyrwyr yn cael eu cynorthwyo'n briodol a'n sefydliadau addysg uwch yn goroesi ac yn ffynnu.

O ran y cap ffioedd, ni chyhoeddwyd unrhyw benderfyniad eto ar gapiau ffioedd dysgu Cymru na chymorth benthyciadau ffioedd ar gyfer 2027-28. Rydym ni'n ystyried y ffordd orau o gynorthwyo myfyrwyr gan gynnal y sector addysg uwch yng Nghymru. Mae hwnnw'n gydbwysedd y mae angen i ni i gyd feddwl amdano'n ofalus.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, over the summer, I met with the Open University, who do brilliant work in ensuring education is accessible to everyone, if that's the path that they wish to pursue. Their fees remain below the maximum borrowing amount, simply because if fee rates were too high, the number of students would decline. With almost a quarter of people in Wales living in relative income poverty, the Open University is a fantastic institution through which education, career development and personal growth are viable opportunities. So, I would like to ask how you will ensure that people in Wales have access to higher education without being held back by ever-increasing loans.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, dros yr haf, fe wnes i gyfarfod â'r Brifysgol Agored, sy'n gwneud gwaith gwych i sicrhau bod addysg yn hygyrch i bawb, os mai dyna'r llwybr y maen nhw'n dymuno ei ddilyn. Mae eu ffioedd yn dal i fod yn is na'r uchafswm benthyg, oherwydd, yn syml, pe bai cyfraddau ffioedd yn rhy uchel, byddai nifer y myfyrwyr yn gostwng. Gyda bron i chwarter y bobl yng Nghymru yn byw mewn tlodi incwm cymharol, mae'r Brifysgol Agored yn sefydliad gwych lle mae addysg, datblygiad gyrfaol a thwf personol yn gyfleoedd ymarferol. Felly, hoffwn ofyn sut wnewch chi sicrhau bod gan bobl yng Nghymru fynediad at addysg uwch heb gael eu dal yn ôl gan fenthyciadau sy'n cynyddu'n barhaus.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It is an issue that potential students are having to reckon with more and more. I was stopped by a young gentleman yesterday who was excited at seeing a politician and wanted a picture. He was studying for a politics, philosophy and economics degree at the Open University and it was working really well for him. He was working still whilst he was doing his degree. We know that the Open University and other providers of part-time courses play an important role in widening access to higher education and supporting flexible learning opportunities. This review of higher education will look at all aspects of higher education, including access to part-time provision.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n fater y mae'n rhaid i ddarpar fyfyrwyr ei ystyried fwy a mwy. Cefais fy stopio gan ŵr ifanc ddoe a oedd wedi cynhyrfu o weld gwleidydd ac eisiau llun. Roedd yn astudio ar gyfer gradd gwleidyddiaeth, athroniaeth ac economeg yn y Brifysgol Agored ac roedd yn gweithio'n dda iawn iddo. Roedd yn gweithio o hyd tra roedd yn gwneud ei radd. Rydym ni'n gwybod bod y Brifysgol Agored a darparwyr eraill o gyrsiau rhan-amser yn chwarae rhan bwysig o ran ehangu mynediad at addysg uwch a chefnogi cyfleoedd dysgu hyblyg. Bydd yr adolygiad hwn o addysg uwch yn ystyried pob agwedd ar addysg uwch, gan gynnwys mynediad at ddarpariaeth ran-amser.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, the Treasury Committee in the House of Commons came forward with a report over the summer that highlighted 28 recommendations to the UK Government, two of which really stood out as very simplistic, but having a big effect. One was around supplying good-quality information to students at the time of accepting their student loan, which you would have thought would be happening already, but isn't happening. And secondly, instead of using the retail prices index, use the consumer prices index, which again would have a significant effect of lowering the interest rates. Would your Government be supportive of adopting these recommendations to make a quick win in a complex field? Obviously, your review is looking at the higher education sector more generally, but students need help today, not in six, 12 or 18 months.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, cyflwynodd Pwyllgor y Trysorlys yn Nhŷ'r Cyffredin adroddiad dros yr haf a dynnodd sylw at 28 o argymhellion i Lywodraeth y DU, yr oedd dau ohonyn nhw wir yn sefyll allan fel pethau syml iawn, ond fyddai'n cael effaith fawr. Roedd un yn ymwneud â darparu gwybodaeth o ansawdd dda i fyfyrwyr ar adeg derbyn ei benthyciad i fyfyrwyr, y byddech chi wedi ei ddisgwyl fyddai'n digwydd eisoes, ond nad yw'n digwydd. Ac yn ail, yn hytrach na defnyddio'r mynegai prisiau manwerthu, defnyddio'r mynegai prisiau defnyddwyr, a fyddai eto'n cael effaith sylweddol o ostwng y cyfraddau llog. A fyddai eich Llywodraeth yn cefnogi mabwysiadu'r argymhellion hyn i gael buddugoliaeth gyflym mewn maes cymhleth? Yn amlwg, mae eich adolygiad yn edrych ar y sector addysg uwch yn fwy cyffredinol, ond mae myfyrwyr angen cymorth heddiw, nid ymhen chwe, 12 neu 18 mis.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's not a matter that I have discussed specifically with the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education, but it's certainly something that I'm willing to look at and see where our position would be. At the end of the day, I'm really concerned about the impact of the debts that students go into. I have just one student left in our family now, but two ex-students who are living with debt. Many of us either are living with debts ourselves or are parents of those who are, and it's something that really concerns us. In brief, I want every potential avenue to be looked at that could take the pressure off students now or potential students in future. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nid yw'n fater yr wyf i wedi ei drafod yn benodol gyda'r Dirprwy Weinidog Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol, ond mae'n sicr yn rhywbeth yr wyf i'n barod i edrych arno a gweld ble fyddai ein safbwynt. Yn y pen draw, rwy'n bryderus iawn am effaith y dyledion y mae myfyrwyr yn eu hysgwyddo. Dim ond un myfyriwr sydd gen i ar ôl yn ein teulu ni bellach, ond dau gyn-fyfyriwr sy'n byw gyda dyled. Mae llawer ohonom ni naill ai'n byw gyda dyledion ein hunain neu'n rhieni i'r rhai sydd yn, ac mae'n rhywbeth sydd wir yn peri gofid i ni. Yn gryno, hoffwn i bob llwybr posibl gael ei ystyried a allai dynnu'r pwysau oddi ar fyfyrwyr nawr neu ddarpar fyfyrwyr yn y dyfodol. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Amseroedd Aros am Lawdriniaeth Cataractau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Waiting Times for Cataract Surgery

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog ddatganiad ar amseroedd aros am lawdriniaeth cataractau yn Sir Gaerfyrddin? OQ64456
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. Will the First Minister make a statement on waiting times for cataract surgery in Sir Gaerfyrddin? OQ64456

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We recognise that people waiting for cataract surgery want treatment as quickly as possible, obviously. That is why we've committed an additional £145 million this year to reduce waiting times, improve access and support clinically led service transformation across Wales. We're also taking forward plans for new surgical hubs, to increase clinical capacity and help more patients receive treatment sooner, including those waiting for cataract surgery.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym ni'n cydnabod bod pobl sy'n aros am lawdriniaeth cataract eisiau triniaeth cyn gynted â phosibl, yn amlwg. Dyna pam rydym ni wedi ymrwymo £145 miliwn ychwanegol eleni i leihau amseroedd aros, i wella mynediad ac i gefnogi trawsnewid gwasanaethau dan arweiniad clinigol ledled Cymru. Rydym ni hefyd yn bwrw ymlaen â chynlluniau ar gyfer canolfannau llawfeddygol newydd, i gynyddu capasiti clinigol ac i helpu mwy o gleifion i gael triniaeth yn gynt, gan gynnwys y rhai sy'n aros am lawdriniaeth cataract.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, First Minister. Despite your Government's investment, including the use of higher cost private providers, and the appointment of a Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health, my constituents still face long waits and last-minute cancellations of cataract operations. What long-term action will the Welsh Government take to train more eye surgeons and increase capacity to meet the growing demand from an ageing population, including patients with glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy and those needing regular eye injections to prevent avoidable blindness?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Er gwaethaf buddsoddiad eich Llywodraeth, gan gynnwys defnyddio darparwyr preifat cost uwch, a phenodi Dirprwy Weinidog Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol, mae fy etholwyr yn dal i wynebu arosiadau maith ac achosion o ganslo llawdriniaethau cataract ar y funud olaf. Pa gamau hirdymor wnaiff Llywodraeth Cymru eu cymryd i hyfforddi mwy o lawfeddygon llygaid a chynyddu'r capasiti i fodloni'r galw cynyddol ymhlith poblogaeth sy'n heneiddio, gan gynnwys cleifion â glawcoma neu retinopathi diabetig a'r rhai sydd angen pigiadau llygaid rheolaidd i atal dallineb y gellir ei osgoi?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's one of those areas where you need rapid treatment in order to avoid more permanent damage. We have two ophthalmologists sitting here in the Senedd Chamber who know far more than I do. The Member referenced the bringing in of private providers. That has a role to play. But the big change in emphasis under this Government is not using that as a backstop and instead building up the kind of capacity that can make reductions in waiting times and a smoother passage of patients through the system more sustainable. I'd point to that as being the main element of what we're trying to do here. Details have been provided by the Minister as we've rolled out these new approaches in the first 100 days. I'm confident that that is the kind of long-term thinking that we need.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n un o'r meysydd hynny lle mae angen triniaeth gyflym arnoch chi er mwyn osgoi niwed mwy parhaol. Mae gennym ni ddau offthalmolegydd yn eistedd yma yn Siambr y Senedd sy'n gwybod llawer mwy nag yr wyf i. Cyfeiriodd yr Aelod at gyflwyno darparwyr preifat. Mae gan hynny ran i'w chwarae. Ond nid defnyddio hynny fel opsiwn wrth gefn yw'r newid pwyslais mawr o dan y Llywodraeth hon, ond yn hytrach datblygu'r math o gapasiti a all wneud gostyngiadau i amseroedd aros a thaith fwy rhwydd drwy'r system i gleifion yn fwy cynaliadwy. Byddwn yn tynnu sylw at hynny fel prif elfen yr hyn yr ydym ni'n ceisio ei wneud yma. Darparwyd manylion gan y Gweinidog wrth i ni gyflwyno'r dulliau newydd hyn yn y 100 diwrnod cyntaf. Rwy'n hyderus mai dyna'r math o feddwl hirdymor sydd ei angen arnom ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Amddiffyn Rhentwyr
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Protecting Renters

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog nodi amserlen ar gyfer cyflwyno mesurau newydd i amddiffyn rhentwyr yn well? OQ64467
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. Will the First Minister set out a timeline for the introduction of new measures to better protect renters? OQ64467

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'll refer Members, first of all, to my declaration of interest as a shareholder in a company renting out a domestic property.

Strengthening the private rented sector is a priority for this Government. I think we've made that pretty clear; we set it out in my legislative statement on 14 July. Renters in Wales deserve a safe, warm, secure and affordable home and should feel confident challenging poor conditions. Positive change requires good law, and in the first phase of our legislative programme we'll deliver legislation that protects tenants and tackles poor landlords, making renting, hopefully, more secure.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe wnaf i gyfeirio'r Aelodau, yn gyntaf oll, at fy natganiad o fuddiant fel cyfranddaliwr mewn cwmni sy'n gosod eiddo domestig.

Mae cryfhau'r sector rhentu preifat yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon. Rwy'n credu ein bod ni wedi gwneud hynny'n eithaf eglur; fe wnaethom ni ei nodi yn fy natganiad deddfwriaethol ar 14 Gorffennaf. Mae rhentwyr yng Nghymru yn haeddu cartref diogel, cynnes, sicr a fforddiadwy a dylen nhw deimlo'n hyderus yn herio amodau gwael. Mae newid cadarnhaol yn gofyn am gyfraith dda, ac yng ngham cyntaf ein rhaglen ddeddfwriaethol byddwn yn cyflwyno deddfwriaeth sy'n amddiffyn tenantiaid ac yn mynd i'r afael â landlordiaid gwael, gan wneud rhentu, gobeithio, yn fwy diogel.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. First Minister, we know that immigration increases demand on housing, which, in turn, leads to increased rents. So, can the First Minister confirm that any planned changes to private and social renters' protections will be prioritised for Welsh people over recent arrivals?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Brif Weinidog, rydym ni'n gwybod bod mewnfudo yn cynyddu'r galw am dai, sydd, yn ei dro, yn arwain at renti uwch. Felly, a all y Prif Weinidog gadarnhau y bydd unrhyw newidiadau arfaethedig i amddiffyniadau rhentwyr preifat a chymdeithasol yn cael eu blaenoriaethu ar gyfer pobl Cymru dros bobl sydd wedi cyrraedd yn ddiweddar?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As I've pointed out many times in this Chamber, we have many pressures on housing. Those pressures, when we look at the big picture, do not come from recent arrivals from overseas. I think it's important to home in on those facts. But there are pressures, and we will always want to make sure that our housing stock is adequate in numbers, that the housing stock quality is of a decent level, which people should be able to gain confidence from. But also, we need to look at the question of affordability. We have a two-phased approach in terms of legislation, and affordability will very much be a part of our considerations. I've invited Members here to contribute to the development of legislation, and if there's an interest across this Chamber in those affordability issues, let's discuss them.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel yr wyf i wedi ei nodi sawl gwaith yn y Siambr hon, mae gennym ni lawer o bwysau ar dai. Nid yw'r pwysau hynny, pan edrychwn ni ar y darlun ehangach, yn dod gan bobl sydd wedi cyrraedd o dramor yn ddiweddar. Rwy'n credu ei bod hi'n bwysig canolbwyntio ar y ffeithiau hynny. Ond mae pwysau, a byddwn ni bob amser eisiau gwneud yn siŵr bod ein stoc dai yn ddigonol o ran niferoedd, bod ansawdd y stoc dai o lefel briodol, y dylai pobl allu fagu hyder ohono. Ond hefyd, mae angen i ni edrych ar y cwestiwn o fforddiadwyedd. Mae gennym ni ddull dau gam o ran deddfwriaeth, a bydd fforddiadwyedd yn sicr yn rhan o'n hystyriaethau. Rwyf i wedi gwahodd Aelodau yma i gyfrannu at ddatblygu deddfwriaeth, ac os oes diddordeb ar draws y Siambr hon yn y materion fforddiadwyedd hynny, gadewch i ni eu trafod nhw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prif Weinidog, private renting has become increasingly unaffordable, with many households now spending a really unsustainable amount of their income simply on keeping a roof over their heads. Recent Citizens Advice data has shown that some people are spending up to 70 per cent of their income on rent alone. In Cardiff, there are instances of rents more than doubling now, with just two months' notice. As a consequence, homelessness services are facing increased demand, not only because people are being evicted from their homes, but because council support with rent is also insufficient, placing greater pressure on social housing and temporary accommodation. Does the First Minister agree with me that spending more than two thirds of an individual's income on rent is not acceptable, and that limiting annual rent increases is essential?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, mae rhentu preifat wedi dod yn fwyfwy anfforddiadwy, â llawer o aelwydydd bellach yn gwario swm gwirioneddol anghynaliadwy o'u hincwm ar gadw to dros eu pennau. Mae data Cyngor ar Bopeth diweddar wedi dangos bod rhai pobl yn gwario hyd at 70 y cant o'u hincwm ar rent yn unig. Yng Nghaerdydd, ceir achosion o renti sy'n mwy na dyblu nawr, gyda dim ond dau fis o rybudd. O ganlyniad, mae gwasanaethau digartrefedd yn wynebu galw cynyddol, nid yn unig oherwydd bod pobl yn cael eu troi allan o'u cartrefi, ond oherwydd bod cymorth cynghorau gyda rhent hefyd yn annigonol, gan roi mwy o bwysau ar dai cymdeithasol a llety dros dro. A yw'r Prif Weinidog yn cytuno â mi nad yw gwario mwy na dwy ran o dair o incwm unigolyn ar rent yn dderbyniol, a bod cyfyngu cynnydd rhent blynyddol yn hanfodol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You don't have to think very hard to work out the poverty that somebody is driven into in real terms when they have so little of their income left after paying their rent. In terms of the issues that cause that, there's a multitude of them. Supply of homes is one of them, and social housing. That's why we are determined to bring in an extra 20,000 additional social homes by 2030. It's about bringing homes into use that are currently not in use. It's about raising the quality of the housing stock as well.

And then there are things, as I've said, that we can do through legislation. Actively exploring different measures for regulating increases in rent, for example, effectively is really important. We can look at what's happening in Scotland. There are learnings from Catalonia too. It's important that we look at what works well, and also look at potential drawbacks. But significant steps need considerable policy development, evidence gathering, and cross-party and cross-sector engagement, which is why we have outlined our ambition to bring forward that second renters Bill as part of a two-phase legislative approach.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Does dim rhaid i chi feddwl yn galed iawn i weithio allan y tlodi y mae rhywun yn cael ei yrru iddo mewn termau real pan fo ganddyn nhw gyn lleied o'i incwm yn weddill ar ôl talu ei rent. O ran y materion sy'n achosi hynny, mae llu ohonyn nhw. Mae cyflenwad cartrefi yn un ohonyn nhw, a thai cymdeithasol. Dyna pam rydym ni'n benderfynol o gyflwyno 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol ychwanegol erbyn 2030. Mae'n fater o ddod â chartrefi i ddefnydd nad ydyn nhw'n cael eu defnyddio ar hyn o bryd. Mae'n fater o godi ansawdd y stoc dai hefyd.

Ac yna ceir pethau, fel y dywedais i, y gallwn ni eu gwneud drwy ddeddfwriaeth. Mae archwilio gwahanol fesurau ar gyfer rheoleiddio cynnydd i rent, er enghraifft, yn effeithiol yn bwysig iawn. Gallwn edrych ar yr hyn sy'n digwydd yn yr Alban. Mae pethau i'w dysgu gan Gatalwnia hefyd. Mae'n bwysig ein bod ni'n edrych ar yr hyn sy'n gweithio'n dda, a hefyd yn edrych ar anfanteision posibl. Ond mae camau sylweddol angen datblygiad polisi sylweddol, casglu tystiolaeth, ac ymgysylltu trawsbleidiol a thraws-sector, a dyna pam rydym ni wedi amlinellu ein huchelgais i gyflwyno'r Bil ail rentwyr hwnnw yn rhan o ddull deddfwriaethol dau gam.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: There's a shortage of housing available for renting. There's an even greater shortage of housing available at affordable rents. The long-term solution is to build more social housing, especially council housing. I have supported rent controls and the return of rent officers for privately rented properties. But we now have a new, very serious problem, Airbnb, which is taking properties out of the private rented sector. This is not a seaside and holiday resort problem only. It is also a problem in cities. What action is the Welsh Government going to take to limit Airbnb in each council area?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae prinder tai ar gael i'w rhentu. Mae prinder mwy fyth o dai sydd ar gael am renti fforddiadwy. Yr ateb hirdymor yw adeiladu mwy o dai cymdeithasol, yn enwedig tai cyngor. Rwyf i wedi cefnogi rheolaethau rhent a dychweliad swyddogion rhent ar gyfer eiddo rhentu preifat . Ond mae gennym ni bellach broblem newydd, ddifrifol iawn, sef Airbnb, sy'n tynnu eiddo allan o'r sector rhentu preifat. Nid problem glan môr a chyrchfannau gwyliau yn unig yw hon. Mae hefyd yn broblem mewn dinasoedd. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn mynd i'w cymryd i gyfyngu Airbnb ym mhob ardal cyngor?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member makes a very good point, and it's an international problem. We have seen some big cities take action on Airbnb. We tend in Wales to look at the more popular seaside areas, because that's where the problems are perceived to be more acute. But the Member is absolutely right that this is an issue that can arise anywhere. I (a) agree that it's an issue, and (b) want us to look at all those solutions that can be put in place. Some have been introduced through co-operation between our parties in the last Government—changes that lead to changing behaviour through use of premiums on council tax and so on. But there are also planning changes that we should always be alive to considering, because I agree this is a significant issue. The main purpose of a house, a flat or an apartment is to be a home, and we should always bear that in mind.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod yn gwneud pwynt da iawn, ac mae'n broblem ryngwladol. Rydym ni wedi gweld rhai dinasoedd mawr yn cymryd camau ar Airbnb. Rydym ni'n tueddu yng Nghymru i edrych ar yr ardaloedd glan môr mwy poblogaidd, oherwydd dyna lle tybir fod y problemau yn fwy dybryd. Ond mae'r Aelod yn llygad ei le bod hon yn broblem sy'n gallu codi yn unrhyw le. Rwy'n (a) cytuno ei fod yn broblem, a (b) eisiau i ni edrych ar yr holl atebion hynny y gellir eu rhoi ar waith. Mae rhai wedi cael eu cyflwyno trwy gydweithrediad rhwng ein pleidiau yn y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf—newidiadau sy'n arwain at newid ymddygiad trwy ddefnyddio premiymau ar dreth gyngor ac yn y blaen. Ond ceir newidiadau cynllunio hefyd y dylem ni bob amser fod yn effro i'w hystyried, oherwydd rwy'n cytuno bod hon yn broblem sylweddol. Prif ddiben tŷ neu fflat yw bod yn gartref, a dylem ni bob amser gadw hynny mewn cof.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog ddatganiad ar y canlyniadau PISA diweddar a gyhoeddwyd ar gyfer Cymru? OQ64450
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. Will the First Minister make a statement on the recently published PISA results for Wales? OQ64450

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: These PISA results are, to say the least, deeply disappointing. They underline to me the scale of the challenge that we face. They reinforce this Government’s determination to take a new and rigorous approach to raising standards. We'll be unapologetically ambitious for every learner, setting clear targets, holding ourselves accountable for delivering them, because raising standards has to be a priority. Today, we publish that foundational literacy and numeracy plan that I have previously referenced to accelerate improvement across Wales in every classroom, because our children and families in Wales deserve nothing less.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r canlyniadau PISA hyn, a dweud y lleiaf, yn hynod siomedig. Maen nhw'n tanlinellu i mi faint yr her sy'n ein hwynebu. Maen nhw'n atgyfnerthu penderfyniad y Llywodraeth hon i fabwysiadu dull newydd a thrwyadl o godi safonau. Byddwn yn uchelgeisiol, heb ymddiheuriad, i bob dysgwr, gan osod targedau eglur, dwyn ein hunain i gyfrif am eu cyflawni, oherwydd mae'n rhaid i godi safonau fod yn flaenoriaeth. Heddiw, rydym ni'n cyhoeddi'r cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol hwnnw yr wyf i wedi cyfeirio ato yn flaenorol i gyflymu gwelliant ledled Cymru ym mhob ystafell ddosbarth, oherwydd nid yw ein plant a'n teuluoedd yng Nghymru yn haeddu dim llai.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for your response, First Minister, but the issues you've outlined are part of the reason why Members in this place and the public at large are so frustrated with your obsessive pursuit of independence when what you should be doing is focusing on these issues in the classrooms to support our children for the best outcomes possible. Wales is falling behind every other UK nation in maths, reading and science, with the gap particularly stark when compared with England. You rightfully want to work with other countries and co-operate and learn from them. Why don't you learn from England as to how they are doing so well with their education outcomes compared with our children here in Wales?

If we're serious about driving up those standards, we have to also address what is happening in our classrooms. We've heard time and time again from Estyn and the teaching unions as to poor behaviour as an issue in our classrooms. We've been clear that teachers need to be properly supported, schools need a stronger approach to discipline, so that teachers can teach and pupils can learn without unnecessary disruption. Given these disappointing PISA results, First Minister, will you accept that improving discipline, supporting teachers and restoring high expectations in our classrooms must be at the heart of any plan to raise educational standards?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am eich ymateb, Brif Weinidog, ond mae'r materion yr ydych chi wedi eu hamlinellu yn rhan o'r rheswm pam mae Aelodau yn y lle hwn a'r cyhoedd yn gyffredinol yn teimlo mor rhwystredig am eich ymdrech obsesiynol i sicrhau annibyniaeth pan mai'r hyn y dylech chi fod yn ei wneud yw canolbwyntio ar y problemau hyn yn yr ystafelloedd dosbarth i gynorthwyo ein plant ar gyfer y canlyniadau gorau posibl. Mae Cymru yn syrthio y tu ôl i bob cenedl arall yn y DU o ran mathemateg, darllen a gwyddoniaeth, gyda'r bwlch yn arbennig o amlwg o'i gymharu â Lloegr. Rydych chi, yn gwbl briodol, eisiau gweithio gyda gwledydd eraill a chydweithredu a dysgu oddi wrthyn nhw. Pam na wnewch chi ddysgu gan Loegr sut maen nhw'n gwneud mor dda gyda'u canlyniadau addysg o'u cymharu â'n plant yma yng Nghymru?

Os ydym ni o ddifrif ynglŷn â chodi'r safonau hynny, mae'n rhaid i ni hefyd fynd i'r afael â'r hyn sy'n digwydd yn ein hystafelloedd dosbarth. Rydym ni wedi clywed dro ar ôl tro gan Estyn a'r undebau addysgu ynghylch ymddygiad gwael fel problem yn ein hystafelloedd dosbarth. Rydym ni wedi bod yn eglur bod angen cefnogi athrawon yn briodol, bod angen dull cryfach o ymdrin â disgyblaeth ar ysgolion, fel y gall athrawon addysgu ac y gall disgyblion ddysgu heb darfu diangen. O ystyried y canlyniadau PISA siomedig hyn, Brif Weinidog, a wnewch chi dderbyn bod yn rhaid i wella disgyblaeth, cefnogi athrawon ac ailgyflwyno disgwyliadau uchel yn ein hystafelloedd dosbarth fod yn ganolog i unrhyw gynllun i godi safonau addysgol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Given the importance of education, I'm surprised that he wasted some of his question discussing constitutional issues, frankly. We have a determination as a Government to look to our track record historically as a proud educating nation—one of the first generally literate populations anywhere in the world. That's something that makes me very proud. I was proud to have two parents that were educationalists, two teaching union presidents. I was brought up with the importance of getting education right and giving our children and young people opportunities right there surrounding me at all times.

I'm desperately disappointed at the PISA results. The measures that we are putting in place around numeracy and literacy, supporting teachers, supporting families and children, are all about raising outcomes. I hope that one of the results of that will be increased PISA scores. There's a global downturn in PISA scores, incidentally. Digitalisation and artificial intelligence might be a part of that. But England has bucked the trend and, absolutely, we should be, and we are making plans already to learn from England about what's happening there. My co-operation isn't exclusively with Scotland and Northern Ireland. I point that out—we work with Ministers in UK Government and internationally too, and on this one, it's because we need to raise standards. And the outcome that we need, of course—better PISA scores would be good—would be raised educational standards: numeracy, literacy, the basics, the foundations of successful lives and careers for our young people. That's what we're aiming for, and we're confident that we're putting the building blocks in place.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
O ystyried pwysigrwydd addysg, rwy'n synnu ei fod wedi gwastraffu rhywfaint o'i gwestiwn yn trafod materion cyfansoddiadol, a bod yn onest. Mae gennym ni benderfyniad fel Llywodraeth i edrych ar ein cofnod hanesyddol fel cenedl addysgu falch—un o'r poblogaethau cyffredinol llythrennog cyntaf yn unrhyw le yn y byd. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth sy'n fy ngwneud i'n falch iawn. Roeddwn i'n falch o fod â dau riant a oedd yn addysgwyr, dau lywydd undebau addysgu. Cefais fy magu gyda phwysigrwydd cael addysg yn iawn a rhoi cyfleoedd i'n plant a'n pobl ifanc o'm cwmpas yn y fan a'r lle bob amser.

Rwy'n siomedig dros ben â'r canlyniadau PISA. Mae'r mesurau yr ydym ni'n eu rhoi ar waith o ran rhifedd a llythrennedd, cefnogi athrawon, cefnogi teuluoedd a phlant, yn fater syml o wella canlyniadau. Rwy'n gobeithio mai un o ganlyniadau hynny fydd sgoriau PISA uwch. Mae dirywiad byd-eang i sgoriau PISA, gyda llaw. Efallai fod digideiddio a deallusrwydd artiffisial yn rhan o hynny. Ond mae Lloegr wedi mynd yn groes i'r duedd ac, yn sicr, dylem ni fod, ac rydym ni eisoes yn gwneud cynlluniau i ddysgu gan Loegr am yr hyn sy'n digwydd yno. Nid yw fy nghydweithrediad gyda'r Alban a Gogledd Iwerddon yn unig. Rwy'n tynnu sylw at hynny—rydym ni'n gweithio gyda Gweinidogion yn Llywodraeth y DU ac yn rhyngwladol hefyd, ac ar yr un yma, mae oherwydd bod angen i ni godi safonau. A'r canlyniad sydd ei angen arnom ni, wrth gwrs—byddai gwell sgoriau PISA yn dda—fyddai safonau addysgol uwch: rhifedd, llythrennedd, y pethau sylfaenol, sylfeini bywydau a gyrfaoedd llwyddiannus i'n pobl ifanc. Dyna'r hyn yr ydym ni'n anelu amdano, ac rydym ni'n hyderus ein bod ni'n rhoi'r blociau adeiladu yn eu lle.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Pa drafodaethau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'u cael gyda Llywodraeth y DU i sicrhau bod Port Talbot yn cael cyfran deg o Gronfa Ddur y DU? OQ64443
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. What discussions has the Welsh Government had with the UK Government to ensure that Port Talbot gets a fair share of the UK Steel Fund? OQ64443

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae cefnogi'r diwydiant dur a chymunedau dur sy'n dibynnu arno fo ledled Cymru yn hollbwysig i'r Llywodraeth yma. Cyn ymweliad diweddar Prif Weinidog y Deyrnas Unedig â Phort Talbot, mi wnaeth ein Dirprwy Brif Weinidog ni siarad yn gyhoeddus am yr angen i Gymru gael ei chyfran deg o gronfa ddur Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig. Mi fu cyfarfod rhwng y ddau. Mi fyddai hynny, wrth gwrs, yn helpu gweithwyr a chymunedau drwy'r cyfnod pontio, ac mi fyddwn ni'n parhau i wneud yr achos hwnnw mor gryf â phosib yn ein trafodaethau ni efo Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Supporting the steel industry and the communities across Wales that depend on it is a priority for this Government. Ahead of the Prime Minister's recent visit to Port Talbot, the Deputy First Minister spoke publicly about the need for Wales to receive its fair share of the UK Government's steel fund. There was a meeting between the two. That, of course, would help workers and communities through the transition period, and we will continue to make that case as strongly as possible in ongoing discussions with the UK Government.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Prif Weinidog, as you mentioned, the Prime Minister came to Port Talbot last month, promising re-industrialisation and good, secure jobs. The UK's own steel strategy says that Wales is expected to account for around half of the UK's steel-making capacity, yet just days after the Prime Minister's visit, his Government was asked two very straightforward questions: how much of its £2.5 billion steel commitment had been spent or allocated and how much of that had been spent in Wales? It could provide a figure for neither. So, I have to ask the question: what will actually change for Port Talbot since Andy Burnham's visit? And I'm sure I know part of the answer, but will you press him for a firm commitment that Port Talbot receives its fair share of that £2.5 billion?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Brif Weinidog, fel roeddech chi'n sôn, daeth Prif Weinidog y DU i Bort Talbot fis diwethaf, gan addo ail-ddiwydiannu a swyddi da, diogel. Mae strategaeth ddur y DU ei hun yn dweud bod disgwyl i Gymru gyfrif am tua hanner capasiti'r DU i gynhyrchu dur, ond ychydig ddyddiau wedi ymweliad y Prif Weinidog, fe ofynnwyd dau gwestiwn syml iawn i'w Lywodraeth ef: faint o'i £2.5 biliwn o'r ymrwymiad i ddur a gafodd ei wario neu ei ddyrannu a faint o hynny a gafodd ei wario yng Nghymru? Ni ellid rhoi ffigwr ar gyfer y naill na'r llall. Felly, mae'n rhaid i mi ofyn y cwestiwn: beth fydd yn newid i Bort Talbot ar ôl ymweliad Andy Burnham? Ac rwy'n siŵr fy mod i'n gwybod rhan o'r ateb, ond a fyddwch chi'n pwyso arno ef am ymrwymiad cadarn y bydd Port Talbot yn cael ei chyfran deg o'r £2.5 biliwn hwnnw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member is right to voice frustrations about what did or didn't come out of that investment. The purpose of it was changed at one point, but one thing we made clear from our position—we still make it clear from Government—is that we must get our fair share of that. We have taken a massive hit to the steel industry here in Wales because UK Governments took their eyes off the ball and didn't act when they should have done.

Welsh Government will work with companies, UK Government and the national wealth fund, which now has control over that £2.5 billion, to explore how support can be maximised and must be maximised for our steel communities across Wales. Let me be clear, if there is investment being made in the steel sector, UK Government must set out clearly how they plan to support the Welsh steel industry, which is what is important to us here.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn iawn i fynegi rhwystredigaethau ynglŷn â'r hyn a ddaeth o'r buddsoddiad hwnnw neu beidio. Cafodd ei bwrpas ei newid ar un adeg, ond un peth a wnaethom ni'n glir o'n safbwynt ni—rydym ni'n dal i egluro hynny yn y Llywodraeth—yw bod yn rhaid i ni gael ein cyfran deg o hwnnw. Rydym ni wedi cael ergyd enfawr i'r diwydiant dur yma yng Nghymru am fod Llywodraethau'r DU wedi tynnu eu llygaid oddi ar y bêl ac heb gymryd camau pan ddylen nhw fod wedi gwneud hynny.

Fe fydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gyda chwmnïau, Llywodraeth y DU a'r gronfa gyfoeth wladol, sy'n rheoli'r £2.5 biliwn hwnnw erbyn hyn, i archwilio sut y gellir gwneud y mwyaf o'r gefnogaeth ar gyfer ein cymunedau cynhyrchu dur ledled Cymru. Gadewch i mi fod yn eglur, os caiff buddsoddiad ei wneud yn y sector dur, mae'n rhaid i Lywodraeth y DU nodi yn bendant sut y bydd hi'n bwriadu cefnogi diwydiant dur Cymru, a dyna'r hyn sy'n bwysig i ni yn y fan hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 8. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi diweddariad ar sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gyda Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Bae Abertawe i ailgychwyn triniaeth ffrwythlondeb yn Sefydliad Ffrwythlondeb Cymru? OQ64431
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. Will the First Minister provide an update on how the Welsh Government is working with Swansea Bay University Health Board to restart fertility treatment at the Wales Fertility Institute? OQ64431

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I know that this will have been a particularly upsetting time for those affected. The immediate workforce issue affecting the service has now been resolved—that's the positive news—enabling planning to start for the resumption of the service, on a phased basis, from 22 September. It is important to note that patients already receiving treatment also were unaffected by the pause and continued their treatment in the usual way. But this has been a difficult time for a number of people.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n gwybod i hwn fod yn gyfnod arbennig o ofidus i'r rhai hynny yr effeithiwyd arnynt. Mae'r mater uniongyrchol o ran y gweithlu a oedd yn effeithio ar y gwasanaeth wedi cael ei ddatrys erbyn hyn—dyna'r newyddion cadarnhaol—sy'n caniatáu i gynllunio ddechrau ar gyfer ailgychwyn y gwasanaeth, o gam i gam, o 22 Medi. Mae'n bwysig nodi hefyd na fu effaith ar gleifion a oedd eisoes yn cael triniaethau, yn sgil yr oedi, â'u bod nhw wedi parhau â'u triniaethau yn y ffordd arferol. Ond mae hwn wedi bod yn gyfnod anodd i nifer o bobl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for your answer, First Minister. It is positive that the system is being started again, but a lot of those people who said their treatment wasn't affected were actually affected, because if you were waiting for frozen embryo transfer, people were told that their treatment was not starting. So, there was miscommunication there from the health board that did cause a lot of upset for a number of families right the way across the country, because, as you know, that centre covers a huge geographical area, all the way from west Wales, east Wales, south Wales and all the way up to Llandrindod Wells.

First Minister, we never want to be in this situation again, because it is a traumatic time, not just for the mothers and the fathers, but for everyone going through a fertility journey. So, what can the Welsh Government do to make sure there is resilience in this service, to make sure people are not waiting years and years and years—which people are—for their fertility journey, because people have a body clock, and if we cannot get this system started soon enough, a lot of people across this country will never have the families that they hope to start?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch i chi am eich ateb, Brif Weinidog. Mae hi'n galonogol bod y system yn cael ei hailgychwyn, ond fe gafodd llawer o'r bobl hynny a oedd yn dweud na chafodd eu triniaethau eu heffeithio wedi cael eu heffeithio mewn gwirionedd, oherwydd os oeddech chi'n aros am drosglwyddo embryo rhewedig, fe ddywedwyd wrth bobl nad oedd eu triniaethau nhw am ddechrau. Felly, roedd camgyfathrebu gan y bwrdd iechyd yn hynny o beth a wnaeth achosi gofid i nifer o deuluoedd ledled y wlad, oherwydd, fel y gwyddoch chi, mae'r ganolfan honno'n cwmpasu ardal ddaearyddol enfawr, yr holl ffordd o'r gorllewin, y dwyrain, y de, a'r holl ffordd hyd at Landrindod.

Brif Weinidog, nid ydym ni'n dymuno bod yn y sefyllfa hon fyth eto, oherwydd mae'n gyfnod cythryblus, nid yn unig i'r mamau a'r tadau, ond i bawb sy'n ymdrin â materion ffrwythlondeb. Felly, beth all Llywodraeth Cymru ei wneud i sicrhau bod gwydnwch yn y gwasanaeth hwn, i sicrhau nad yw pobl yn aros blynyddoedd lawer iawn—fel gwna rhai—am eu taith ffrwythlondeb, oherwydd mae gan bobl gloc corff, ac os na allwn ni gychwyn y system hon yn ddigon cynnar, ni fydd llawer o bobl ledled y wlad hon byth yn gweld y teuluoedd y maen nhw'n gobeithio eu cychwyn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: That word 'resilience' is important. We use 'sustainability'. They mean very much the same when it comes to something like this: having services that are stable. In this particular case, the pause was necessary in order to comply with the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority licensing requirement. So, a clinical issue, but the impact, of course, is a very human issue. We will do what we can to build resilience across those services. For the individuals affected here, the health board has now started contacting patients, I understand, to confirm the next steps in their treatment pathway. The Wales Fertility Institute is continuing to work on the wider workforce challenges, working with the joint commissioning committee to explore possibilities for, perhaps, interim support options to comply with those licensing requirements, which are a must; these aren't optional. Work is also ongoing to strengthen, as you say, the resilience and sustainability of the service, both within the health board itself and in conjunction with that relationship that it has with the joint commissioning committee. That work will continue. Yes, there are short-term things to do, but that will continue beyond the short term too.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r gair hwnnw, 'gwydnwch', yn un pwysig. Fe fyddwn ni'n defnyddio 'cynaliadwyedd'. Maen nhw'n golygu'r un peth yn union o ran rhywbeth fel hyn: bod â gwasanaethau sefydlog. Yn yr achos arbennig hwn, roedd y saib yn angenrheidiol ar gyfer cydymffurfio â gofyniad trwyddedu'r Awdurdod Ffrwythlondeb ac Embryoleg Dynol. Felly, roedd hwnnw'n fater clinigol, ond roedd ei effaith, wrth gwrs, yn ddynol iawn. Fe fyddwn ni'n gwneud yr hyn a allwn ni i feithrin gwydnwch ar draws y gwasanaethau hynny. Ar gyfer yr unigolion yr effeithiwyd arnynt yma, mae'r bwrdd iechyd wedi dechrau cysylltu â chleifion erbyn hyn, rwy'n deall, i gadarnhau'r camau nesaf ar lwybr eu triniaeth. Mae Sefydliad Ffrwythlondeb Cymru yn parhau i weithio ar yr heriau ehangach o ran y gweithlu, gan weithio gyda'r cyd-bwyllgor comisiynu i archwilio posibiliadau ar gyfer dewisiadau cymorth dros dro i gydymffurfio â'r gofynion trwyddedu hynny, sy'n angenrheidiol; nid yw'r rhain yn ddewisol. Mae gwaith yn mynd rhagddo hefyd i gryfhau, fel rydych chi'n dweud, gwydnwch a chynaliadwyedd y gwasanaeth, yn y bwrdd iechyd ei hun ac ar y cyd gyda'r berthynas honno sydd ganddo â'r cyd-bwyllgor comisiynu. Fe fydd y gwaith hwnnw'n parhau. Oes, mae yna bethau i'w gwneud yn y byrdymor, ond fe fydd hynny'n parhau wedi'r byrdymor hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cyllid Teg i Gymru
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fair Funding for Wales

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 9. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am ei drafodaethau gyda Llywodraeth y DU ar sicrhau cyllid teg i Gymru? OQ64457
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 9. Will the First Minister provide an update on his discussions with the UK Government on securing fair funding for Wales? OQ64457

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This Government is committed to pressing the case for a fairer funding settlement for Wales. That means a number of different things. When I met the Prime Minister in Glasgow in July, I emphasised the need for the historic underfunding of Wales to be addressed. On Thursday, we will be hosting the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee, bringing together finance Ministers from right across the UK, if that's okay with everyone.

Funding reform is a key priority for the Cabinet Minister for Finance, and in her bilateral meeting with the Chief Secretary to the Treasury that day she will raise a number of priorities, which include delivering the £14 billion promise on rail, a formal review of the fiscal framework and the Barnett formula. I will also make this case directly to the Prime Minister when we meet again in October.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi ymrwymo i wthio'r achos dros setliad cyllido tecach i Gymru. Mae hynny'n golygu nifer o wahanol bethau. Pan wnes i gyfarfod â Phrif Weinidog y DU yn Glasgow ym mis Gorffennaf, fe wnes i bwysleisio'r angen i fynd i'r afael â thanariannu hanesyddol Cymru. Ddydd Iau, fe fyddwn ni'n croesawu'r Pwyllgor Sefydlog Rhyngweinidogol ar Gyllid, sy'n dod â Gweinidogion cyllid o bob cwr o'r DU at ei gilydd, os yw hynny'n iawn gyda phawb.

Mae diwygio cyllid yn flaenoriaeth allweddol i Weinidog Cyllid y Cabinet, ac yn ei chyfarfod dwyochrog gyda Phrif Ysgrifennydd y Trysorlys ar y diwrnod hwnnw fe fydd hi'n codi nifer o flaenoriaethau, sy'n cynnwys cyflawni'r addewid £14 biliwn o ran rheilffyrdd, ac adolygiad ffurfiol o'r fframwaith cyllidol a fformiwla Barnett. Fe fyddaf i'n dadlau'r achos hwn yn uniongyrchol i'r Prif Weinidog hefyd pan fyddwn ni'n cyfarfod unwaith eto ym mis Hydref.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I funded businesses for over 40 years. To succeed, a business needs two things, essentially: the ability to borrow and the ability to save. Running a country is no different. Without the financial tools to construct a functioning economy, Wales will continue to be poor. Is this the Wales that we all want for our children? Wales is being pickpocketed. You mentioned about rail. HS2: we're footing the bill for infrastructure projects in England whilst ours crumble. And why? The Barnett formula gives us less per head than our Northern Irish and Scottish counterparts. Why? Demanding fair funding is not us taking the begging bowl to London, nor is it grievance politics. It's common sense and the bare minimum to stop ingrained, intergenerational poverty, which plagues Wales. It doesn't have to be this way. We have the entrepreneurs, we have the people, the skills and the resources. Wales can be prosperous.

First Minister, following your meeting yesterday with the Ministers of Northern Ireland and Scotland, would you please outline your long-term vision of what a real Government can achieve economically in Wales with the right economic levers?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe fues i'n ariannu busnesau am dros 40 mlynedd. I lwyddo, mae angen dau beth ar fusnes: y gallu i fenthyca a'r gallu i gynilo. Nid yw rhedeg gwlad yn ddim gwahanol. Yn absenoldeb arfau ariannol i adeiladu economi sy'n gweithio, bydd Cymru yn dal i fod yn dlawd. Ai dyma'r Gymru yr ydym ni ei heisiau ar gyfer ein plant? Mae Cymru'n cael ei phluo. Roeddech chi'n sôn am reilffyrdd. HS2: rydym ni'n talu biliau am brosiectau seilwaith yn Lloegr tra bod ein seilwaith ni yn chwalu. A pham felly? Mae fformwla Barnett yn rhoi llai o arian y pen na'n cymheiriaid yng Ngogledd Iwerddon a'r Alban. Pam? Nid yw mynnu cyllid teg yn golygu ein bod ni'n mynd i Lundain i ofyn cardod, nac yn wleidyddiaeth achwyniad ychwaith. Synnwyr cyffredin yw hyn a'r peth lleiaf i atal tlodi sydd wedi ymwreiddio, o un genhedlaeth i'r llall, sy'n plagio Cymru. Nid oes raid iddi fod fel hyn. Mae'r entrepreneuriaid gennym ni, mae'r bobl, y sgiliau a'r adnoddau gennym ni. Fe all Cymru fod yn ffyniannus.

Brif Weinidog, yn dilyn eich cyfarfod gyda Gweinidogion Gogledd Iwerddon a'r Alban ddoe, a wnewch chi amlinellu eich gweledigaeth hirdymor o'r hyn y gall Llywodraeth wirioneddol ei gyflawni yn economaidd yng Nghymru gyda'r ysgogiadau economaidd cywir?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm grateful for the question. Right across the UK, we should be—. There is an interest in making sure that when the Treasury makes decisions on spending they are made fairly. It relates to Scotland, it relates to Northern Ireland, it also relates to regions of England. What I will do as the First Minister of Wales, with my team, with your backing here hopefully, is make the case always for us to get that fair funding package.

That does include all those different elements: giving us the borrowing powers; giving us the right to be able to draw down from our reserves; making sure that the overall package under Barnett actually works for us; making sure that where there is a lack of powers—on rail, for example—that that doesn't mean we end up £5 billion out of pocket on HS2. There are fundamental unfairnesses right across the board. The Cabinet Minister for Finance will reinforce those points with the UK Treasury later this week. We look forward to working positively with them in helping them to recognise the value of devolution and giving us the tools to do the job that we're here to do.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n ddiolchgar am y cwestiwn. Ledled y DU, fe ddylem ni—. Mae yna ddiddordeb o ran sicrhau pan fydd Trysorlys yn gwneud penderfyniadau ar wariant eu bod yn cael eu gwneud yn deg. Mae'n berthnasol i'r Alban, yn berthnasol i Ogledd Iwerddon, mae'n berthnasol i ranbarthau Lloegr hefyd. Yr hyn y byddaf i'n ei wneud fel Prif Weinidog Cymru, gyda fy nhîm, gyda'ch cefnogaeth chi yma rwy'n gobeithio, yw dadlau'r achos bob amser i ni fod â'r pecyn cyllido teg hwnnw.

Mae hynny'n cynnwys yr holl wahanol elfennau hynny: rhoi'r pwerau benthyca i ni; rhoi'r hawl i ni allu tynnu i lawr o'n cronfeydd wrth gefn; sicrhau bod y pecyn cyffredinol o dan Barnett yn gweithio yn wirioneddol i ni; sicrhau nad yw hynny'n golygu ein bod ni'n colli £5 biliwn oherwydd HS2. Mae yna annhegwch sylfaenol drwyddi draw. Fe fydd Gweinidog Cyllid y Cabinet yn atgyfnerthu'r pwyntiau hynny gyda Thrysorlys y DU yn ddiweddarach yr wythnos hon. Rydym ni'n edrych ymlaen at weithio mewn dull cadarnhaol gyda nhw i'w helpu i gydnabod gwerth datganoli a rhoi'r offer i ni wneud y gwaith yr ydym ni yma i'w wneud.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Strengthening the governance of the NHS is very, very important for my health team and all of us in Government, with actions having already been undertaken as part of the first 100 days plan. This includes ensuring patients have full confidence that concerns will be heard, that they'll be investigated quickly and used, crucially, to improve care. A new national clinical governance framework to improve clinical governance across NHS Wales will be published early in 2027, bringing together those issues of safeguarding, patient safety, quality improvement and organisational learning to support safer services and greater accountability too.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae cryfhau llywodraethu'r GIG yn bwysig iawn, iawn i fy nhîm iechyd a phob un ohonom ni yn y Llywodraeth, ac mae chamau eisoes wedi'u cymryd fel rhan o'r cynllun 100 diwrnod cyntaf. Mae hyn yn cynnwys sicrhau bod gan gleifion hyder llawn y bydd pryderon yn cael eu clywed, y byddan nhw'n cael eu hymchwilio'n gyflym a'u defnyddio, yn hollbwysig, i wella gofal. Bydd fframwaith llywodraethu clinigol cenedlaethol newydd i wella llywodraethu clinigol ledled GIG Cymru yn cael ei gyhoeddi yn gynnar yn 2027, gan ddod â'r materion diogelu, diogelwch cleifion, gwella ansawdd a dysgu sefydliadol hynny at ei gilydd i gefnogi gwasanaethau mwy diogel a mwy o atebolrwydd hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. The Welsh Gender Service has been subject to an independent clinical review because NHS Wales commissioners identified concerns about the appropriateness of referrals and the robustness of clinical governance and patient safeguards, yet 26 of your own backbenchers have publicly objected to the clinically led pause. There is not a modicum of evidence that this Welsh Government and Plaid Cymru have demonstrated that patient safety comes before ideology. So, if the independent review concludes that the Welsh Gender Service's current assessment process must fundamentally change or that some referrals should not have proceeded, will you guarantee—'yes' or 'no'—that your Government will accept the clinicians' conclusions in full, without political interference from Ministers, backbenchers or campaign groups, even if those conclusions are politically inconvenient? 'Yes' or 'no'?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi. Mae Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru wedi bod yn destun adolygiad clinigol annibynnol am fod comisiynwyr GIG Cymru wedi nodi pryderon ynghylch priodoldeb atgyfeiriadau a chadernid llywodraethu clinigol a diogelwch cleifion, ond mae 26 o blith eich meinciau cefn chi wedi mynegi gwrthwynebiad yn gyhoeddus i'r oedi a arweiniwyd yn glinigol. Nid oes y mymryn lleiaf o dystiolaeth bod Llywodraeth Cymru a Phlaid Cymru wedi arddangos bod diogelwch cleifion yn dod o flaen ideoleg. Felly, os yw'r adolygiad annibynnol yn dod i'r casgliad y bydd yn rhaid i broses asesu bresennol Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru newid yn sylfaenol neu na ddylai rhai atgyfeiriadau fod wedi digwydd, a wnewch chi warantu—'gwnewch' neu 'na wnewch'—y bydd eich Llywodraeth chi'n derbyn casgliadau'r clinigwyr yn llawn, heb ymyrraeth wleidyddol oddi wrth Weinidogion, y meinciau cefn na grwpiau ymgyrchu, hyd yn oed os yw'r casgliadau hynny'n anghyfleus yn wleidyddol? 'Gwnewch' neu 'na wnewch'?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We've made it very, very clear that, yes, this will be judged on clinical evidence. That's what this is about. This hasn't been about Ministers making decisions, this has been the joint commissioning committee. There's a real irony, though, isn't there, about this throwing of an accusation of behaving in an ideological way when we have extreme ideology from the Reform benches here, not interested at all in the anxiety caused by this pause in services for some very, very vulnerable people, many of whom have been ably represented by Members of my party and, no doubt, others too.

Let's remember who is at the heart of issues like this—people who are feeling that they are paying the price for the failure of a health system. What we need to make sure is that we have a review to understand exactly what has happened based on clinical evidence. That's what everybody wants to see happening, whilst supporting the trans community in the process.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe'i gwnaethom ni hi'n eglur iawn, iawn y bydd hyn yn cael ei farnu ar sail tystiolaeth glinigol. Dyna beth mae hwn yn ymwneud ag o. Nid yw hyn wedi bod am Weinidogion yn gwneud penderfyniadau, y cyd-bwyllgor comisiynu sydd wedi gwneud hyn. Mae yna eironi gwirioneddol, fodd bynnag, onid oes, ynglŷn â gwneud cyhuddiad fel hwn o ymddwyn mewn ffordd ideolegol pan fyddwn ni'n cael ideoleg eithafol o feinciau Reform yn y fan hon, heb fod â diddordeb o gwbl yn y pryder a achosir gan yr oedi hwn i wasanaethau ar gyfer rhai pobl agored iawn, iawn i niwed y mae llawer ohonyn nhw wedi cael eu cynrychioli yn fedrus gan Aelodau fy mhlaid i ac eraill hefyd, yn ddiamau.

Gadewch i ni gofio pwy sydd wrth wraidd materion fel hyn—pobl sy'n teimlo eu bod nhw'n talu'r pris am fethiant cyfundrefn iechyd. Yr hyn y mae angen i ni ei sicrhau yw bod adolygiad gennym ni er mwyn deall yn union yr hyn sydd wedi digwydd ar sail tystiolaeth glinigol. Dyna'r hyn y mae pawb yn awyddus i'w weld yn digwydd, wrth gefnogi'r gymuned drawsrywiol yn y broses honno.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Y Cwricwlwm i Gymru
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Curriculum for Wales

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 11. Pa gymorth a ddarparwyd gan Lywodraeth Cymru i ysgolion o ran cyflwyno'r Cwricwlwm i Gymru yn ystod ei 100 diwrnod cyntaf mewn grym? OQ64475
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 11. What support did the Welsh Government provide to schools to deliver the Curriculum for Wales during its first 100 days in office? OQ64475

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: In our first 100 days, our national support programme for curriculum and assessment design has provided expert coaching and learning through national events to, I understand, over 250 schools and 340 practitioners across Wales. We have committed to reviewing the curriculum for Wales so that we can be clear that it ensures every learner benefits from high standards and excellent teaching always.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn ein 100 diwrnod cyntaf, mae ein rhaglen gymorth genedlaethol ar gyfer dylunio ac asesu cwricwlwm wedi darparu hyfforddiant a dysgu arbenigol trwy ddigwyddiadau cenedlaethol, rwy'n deall, ar gyfer dros 250 o ysgolion a 340 o ymarferwyr ledled Cymru. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i adolygu'r cwricwlwm i Gymru er mwyn gallu bod yn glir ei fod yn sicrhau y bydd pob dysgwr yn elwa ar safonau uchel ac addysgu rhagorol bob amser.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, relationships and sexuality education, RSE, is mandatory for every learner aged three to 16, and, bizarrely, no Government opt-out is available for parents wishing to withdraw their children. That places an exceptional duty on your Government to ensure it is delivered consistently, sensitively and by properly trained staff. Yet Estyn's review found limited specialist development, lower staff confidence in teaching sensitive aspects of RSE and inconsistent local authority support, while schools remain responsible for designing their own RSE curriculum within the Government's mandatory code. If RSE is too important for parents to opt out, surely the Government cannot opt out of its duty. Estyn's findings represent a serious failure to fulfil that duty. The Government's failure to fulfil its duty to parents and children needs immediate rectification. As you cannot guarantee consistent provision, will you give responsibility back to parents to allow an opt-out, particularly for very young children?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, mae addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb yn orfodol i bob dysgwr o dair oed hyd 16 ac, yn rhyfedd, nid oes unrhyw ddewis i optio allan gan y Llywodraeth i rieni sy'n dymuno eithrio eu plant. Mae hynny'n rhoi dyletswydd neilltuol ar eich Llywodraeth chi i sicrhau ei bod yn cael ei darparu yn gyson, yn sensitif, a chan staff sydd wedi eu hyfforddi yn briodol. Ac eto roedd adolygiad Estyn yn canfod datblygiad arbenigol cyfyngedig, llai o hyder gan staff wrth ddysgu agweddau sensitif ar addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb a chefnogaeth anghyson oddi wrth yr awdurdodau lleol, pan fo'r ysgolion yn dal i fod yn gyfrifol am ddylunio eu cwricwlwm addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb yn unol â deddfwriaeth orfodol y Llywodraeth. Os yw addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb yn rhy bwysig i rieni allu eithrio eu plant, siawns na ddylai'r Llywodraeth esgeuluso ei dyletswydd. Mae canfyddiadau Estyn yn cynrychioli methiant difrifol o ran gwneud y ddyletswydd honno. Mae angen unioni methiant y Llywodraeth i gyflawni ei dyletswydd i rieni a phlant ar unwaith. Gan nad ydych chi'n gallu gwarantu darpariaeth gyson, a wnewch chi roi'r cyfrifoldeb yn ôl i rieni i ganiatáu eithrio plant, yn enwedig plant ifanc iawn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I think it's always important, where there are contentious issues or issues of concern to parents, that they are given reassurance at all times. The first thing to say is that whilst, yes, RSE is mandatory for three to 16-year-olds, it's not the same relationship and sexuality education for pupils from three to 16. RSE is legally required to be developmentally appropriate. That is the point—helping our children and young people through their lives, at the right time, to learn about the world around them, the relationships that they have with others. It must be factual. It must be pluralistic. It means that schools must present a range of views held in society, not push a particular view. These are the reassurances that are important for parents to hear, and the Government will always make sure that the information is available to them. If not, we'll up our game.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwyf i'n credu ei bod hi'n bwysig bob amser, pan fo materion dadleuol neu faterion sy'n peri pryder i rieni, eu bod nhw'n cael sicrwydd bob amser. Y peth cyntaf i'w ddweud, er bod addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb yn orfodol i rai rhwng tair a 16 oed, yw nad yr un yw'r addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb ar gyfer disgyblion o dair i 16 oed. Mae'n ofynnol i'r addysg cydberthynas a rhywioldeb fod yn briodol i bob cam datblygiad. Dyna'r pwynt—cynorthwyo ein plant a'n pobl ifanc trwy eu bywydau, ar yr adeg iawn, i ddysgu am y byd o'u cwmpas, y berthynas sydd ganddyn nhw ag eraill. Mae'n rhaid i hynny fod yn ffeithiol. Mae'n rhaid i hynny fod yn blwraliaethol. Mae'n golygu bod yn rhaid i ysgolion gyflwyno ystod o safbwyntiau sydd yn y gymdeithas, ac nid gwthio safbwynt arbennig. Dyma'r sicrwydd sy'n bwysig i rieni ei glywed, ac fe fydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau bob amser y bydd y wybodaeth ar gael iddyn nhw. Os nad yw, byddwn ni'n cymryd camau i wella hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Doeddwn i wir ddim yn disgwyl e. [Chwerthin.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae hwn yn wers. [Chwerthin.] Yn 2026-27, mi ydyn ni’n darparu £9.1 miliwn i Cefnogi Trydydd Sector Cymru, gan helpu sefydliadau i gael cyngor a chymorth ar wirfoddoli, llywodraethu, cyllid cynaliadwy ac ymgysylltu.

Mi fydd y sector gwirfoddol a gwirfoddolwyr eu hunain yn hanfodol i gyflawni blaenoriaethau’r Llywodraeth. Mi fydd hynny’n cynnwys gofal iechyd ataliol, mynd i’r afael â thlodi plant, darparu mynediad at ofal plant, darpariaeth chwarae, helpu pobl ifanc i gael gwaith. Mae'n rhestr hir.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
It's a lesson. [Laughter.] In 2026–27, we are providing £9.1 million to Third Sector Support Wales, helping organisations access support on volunteering, governance, sustainable funding and engagement.

The voluntary sector and volunteers themselves will be critical in delivering the Government's priorities. This will include preventative healthcare, tackling child poverty, providing access to childcare, play provision, supporting young people into work. It's a long list.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Pan oeddwn i'n gweithio yn y trydydd sector cyn dod fan hyn, roeddwn i'n ddigon ffodus i fod yn rhan o ymgynghoriadau ynglŷn â pholisi cymunedol gan y Building Communities Trust, ac mae'n rhaid i mi ddweud bod yr ymgynghori yna gyda'n cymunedau ni yn wych, ac roeddwn i'n teimlo fel fy mod i wir wedi cael cyfle i fewnbynnu i hynny. Ydych chi'n gallu jest cadarnhau y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn gwrando ar y mewnbwn pwysig yma y mae'r cymunedau wedi'i roi i'r ymgynghoriad yna, plîs?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. When I worked in the third sector before coming here, I was fortunate enough to be part of consultations on community policy by the Building Communities Trust, and I have to say that that consultation with our communities was excellent, and I felt that I'd really had an opportunity to have an input into that. Can you just confirm that the Welsh Government will listen to that important input that communities have provided to that consultation?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Dwi'n hapus iawn i gadarnhau hynny. Pan ydyn ni yn edrych ar draws ystod gwaith y Llywodraeth, rydyn ni'n edrych ar bartneriaeth. Dydy'r syniadau i gyd, dydy'r ddealltwriaeth i gyd, ddim yn dod o feinciau'r Llywodraeth ei hun; mae o'n dod o ymgysylltu efo eraill a gwrando ar beth sydd yn gweithio yn dda a beth sydd ddim, beth ydy'r rhwystredigaethau ac yn y blaen.

Pan fo'n dod at weithredu gwirfoddol, wel mae hynny'n cynnwys ein cymunedau ni i gyd, ac mae'n bwysig ein bod ni yn dangos ein bod ni bob amser yn Llywodraeth sydd yn gwrando. Dydy hynny ddim wastad yn golygu, wrth gwrs, gallu rhoi yn union beth mae pobl yn gofyn amdano fo, ond beth mae rhywun yn chwilio amdano fo ydy dealltwriaeth gan gymunedau—a thrwy hynny, sefydliadau gwirfoddol—am pam rydyn ni'n gwneud y penderfyniadau rydyn ni'n eu gwneud, a'u bod nhw wastad yn ceisio bod yn benderfyniadau sydd yn cefnogi gweithgarwch cymunedol ym mhob ffordd y gallwn ni ei wneud.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I am very happy to confirm that. When we look across the range of the Government's work, we're looking at partnership. All of the ideas and all of that understanding doesn't just come from the Government's benches; it comes from engaging with others and listening to what works well, what doesn't work well, and what the frustrations or barriers are and so on.

When it comes to voluntary action, that includes all of our communities, and it's important that we do show that we are always a Government that listens. That doesn't always, of course, mean being able to give people exactly what they're asking for, but what you're looking for is that understanding from communities—and through that, voluntary organisations—about why we make the decisions that we make, and that they are always intended to be decisions that support community engagement in every way that we can.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. We got through quite a few questions there. My apologies to those I wasn't able to call, but we got a lot of questions in there, so diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Fe aethom ni drwy gryn dipyn o gwestiynau yn y fan yno. Rwy'n ymddiheuro i'r rhai na fu modd i mi eu galw, ond fe gawsom ni lawer o gwestiynau yn y fan yna, felly diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Business Statement and Announcement
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Fe fyddwch chi'n gweld bod yna nifer o ddatganiadau wedi'u hychwanegu at agenda heddiw. Yn dilyn cais yn y Pwyllgor Busnes heddiw, mae datganiad y Prif Weinidog wedi'i ymestyn i 60 munud yn hytrach na'r 45 a nodwyd yn y lle cyntaf. Mae hefyd busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi'i nodi yn y datganiad busnes, sydd ar gael i'r holl Aelodau yn electronig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Llywydd. You will see that there are a number of statements that have been added to today's agenda. Following a request in the Business Committee today, the First Minister's statement has been extended to 60 minutes rather than the 45 previously stated. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available to all Members electronically.
