XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I gloi, Ddirprwy Lywydd, fe welais i'r potensial hwn fy hun yng nghynhadledd Cymdeithas Addysg Ryngwladol Ewrop yng Nglasgow wythnos diwethaf. Yno bues i'n cyfarfod â chynrychiolwyr ein holl brifysgolion, a chael trafodaethau cadarnhaol gyda nhw a chyda phartneriaid rhyngwladol sy'n awyddus i weithio gyda nhw. Fe glywais i hefyd sut y byddai ailymuno gydag Erasmus+ yn creu cyfleoedd newydd i fyfyrwyr, staff a sefydliadau ar gyfer astudio, hyfforddi, gweithio ac ymchwilio mewn gwledydd eraill.

Yn y bôn, nod yr adolygiad hwn yw sicrhau bod gennym system addysg uwch sy’n gadarn yn ariannol, sydd ag enw da yn rhyngwladol, sydd â gwreiddiau dwfn mewn cymunedau, sy’n cefnogi’r Gymraeg, ac sy’n medru helpu i adeiladu Cymru fwy ffyniannus. Rwy’n edrych ymlaen yn fawr at ddilyn cynnydd y panel a gweithio gyda’r sector ac ar draws y Senedd hon i lunio dyfodol cynaliadwy ar gyfer addysg uwch yng Nghymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
To close, Dirprwy Lywydd, I saw this potential myself at last week’s European Association for International Education conference in Glasgow. There I met representatives from all our universities, and I had productive meetings with them and with international partners who are eager to work with them. I also heard about how rejoining Erasmus+ will provide new opportunities to students, staff and institutions for international study, work placements, exchanges, training and research in other countries.

Fundamentally, the aim of this review is to ensure that we have a higher education system that is financially resilient, that is internationally respected, that is rooted in communities, that is supportive of the Welsh language, and that is capable of helping to build a more prosperous Wales. I look forward very much to following the panel's progress and working with the sector and across the Senedd to shape a sustainable future for higher education in Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I thank the Minister for the advance notice of today's statement, and I agree with the fundamental premise behind the review. We know that higher education in Wales at the moment is in an incredibly difficult position, and we all want to see it being in the best and strongest place it possibly can be. I declare an interest as somebody who has just finished a Master's degree from a Welsh educational institution, but I'm still awaiting award of the qualification so I can't quite use it for bragging rights just yet.

But one of the things that I found pertinent when speaking to some of my fellow students on the course is their perception around value for money when it comes to higher education at the moment. We know that tuition fees and student debt are incredible burdens for students going to university at the moment. My own level of student debt stands at just over £60,000 for an undergraduate and then a one-year Master's degree. I currently pay about £600 a month in student loan payments, and I'm one of the lucky ones, thanks to being in this job. But the average student who does graduate will work potentially for a decade—10 years or more—before they even begin to pay back more than just the interest on their student loans.

When it comes down to value for money for university graduates, that's one of the things that they consider when looking to go. When we look at the average earnings for university graduates after five years of graduating from their course, they were, in 2023-24, £31,500 for graduates from Welsh institutions. That compares to £33,000 from English institutions and £35,100 from Scottish ones. So, when we're asking the question about why should students choose universities in Wales, we also need to address the employability, the reward for that employment and the return on their investment into their education that they get when moving forward into Wales.

I'm glad that the review as well will consider the impact of AI as a crucial factor. I think that it's definitely contributing to the current graduate recruitment crisis that is ongoing across the UK, and it's clear to me that there needs to be at least some aspect of education in terms of AI in teaching our university students and our young people how to use it effectively, as it's likely going to be an embedded part of the modern economy for all graduates going forward.

I also think it's important that we look at how our university system can engage with technical education alongside. We know that there are certainly noises being made by the UK Government, and I think there is sentiment shared across the Chamber about the importance of technical education and education in trades and skills, and we should look at whether there is a part that our universities can play in bringing that technical education to bear for our young people.

Research and innovation is also an incredibly important aspect of our tertiary education system. We've seen the result of research and innovation. The AI craze that's going on in the economy at the moment has delivered incredible amounts of investment and value to the economy, and that's as a direct result of research undertaken by universities and recent graduates. So, I fundamentally support the objective of the review to see how we can strengthen our research and innovation in Wales.

I also welcome the overtures made within the review about strengthening the ties between employers and education, whether that is between the private sector and the public sector, and I hope that the review does take evidence from private sector employers in Wales to try and find out where the gaps may lie in between, why the entry-level jobs aren't existing and the opportunities don't exist in the same way as they have done in previous years when compared to the number of graduates.

Finally, I welcome the scope of the review, including colleges and degree apprenticeships, but I'd like to ask: will it also include fully remote university study? That’s something I'm noticing is an increasing trend—people who are studying their courses, whether it's undergraduate or postgraduate, fully remotely. And I note that the full report is due from the review from winter 2027-28, with the aim of measures being introduced for the start of the 2028-29 academic year. Given the funding deficit currently facing universities and the reduction in enrolment numbers, are there any actions planned or mechanisms in place to take shorter term actions if they are necessary? Because there will be some students who are either looking at starting university now or are currently involved in their courses who may be concerned about the future of their education given the funding shortfall, even though the review is not due to conclude for a couple of years yet. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ddiolch i'r Gweinidog am roi gwybod am y datganiad heddiw ymlaen llaw, ac rwy'n cytuno â'r gynsail sylfaenol y tu ôl i'r adolygiad. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod addysg uwch yng Nghymru mewn sefyllfa arbennig o anodd ar hyn o bryd, ac rydyn ni i gyd eisiau ei gweld yn y lle gorau a chryfaf y gall fod. Rwy'n datgan buddiant fel rhywun sydd newydd orffen gradd Meistr o sefydliad addysgol yng Nghymru, ond rwy'n dal i aros i'r cymhwyster gael ei ddyfarnu felly allaf i ddim brolio amdano eto.

Ond un o'r pethau a oedd yn berthnasol wrth siarad â rhai o fy nghyd-fyfyrwyr ar y cwrs yw eu canfyddiad o'r gwerth am arian y mae addysg uwch yn ei roi ar hyn o bryd. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod ffioedd dysgu a dyled myfyrwyr yn faich anhygoel ar fyfyrwyr sy'n mynd i'r brifysgol ar hyn o bryd. Mae gen i ddyled myfyrwyr o ychydig dros £60,000 ar gyfer gradd israddedig ac yna gradd Meistr flwyddyn o hyd. Ar hyn o bryd rwy'n talu tua £600 y mis mewn taliadau benthyciadau myfyrwyr, ac rwy'n un o'r rhai lwcus, diolch i'r ffaith fy mod i yn y swydd hon. Ond bydd y myfyriwr cyffredin sy'n graddio yn gweithio am ddegawd—10 mlynedd neu fwy—cyn iddyn nhw hyd yn oed dechrau talu mwy na dim ond y llog ar eu benthyciadau myfyrwyr.

O ran gwerth am arian i raddedigion prifysgol, dyna un o'r pethau maen nhw'n eu hystyried pan fyddan nhw'n meddwl am mynd. Pan edrychwn ni ar enillion cyfartalog graddedigion prifysgol bum mlynedd ar ôl iddyn nhw raddio o'u cwrs, roedden nhw, yn 2023-24, yn £31,500 ar gyfer graddedigion o sefydliadau yng Nghymru. Mae hynny'n cymharu â £33,000 o sefydliadau yn Lloegr a £35,100 o rai yn yr Alban. Felly, pan ydyn ni'n gofyn y cwestiwn pam ddylai myfyrwyr ddewis prifysgolion yng Nghymru, mae angen i ni hefyd fynd i'r afael â'r cyflogadwyedd, y wobr am y gyflogaeth honno a'r enillion maen nhw'n eu cael ar y buddsoddiad yn eu haddysg wrth symud ymlaen i Gymru.

Rwy'n falch hefyd y bydd yr adolygiad yn ystyried effaith AI fel ffactor hanfodol. Rwy'n credu ei fod yn bendant yn cyfrannu at yr argyfwng recriwtio graddedigion presennol sy'n cael ei weld ledled y DU, ac mae'n amlwg i mi fod angen o leiaf ryw agwedd ar addysg o ran AI wrth addysgu ein myfyrwyr prifysgol a'n pobl ifanc sut i'w ddefnyddio'n effeithiol, gan ei fod yn debygol o fod wedi'i ymwreiddio yn yr economi fodern i bob unigolyn graddedig yn y dyfodol.

Rwy'n credu hefyd ei bod yn bwysig ein bod ni'n edrych ar sut y gall ein system prifysgolion ymgysylltu â'r addysg dechnegol ochr yn ochr â hi. Rydyn ni gwybod bod sïon gan Lywodraeth y DU, ac rwy'n credu bod yr un teimladau'n cael eu rhannu ar draws y Siambr, am bwysigrwydd addysg dechnegol ac addysg mewn crefftau a sgiliau, a dylen ni edrych ar a oes rhan y gall ein prifysgolion ei chwarae wrth gyflwyno'r addysg dechnegol honno i'n pobl ifanc.

Mae ymchwil ac arloesi hefyd yn agwedd hynod bwysig ar ein system addysg drydyddol. Rydyn ni wedi gweld canlyniad ymchwil ac arloesi. Mae'r cyffro AI mawr sy'n digwydd yn yr economi ar hyn o bryd wedi rhoi symiau anhygoel o fuddsoddiad a gwerth i'r economi, ac mae hynny o ganlyniad uniongyrchol i ymchwil y mae prifysgolion a graddedigion diweddar wedi ymgymryd â hi. Felly, rwy'n cefnogi yn sylfaenol amcan yr adolygiad i weld sut y gallwn ni gryfhau ein hymchwil ac arloesi yng Nghymru.

Rwyf hefyd yn croesawu'r mynegiadau a wneir yn yr adolygiad ynghylch cryfhau'r cysylltiadau rhwng cyflogwyr ac addysg, boed hynny rhwng y sector preifat a'r sector cyhoeddus, ac rwy'n gobeithio y bydd yr adolygiad yn cymryd tystiolaeth gan gyflogwyr sector preifat yng Nghymru i geisio darganfod ble y gall y bylchau rhyngddynt nhw fod, pam nad oes swyddi lefel mynediad ar gael a pham nad oes cyfleoedd ar gael yn yr un ffordd ag y maen nhw wedi bod mewn blynyddoedd blaenorol o gymharu â nifer y graddedigion.

Yn olaf, rwy'n croesawu cwmpas yr adolygiad, gan gynnwys colegau a phrentisiaethau gradd, ond hoffwn i ofyn: a fydd hefyd yn cynnwys astudiaethau prifysgol o bell? Rwy'n sylwi bod hynny'n duedd gynyddol—pobl sy'n astudio eu cyrsiau, boed nhw'n rhai israddedig neu ôl-raddedig, yn gyfan gwbl o bell. Ac rwy'n nodi bod disgwyl i'r adroddiad llawn o'r adolygiad fod ar gael o aeaf 2027-28, gyda'r nod o gyflwyno mesurau ar gyfer dechrau blwyddyn academaidd 2028-29. O ystyried y diffyg cyllido sy'n wynebu prifysgolion ar hyn o bryd a'r gostyngiad yn y nifer sy'n cofrestru, a oes unrhyw gamau wedi'u cynllunio neu ddulliau ar waith i gymryd camau yn y tymor byrrach os bydd angen? Oherwydd bydd yna rai myfyrwyr sydd naill ai'n ystyried dechrau prifysgol nawr neu sy'n dilyn eu cyrsiau ar hyn o bryd a allai fod yn bryderus am ddyfodol eu haddysg o ystyried y diffyg cyllid, er nad oes disgwyl i'r adolygiad gael ei gwblhau am flwyddyn neu ddwy eto. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. There are so many different aspects there; I'll try to cover as many as I can.

Value for money and tuition fees. We recognise the importance of a fair and sustainable system of student support. I look at it in terms of three aspects, in many ways. The student fees are what keep our universities going. So they need those fees, unless we find other models of funding. There's also the aspect of making it fair for students as well, and you mentioned the burden of the debt that many young people carry. I should maybe also declare an interest. I have three children who went to university and are currently burdened with a huge amount of debt, which they will spend most of their working life repaying. And there are conversations going on amongst young people now as to whether it's worth them going to university or not. So, that is another aspect. And the third aspect, of course, is in terms of Welsh Government support. We want the benefits of that to be the best for Wales. So, when we look at those three aspects, it's a tightrope we have to walk in order to get that balance right.

You mentioned technical education. Now, I'm a firm believer in engaging with young people and educating them around the different pathways that are possible for them, not only the traditional work or university route, but there are other routes as well to further education, to work-based learning, apprenticeship schemes and so on. And in 2027, when we'll be introducing vocational certificates of secondary education as part of the Welsh curriculum, they will be exposed to opportunities to have vocational studies, which will engage a number of learners that are disengaged at the moment, and will open opportunities for them to maybe follow pathways that can lead to skills development and even apprenticeship degrees. I believe that our universities should look at providing more technical education. It's one of the interesting discussions I had with Professor Prendergast, because he is the chair of South East Technological University in Ireland. So I'm looking forward to him bringing his experience to bear on the work of the panel.

Research and innovation. We need to support our universities to have a greater share of that UK Research and Innovation funding. They currently only get about 2 per cent, whereas the Barnett consequential would be something around 5 per cent. So we need to support them to compete better for that funding.

And finally, you mentioned short-term actions. The panel will report back in about 18 months' time, but there will be a preliminary report in about six to nine months' time, especially around the financial support for students. Medr are keeping a close eye on what is going on in every university in Wales, and they feed that information back to me. So, if we need to step in and support, we will, but, at the moment, it's just a matter of monitoring the situation, keeping a close eye on what is happening and providing the best level of support we can. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Mae cymaint o wahanol agweddau yn y fan yna; fe wnaf i geisio trafod cymaint ohonyn nhw ag y gallaf.

Gwerth am arian a ffioedd dysgu. Rydyn ni'n cydnabod pwysigrwydd system cymorth myfyrwyr sy'n deg ac yn gynaliadwy. Rwy'n ei hystyried yn nhermau tair agwedd, mewn sawl ffordd. Y ffioedd myfyrwyr yw'r hyn sy'n cadw ein prifysgolion i fynd. Felly mae angen y ffioedd hynny arnyn nhw, oni bai ein bod ni'n dod o hyd i fodelau cyllido eraill. Mae yna hefyd yr agwedd o sicrhau ei bod yn deg i fyfyrwyr hefyd, ac fe wnaethoch chi sôn am faich y mae llawer o bobl ifanc yn ei ysgwyddo o ran dyled. Efallai y dylwn i ddatgan buddiant hefyd. Mae gen i dri phlentyn sydd wedi mynd i'r brifysgol ac sydd, ar hyn o bryd, yn ysgwyddo llawer iawn o ddyled, y byddan nhw'n treulio'r rhan fwyaf o'u bywyd gwaith yn ei had-dalu. Ac mae yna sgyrsiau yn digwydd ymhlith pobl ifanc nawr ynghylch a yw'n werth iddyn nhw fynd i'r brifysgol ai peidio. Felly, mae hynny'n agwedd arall. A'r drydedd agwedd, wrth gwrs, yw'r cymorth gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Rydyn ni eisiau i fanteision hynny fod y gorau i Gymru. Felly, pan edrychwn ni ar y tair agwedd yna, mae'n llwybr anodd y mae'n rhaid i ni gerdded er mwyn cael y cydbwysedd hwnnw'n iawn.

Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am addysg dechnegol. Nawr, rwy'n credu'n gryf mewn ymgysylltu â phobl ifanc a'u haddysgu am y gwahanol lwybrau sy'n bosibl iddyn nhw, nid yn unig y llwybr gwaith neu brifysgol traddodiadol, ond mae yna lwybrau eraill hefyd i addysg bellach, i ddysgu seiliedig ar waith, cynlluniau prentisiaeth ac yn y blaen. Ac yn 2027, pan fyddwn ni'n cyflwyno tystysgrifau addysg uwchradd galwedigaethol fel rhan o gwricwlwm Cymru, bydd yna gyfleoedd iddyn nhw ymgymryd ag astudiaethau galwedigaethol, a fydd yn ennyn diddordeb llawer o ddysgwyr sydd wedi'u hymddieithrio ar hyn o bryd, ac yn agor cyfleoedd efallai iddyn nhw ddilyn llwybrau a all arwain at ddatblygu sgiliau a hyd yn oed graddau prentisiaeth. Rwy'n credu y dylai ein prifysgolion ystyried darparu mwy o addysg dechnegol. Mae'n un o'r trafodaethau diddorol y ces i gyda'r Athro Prendergast, oherwydd ef yw cadeirydd Prifysgol Dechnolegol y De-ddwyrain yn Iwerddon. Felly rwy'n edrych ymlaen at y profiad y gall ei gyfrannu at waith y panel.

Ymchwil ac arloesi. Mae angen i ni gefnogi ein prifysgolion i gael cyfran uwch o'r cyllid hwnnw gan Ymchwil ac Arloesi y DU. Ar hyn o bryd dim ond tua 2 y cant maen nhw'n ei gael, er y byddai arian canlyniadol Barnett tua 5 y cant. Felly mae angen i ni eu cefnogi i gystadlu'n well am y cyllid hwnnw.

Ac yn olaf, fe sonioch chi am gamau gweithredu tymor byr. Bydd y panel yn adrodd yn ôl ymhen tua 18 mis, ond fe fydd yna adroddiad rhagarweiniol ymhen tua chwech i naw mis, yn enwedig ynghylch y cymorth ariannol i fyfyrwyr. Mae Medr yn cadw llygad agos ar yr hyn sy'n digwydd ym mhob prifysgol yng Nghymru, ac maen nhw'n rhoi'r wybodaeth honno i mi. Felly, os oes angen i ni gamu i mewn a chefnogi, fe wnawn ni, ond, ar hyn o bryd, mater o fonitro'r sefyllfa, cadw llygad agos ar yr hyn sy'n digwydd a darparu'r lefel orau o gefnogaeth y gallwn ni ydyw. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I refer Members to my register of interests and the fact that I am an adult learner at Cardiff and Vale College? I wanted to start—. Thank you for your statement, Deputy Minister. But I think it would be remiss of me to start this statement without asking about what I think is the elephant in the room here, which is: what about further education? When you came into Government, you and the Cabinet Minister said you would take a systemic approach to education, combining higher education and further education, and I think that is the right approach. It runs from early years right the way through people's life course.

However, what we have here is one part of the system hived off, and that is in sharp contrast to the approach taken by the previous Labour Government, where we issued a comprehensive call for evidence on tertiary education. So, I suppose my first question to you is: you are very well aware—I don't need to remind you—of the funding pressures in FE, the participation pressures in FE. You'll have heard from the chief executives and principals in recent months. I know, too, that you are very well aware that FE is where some of our most disadvantaged, most vulnerable learners are educated—the learners who are most likely to have their life chances inhibited by becoming not in education, employment or training. You've said in the statement that there are finite resources and there will have to be trade-offs. Given that this review just looks at higher education, how will you measure any potential trade-offs for FE? How will you consider the pressures on FE, and how will you consider the need to look after those learners?

The statement commits to looking at part-time learners, and I've asked you previously about part-time learners. The Diamond reforms have been a huge success in terms of the numbers of part-time learners studying at our universities. What assurance can you give that the review will protect the interests of part-time learners in higher education?

There's no mention of Seren in this statement today, and when you issued the statement in the summer announcing there would be a review of higher education, there was a reference to Seren. You said there would be a review of Academi Seren, and indeed it's picked up in the Cabinet Minister's action plan on literacy. You said that it would be about bringing together Reaching Wider and the Seren programme. Now, I know that you are very well aware that Reaching Wider is a different kind of programme to Seren. Reaching Wider is participation; Seren is about stretch. It's about ensuring that our most able learners can go to the very furthest point that they can go. It is the only thing that we do in Wales that benefits our more able and talented learners.

So, I'd like to ask you whether this review—and I welcome that there's an independent chair and that we're going to be kept updated—is going to look at the Seren programme as well, or whether that is going to be done separately. Is it your intention, as part of the review of Seren, to engage with Oxford and Cambridge? Because if young people are capable of going to some of the very best universities, not just in the UK, but anywhere in the world, then they should be encouraged to do that.

We on these benches have always viewed Seren as a learner-focused programme designed to ensure that our young people can be the very best that they can be. I want to offer you a gentle warning that we will fight very hard on these benches to protect that aspect of Seren, and I want to ask you whether it is your intention, as part of the work that you're doing on Seren, or as part of this review, to try in any way to discourage young people from studying, whether it's over the border or wherever they want to go, to achieve their education and be the very best that they can be.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf i gyfeirio Aelodau at fy nghofrestr buddiannau ac at y ffaith fy mod i'n oedolyn sy'n ddysgwr yng Ngholeg Caerdydd a'r Fro? Roeddwn i eisiau dechrau—. Diolch am eich datganiad, Ddirprwy Weinidog. Ond dydw i ddim yn credu y byddai'n iawn i mi ddechrau'r datganiad hwn heb ofyn am yr eliffant yn yr ystafell, yn fy marn i, sef: beth am addysg bellach? Pan ddaethoch chi i mewn i'r Llywodraeth, fe wnaethoch chi a'r Gweinidog Cabinet ddweud y byddech chi'n cymryd agwedd systemig at addysg, gan gyfuno addysg uwch ac addysg bellach, ac rwy'n credu mai dyna'r dull cywir. Mae'n mynd o'r blynyddoedd cynnar yr holl ffordd trwy fywyd pobl.

Fodd bynnag, yr hyn sydd gennym ni yma yw un rhan o'r system wedi'i gwahanu, ac mae hynny'n wahanol iawn i'r dull a fabwysiadwyd gan y Llywodraeth Lafur flaenorol, lle gwnaethon ni gyhoeddi galwad gynhwysfawr am dystiolaeth ar addysg drydyddol. Felly, mae'n debyg mai fy nghwestiwn cyntaf i chi yw: rydych chi'n ymwybodol iawn—does dim angen i mi eich atgoffa—o'r pwysau cyllido ar AB, y pwysau cyfranogi ar AB. Byddwch chi wedi clywed gan y prif weithredwyr a'r penaethiaid yn ystod y misoedd diwethaf. Rwy'n gwybod, hefyd, eich bod chi'n ymwybodol iawn mai AB yw lle mae rhai o'n dysgwyr mwyaf difreintiedig, mwyaf agored i niwed yn cael eu haddysgu—y dysgwyr sydd fwyaf tebygol o gael eu cyfleoedd bywyd wedi'u hatal trwy beidio â bod mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant. Rydych chi wedi dweud yn y datganiad bod adnoddau yn gyfyngedig ac y bydd angen cyfaddawdau. O ystyried bod yr adolygiad hwn yn edrych ar addysg uwch yn unig, sut y byddwch chi'n mesur unrhyw gyfaddawdau posibl ar gyfer AB? Sut y byddwch chi'n ystyried y pwysau ar AB, a sut y byddwch chi'n ystyried yr angen i ofalu am y dysgwyr hynny?

Mae'r datganiad yn ymrwymo i ystyried dysgwyr rhan-amser, ac rwyf wedi gofyn i chi o'r blaen am ddysgwyr rhan-amser. Mae diwygiadau Diamond wedi bod yn llwyddiant ysgubol o ran nifer y dysgwyr rhan-amser sy'n astudio yn ein prifysgolion. Pa sicrwydd allwch chi ei roi y bydd yr adolygiad yn amddiffyn buddiannau dysgwyr rhan-amser mewn addysg uwch?

Does dim sôn am Seren yn y datganiad hwn heddiw, a phan wnaethoch chi gyhoeddi'r datganiad yn yr haf a oedd yn nodi y byddai adolygiad o addysg uwch, roedd yna gyfeiriad at Seren. Fe wnaethoch chi ddweud y byddai adolygiad o Academi Seren, ac yn wir mae'n cael ei nodi yng nghynllun gweithredu'r Gweinidog Cabinet ar lythrennedd. Fe wnaethoch chi ddweud y byddai'n ymwneud â dod ag Ymestyn yn Ehangach a rhaglen Seren at ei gilydd. Nawr, rwy'n gwybod eich bod chi'n ymwybodol iawn bod Ymestyn yn Ehangach yn fath gwahanol o raglen i Seren. Mae Ymestyn yn Ehangach yn ymwneud â chyfranogi; mae Seren yn ymwneud ag ymestyn. Mae'n ymwneud â sicrhau bod ein dysgwyr mwyaf abl yn gallu mynd i'r pwynt pellaf y gallan nhw fynd. Dyma'r unig beth rydyn ni'n ei wneud yng Nghymru sydd o fudd i'n dysgwyr mwy abl a thalentog.

Felly, hoffwn ofyn i chi a yw'r adolygiad hwn—ac rwy'n croesawu bod yna gadeirydd annibynnol a'n bod ni'n mynd i gael y newyddion diweddaraf—yn mynd i fod yn edrych ar raglen Seren hefyd, neu a yw hynny'n mynd i gael ei wneud ar wahân. A yw'n fwriad gennych, fel rhan o'r adolygiad o Seren, i ymgysylltu â Rhydychen a Chaergrawnt? Oherwydd os yw pobl ifanc yn gallu mynd i rai o'r prifysgolion gorau, nid yn unig yn y DU, ond unrhyw le yn y byd, yna dylen nhw gael eu hannog i wneud hynny.

Rydyn ni, ar y meinciau hyn, bob amser wedi gweld Seren fel rhaglen sy'n canolbwyntio ar ddysgwyr sydd wedi'i chynllunio i sicrhau bod ein pobl ifanc yn gallu bod y gorau y gallan nhw fod. Hoffwn i gynnig rhybudd ysgafn i chi y byddwn ni'n ymladd yn galed iawn ar y meinciau hyn i amddiffyn yr agwedd honno ar Seren, ac rwyf eisiau gofyn i chi a yw'n fwriad gennych, fel rhan o'r gwaith rydych chi'n ei wneud ar Seren, neu fel rhan o'r adolygiad hwn, i geisio mewn unrhyw ffordd i atal pobl ifanc rhag astudio, p’un a yw hynny dros y ffin neu ble bynnag maen nhw eisiau mynd, i gyflawni eu haddysg ac i fod y gorau y gallan nhw fod.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Thank you, Lynne. A number of important points. I'll start off with your first point around the pressures on FE colleges. We absolutely recognise that there are pressures, as there were last year, which is why Medr allocated an additional £6.25 million in this financial year to support those pressures.

In discussions I've had with Medr and ColegauCymru with regard to this academic term, we are seeing the pressures again in terms of increased enrolments, especially around levels 1 and 2. So, we will be considering the situation and making a decision around about November, when numbers will have settled down. We understand that funding pressures are acute on one or two FE colleges, but those discussions are ongoing.

We want to support the FE colleges as best as we can, because, for the reasons you outlined, they do provide opportunities for those young people, especially those at risk of becoming NEET, and we are acutely aware that we can't allow them to fall through the net in any way by not supporting them. So, we will take a considered view when we know the final numbers closer to November. But in terms of your wider point, we are well aware of the financial challenges.

Part-time learners: absolutely, the review will look at this. I believe in lifelong learning as being an opportunity for people to upskill, reskill, and to re-engage with education at any time in their life, and that can be done through part-time provision or through apprenticeship schemes or in-work provision through the trade union movement as well.

Seren: I'm hoping to make an announcement soon about Seren. You're right, I did say back on 11 June, I think it was, when I made a statement, that we are hoping to bring together the strongest elements of Academi Seren and also the Reaching Wider programme. And you're absolutely right to say that they are two different programmes. Academi Seren provides the stretch for the most able and talented pupils and we want to keep that, obviously, because we need to stretch our most academically gifted young people. And it's not a matter of discouraging them from studying wherever they choose. I would just want to flip that on its head: what we want to do as a Welsh Government is to encourage them to stay in Wales and to support our universities here. But it's not about discouragement at all, it's about encouraging them to stay, which is slightly different to what you were possibly alluding to.

The Reaching Wider programme is important as well, because it targets young people from disadvantaged communities, and you know and others know that the number of young people from disadvantaged communities going to universities is lower in Wales than in any of the other home nations. So, we want to encourage, through a cohesive programme, that to happen as well. So, I think that answers the main points, Lynne, and I'd be happy to have a conversation with you about any of these, moving forward. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Diolch, Lynne. Nifer o bwyntiau pwysig. Fe wnaf i ddechrau gyda'ch pwynt cyntaf ynghylch y pwysau ar golegau AB. Rydyn ni'n cydnabod yn llwyr bod yna bwysau, fel yr oedd y llynedd, a dyna pam y dyrannodd Medr £6.25 miliwn ychwanegol yn y flwyddyn ariannol hon i gefnogi'r pwysau hynny.

Mewn trafodaethau rwyf wedi eu cael gyda Medr a ColegauCymru o ran y tymor academaidd hwn, rydyn ni'n gweld y pwysau eto o ran mwy o bobl yn cofrestru, yn enwedig o gwmpas lefelau 1 a 2. Felly, byddwn ni'n ystyried y sefyllfa ac yn gwneud penderfyniad tua mis Tachwedd, pan fydd y niferoedd wedi setlo. Rydyn ni'n deall bod y pwysau cyllido ar un neu ddau o golegau AB yn acíwt, ond mae'r trafodaethau hynny'n parhau.

Rydyn ni eisiau cefnogi'r colegau AB cystal ag y gallwn ni, oherwydd, am y rhesymau y gwnaethoch chi eu hamlinellu, maen nhw yn rhoi cyfleoedd i'r bobl ifanc hynny, yn enwedig y rhai sydd mewn perygl o fod yn NEET, ac rydyn ni'n ymwybodol iawn na allwn ni ganiatáu iddyn nhw syrthio drwy'r rhwyd mewn unrhyw ffordd trwy beidio â'u cefnogi. Felly, byddwn ni'n dod i farn ystyriol pan fyddwn ni'n gwybod y niferoedd terfynol yn agosach at fis Tachwedd. Ond o ran eich pwynt ehangach, rydyn ni'n ymwybodol iawn o'r heriau ariannol.

Dysgwyr rhan-amser: yn bendant, bydd yr adolygiad yn edrych ar hyn. Rwy'n credu mewn dysgu gydol oes fel cyfle i bobl uwchsgilio, ailsgilio, ac ailymgysylltu ag addysg ar unrhyw adeg yn eu bywyd, ac mae'n bosibl gwneud hynny trwy ddarpariaeth ran-amser neu drwy gynlluniau prentisiaeth neu ddarpariaeth mewn gwaith trwy'r mudiad undebau llafur hefyd.

Seren: rwy'n gobeithio gwneud cyhoeddiad cyn bo hir am Seren. Rydych chi'n iawn, fe wnes i ddweud, nôl ar 11 Mehefin, rwy'n credu, pan wnes i ddatganiad, ein bod ni'n gobeithio dod ag elfennau cryfaf Academi Seren a hefyd raglen Ymestyn yn Ehangach ynghyd. Ac rydych chi'n hollol gywir i ddweud eu bod nhw'n ddwy raglen wahanol. Mae Academi Seren yn darparu'r ymestyniad i'r disgyblion mwyaf abl a thalentog ac rydyn ni eisiau cadw hynny, yn amlwg, oherwydd mae angen i ni ymestyn ein pobl ifanc fwyaf dawnus yn academaidd. A dydy e ddim yn fater o'u hatal nhw rhag astudio ble bynnag y mynnant. Hoffwn i droi hynny ar ei ben: yr hyn rydyn ni eisiau ei wneud fel Llywodraeth Cymru yw eu hannog i aros yng Nghymru a chefnogi ein prifysgolion yma. Ond dydy e ddim yn ymwneud â gwrthanogaeth o gwbl, mae'n ymwneud â'u hannog i aros, sydd ychydig yn wahanol i'r hyn yr oeddech chi'n cyfeirio ato o bosibl.

Mae rhaglen Ymestyn yn Ehangach yn bwysig hefyd, oherwydd mae'n targedu pobl ifanc o gymunedau difreintiedig, ac rydych chi'n gwybod ac mae eraill yn gwybod bod nifer y bobl ifanc o gymunedau difreintiedig sy'n mynd i brifysgolion yn is yng Nghymru nag yn unrhyw un o'r gwledydd cartref eraill. Felly, rydyn ni eisiau annog hynny i ddigwydd hefyd trwy raglen gydlynol. Felly, rwy'n credu bod hynny'n ateb y prif bwyntiau, Lynne, a byddwn i’n hapus i gael sgwrs gyda chi am unrhyw un o'r rhain, wrth symud ymlaen. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Apologies for my slight lapse in concentration, things seem to be more lively outside the Chamber today than they have been, perhaps, inside it.

Thank you, Cabinet Minister, for your statement. Tertiary education is, of course, crucial in developing the skills and knowledge that our economy needs now and in the future, and the stakes for the higher education review could hardly be higher at this stage. And the many external reviews of Welsh higher education over recent decades, in my view, have failed to secure the long-term sustainability of the sector and have instead contributed to a cycle of managed decline.

But on this review specifically, you'll be aware, Cabinet Minister, that in Scotland when Ministers have sought to work with universities to develop solutions and secure their commitments to change, before holding them to account for delivery, there's been that close working relationship with those universities. So, I wonder how you will ensure and give assurances to our universities here in Wales that you'll be adopting a similar approach, working seriously with those universities as partners in developing and implementing these reforms, of course within the context of the independent panel that you're seeking to or you will be setting up.

There's already been mention of the central role that universities play in our economy and our growth in the future. We welcome the review's commitment to look at the role that alternative pathways, such as colleges and degree apprenticeships, should play in a wider education landscape. Of course, colleges can provide flexible modes of delivery and be more accessible to learners, and we know the increasing importance of a degree apprenticeship. So, will you direct the review to look specifically at what barriers there are in Wales to prevent our young people from accessing some of those alternative pathways that colleagues have already mentioned, those alternative pathways to higher education.

Within that context of economic growth, universities are important engines of place-based economic growth as well, not just the institution on its own. There are great examples of universities working closely in partnership with colleges and local industry to respond to the skills that are needed. Now, FE is not covered in the review, so how will you make sure there's a joined-up approach to meeting place-based skills requirements and opportunities across the tertiary systems? I appreciate that HE does need to be reviewed, but the context of their place is really important, particularly in a place like Wales.

Deputy Minister, in your terms of reference, you state that the scale and urgency of pressures on universities mean that the underlying funding sustainability of Welsh universities and the Welsh student support system must now be addressed. There's a real sense of urgency in your statements there, but the timeline that you're looking at is looking to make changes in the 2028-29 academic year. That's two years away. It doesn't really feel that urgent, quite frankly. Welsh students starting university in September will be entering the final year of their courses by the time any changes come in. Could you confirm whether you think that a two-year wait for this reform is acceptable to students, universities and businesses under pressure right now?

I just want to follow up on a comment that my colleague Lynne Neagle raised as well, Minister, in relation to this ambition of students seeking an education where it's best for them. Wales is already home to world-class universities. For many students, though, looking elsewhere in the UK or abroad is simply what's best for them and their future pathway. That should be a choice that is equally available to them. Higher education should allow our students to aspire to become the best that they can be, to be supported. They don't want to feel hemmed in by Wales-specific Government support or not. So, will you, on the floor of the Senedd today, commit to not holding back those Welsh student aspirations to study wherever is best for them? Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Ymddiheuriadau bod fy meddwl wedi crwydro am ennyd, mae'n ymddangos bod pethau'n fwy bywiog y tu allan i'r Siambr heddiw nag y maen nhw wedi bod y tu mewn iddi, efallai.

Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet, am eich datganiad. Mae addysg drydyddol, wrth gwrs, yn hanfodol wrth ddatblygu'r sgiliau a'r wybodaeth sydd eu hangen ar ein heconomi nawr ac yn y dyfodol, ac ni allai'r fantol fod yn fwy ar gyfer yr adolygiad o addysg uwch ar hyn o bryd. Ac, yn fy marn i, mae'r adolygiadau allanol niferus o addysg uwch yng Nghymru dros y degawdau diwethaf wedi methu â sicrhau cynaliadwyedd hirdymor y sector, ac yn hytrach wedi cyfrannu at gylch o ddirywiad wedi'i reoli.

Ond o ran yr adolygiad hwn yn benodol, fe fyddwch chi'n ymwybodol, Weinidog Cabinet, yn yr Alban pan fydd Gweinidogion wedi ceisio gweithio gyda phrifysgolion i ddatblygu atebion a sicrhau eu hymrwymiadau i newid, cyn eu dwyn i gyfrif am gyflawni, mae'r berthynas waith agos honno wedi bod gyda'r prifysgolion hynny. Felly, tybed sut y byddwch chi'n sicrhau, ac yn rhoi sicrwydd i'n prifysgolion ni yma yng Nghymru, y byddwch chi'n mabwysiadu dull tebyg, gan weithio o ddifrif gyda'r prifysgolion hynny fel partneriaid wrth ddatblygu a gweithredu'r diwygiadau hyn, wrth gwrs yng nghyd-destun y panel annibynnol rydych chi'n ceisio'i sefydlu, neu y byddwch chi'n ei sefydlu.

Mae sôn wedi bod eisoes am y rôl ganolog y mae prifysgolion yn ei chwarae yn ein heconomi a'n twf yn y dyfodol. Rydyn ni'n croesawu ymrwymiad yr adolygiad i edrych ar y rôl y dylai llwybrau eraill, fel colegau a phrentisiaethau gradd, ei chwarae mewn tirwedd addysg ehangach. Wrth gwrs, gall colegau ddarparu dulliau hyblyg o gyflwyno a bod yn fwy hygyrch i ddysgwyr, ac rydyn ni'n gwybod am bwysigrwydd cynyddol prentisiaeth gradd. Felly, a wnewch chi gyfarwyddo'r adolygiad i edrych yn benodol ar y rhwystrau yng Nghymru sy'n atal ein pobl ifanc rhag cael mynediad at rai o'r llwybrau eraill hynny y mae cyd-Aelodau eisoes wedi sôn amdanyn nhw, y llwybrau eraill hynny i addysg uwch.

Yng nghyd-destun y twf economaidd hwnnw, mae prifysgolion yn ysgogwyr pwysig o ran twf economaidd sy'n seiliedig ar le hefyd, nid dim ond y sefydliad ar ei ben ei hun. Mae yna enghreifftiau gwych o brifysgolion yn gweithio'n agos mewn partneriaeth â cholegau a diwydiant lleol i ymateb i'r sgiliau sydd eu hangen. Nawr, dydy AB ddim yn cael ei chynnwys yn yr adolygiad, felly sut fyddwch chi'n sicrhau bod yna ddull cydgysylltiedig o fodloni gofynion a chyfleoedd sgiliau sy'n seiliedig ar le ar draws y systemau trydyddol? Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi bod angen adolygu AU, ond mae cyd-destun eu lle yn bwysig iawn, yn enwedig mewn lle fel Cymru.

Ddirprwy Weinidog, yn eich cylch gwaith, rydych chi'n nodi bod maint y pwysau ar brifysgolion a'r ffaith bod angen mynd i'r afael â hyn ar frys yn golygu bod yn rhaid nawr ymdrin â chynaliadwyedd cyllido sylfaenol prifysgolion yng Nghymru a'r system cymorth myfyrwyr yng Nghymru. Mae yna ymdeimlad gwirioneddol yn eich datganiadau yn y fan yna bod angen gweithredu ar frys, ond mae'r amserlen rydych chi'n ei hystyried yn disgwyl gwneud newidiadau ym mlwyddyn academaidd 2028-29. Mae hynny ymhen dwy flynedd. Dydy e ddim yn teimlo bod cymaint â hynny o frys, a bod yn onest. Bydd myfyrwyr o Gymru sy'n dechrau prifysgol ym mis Medi yn mynd i mewn i flwyddyn olaf eu cyrsiau erbyn i unrhyw newidiadau gael eu cyflwyno. Allech chi gadarnhau a ydych o'r farn bod aros dwy flynedd am y diwygio hyn yn dderbyniol i fyfyrwyr, prifysgolion a busnesau sydd dan bwysau ar hyn o bryd?

Rwyf am ddweud mwy am sylw a gafodd ei godi gan fy nghyd-Aelod Lynne Neagle hefyd, Weinidog, o ran yr uchelgais hon bod myfyrwyr yn chwilio am addysg yn y lle sydd orau iddyn nhw. Mae Cymru eisoes yn gartref i brifysgolion o'r radd flaenaf. Fodd bynnag, i lawer o fyfyrwyr, chwilio mewn mannau eraill yn y DU neu dramor yw'r hyn sydd orau iddyn nhw ac i'w llwybr yn y dyfodol. Dylai hynny fod yn ddewis sydd ar gael iddyn nhw yn yr un modd. Dylai addysg uwch ganiatáu i'n myfyrwyr anelu at fod y gorau y gallan nhw fod, i gael eu cefnogi. Dydyn nhw ddim eisiau teimlo eu bod yn cael eu cyfyngu gan gymorth y Llywodraeth sy'n benodol i Gymru ai peidio. Felly, a wnewch chi, ar lawr y Senedd heddiw, ymrwymo i beidio â rhwystro dyheadau myfyrwyr o Gymru i astudio lle bynnag sydd orau iddyn nhw? Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Sam. Thank you. A number of points and I'll deal with them as you presented them. The first one, working with the university sector: since coming into post, I think I have had more meetings with the university sector than most sectors. I've met with all the vice-chancellors on more than one occasion. I've also had more than one meeting with the chairs of the universities as well, as well as Universities Wales as the umbrella body. In Scotland last week, in the international education conference that I attended, there was a stand where all the universities of Wales were present. I spoke to every one of them about the strengths they had and the offer they could give to students, not only in the United Kingdom but across the whole of the world. So, I'm in constant touch with every one of our university partners.

In terms of the economy and developing skills, skills is the bedrock of growing the economy. If we want a thriving, prosperous economy, if we want to meet the ambitions of this Welsh Government to increase productivity as well, skills is at the heart of that. It's why we are conducting a skills audit at present. The skills audit will end, in terms of inviting people to present evidence, at the end of this month, and hopefully the report will be published around about March or April of next year. That will inform employers, universities, FE colleges and work-based learning providers about emerging sectors, where we think the priorities in terms of skills growth are going to be in the future. Because we know that sectors like AI, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors and green energy are moving rapidly, so we need to recognise the skills pipeline that we need to meet those job opportunities coming down the line.

In terms of that skills development, we are holding a skills summit on 8 October in the Swansea.com Stadium. We’re hoping to get between 150 and 170 representatives from universities, FE and, crucially, employers as well. As it happens, this afternoon I had a meeting with organisations representing the biggest employers in Wales. I had an opportunity to tell them about this skills audit. I told them that their role in developing the Welsh economy with the Welsh Government, with HE, with FE, with apprenticeship providers, is absolutely crucial, and they were on board with that message.

On the final point you made, similar to Lynne, about curtailing choice, there's absolutely no intention to curtail choice. But it's incumbent on a Welsh Government to support our Welsh universities. What we want to do is to strengthen the offer that our Welsh universities are providing so that they can get more students from Wales and from the UK to come here to Wales to study and, potentially, to work as well. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Sam. Diolch. Nifer o bwyntiau, ac fe wnaf i ymdrin â nhw fel y gwnaethoch chi eu cyflwyno nhw. Yr un cyntaf, gweithio gyda sector y prifysgolion: ers dod i'r swydd, rwy'n credu fy mod i wedi cael mwy o gyfarfodydd gyda'r sector prifysgolion na'r rhan fwyaf o sectorau. Rwyf i wedi cwrdd â phob is-ganghellor ar fwy nag un achlysur. Rwyf i hefyd wedi cael mwy nag un cyfarfod gyda chadeiryddion y prifysgolion hefyd, yn ogystal â Phrifysgolion Cymru fel y corff ymbarél. Yn yr Alban yr wythnos diwethaf, yn y gynhadledd addysg ryngwladol yr oeddwn i'n bresennol ynddi, roedd stondin lle roedd holl brifysgolion Cymru yn bresennol. Siaradais i â phob un ohonyn nhw am y cryfderau oedd ganddyn nhw a'r cynnig y gallen nhw ei roi i fyfyrwyr, nid yn unig yn y Deyrnas Unedig ond ar draws y byd i gyd. Felly, rydw i'n cysylltu'n gyson â phob un o'n partneriaid prifysgolion.

O ran yr economi a datblygu sgiliau, sgiliau yw sylfaen tyfu'r economi. Os ydyn ni eisiau economi lewyrchus, ffyniannus, os ydyn ni eisiau cyflawni uchelgeisiau Llywodraeth Cymru i gynyddu cynhyrchiant hefyd, mae sgiliau wrth wraidd hynny. Dyna pam ein bod ni'n cynnal archwiliad sgiliau ar hyn o bryd. Bydd yr archwiliad sgiliau yn dod i ben, o ran gwahodd pobl i gyflwyno tystiolaeth, ddiwedd y mis hwn, a gobeithio y bydd yr adroddiad yn cael ei gyhoeddi tua mis Mawrth neu Ebrill y flwyddyn nesaf. Bydd hynny'n rhoi gwybod i gyflogwyr, prifysgolion, colegau AB a darparwyr dysgu seiliedig ar waith am sectorau sy'n datblygu, lle y credwn y bydd y blaenoriaethau o ran twf sgiliau yn y dyfodol. Oherwydd rydyn ni'n gwybod bod sectorau fel AI, gweithgynhyrchu uwch, lled-ddargludyddion ac ynni gwyrdd yn symud yn gyflym, felly mae angen i ni gydnabod y llif sgiliau sydd ei angen arnon ni i fodloni'r cyfleoedd am swyddi hynny sydd yn yr arfaeth.

O ran y datblygiad sgiliau hwnnw, rydyn ni'n cynnal uwchgynhadledd sgiliau ar 8 Hydref yn Stadiwm Swansea.com. Rydyn ni'n gobeithio cael rhwng 150 a 170 o gynrychiolwyr o brifysgolion, AB ac, yn hollbwysig, cyflogwyr hefyd. Fel mae'n digwydd, y prynhawn yma cefais i  gyfarfod gyda sefydliadau sy'n cynrychioli'r cyflogwyr mwyaf yng Nghymru. Cefais gyfle i ddweud wrthyn nhw am yr archwiliad sgiliau hwn. Dywedais wrthyn nhw fod eu rôl yn datblygu economi Cymru gyda Llywodraeth Cymru, gydag AU, gydag AB, gyda darparwyr prentisiaethau, yn hollbwysig, ac roedden nhw'n cytuno â'r neges honno.

Ar y pwynt olaf y gwnaethoch chi, yn debyg i Lynne, ynglŷn â chyfyngu ar ddewis, does dim bwriad o gwbl i gyfyngu ar ddewis. Ond mae'n ddyletswydd ar Lywodraeth Cymru i gefnogi ein prifysgolion ni yng Nghymru. Yr hyn yr ydyn ni eisiau'i wneud yw cryfhau'r cynnig y mae ein prifysgolion yng Nghymru yn ei ddarparu fel y gallan nhw gael mwy o fyfyrwyr o Gymru ac o'r DU i ddod yma i Gymru i astudio ac, o bosibl, i weithio hefyd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'd also like to refer you to my register of interests, please. Until May, I used to work at a university in Wales, and I still have family members who work in the HE sector in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Hoffwn i eich cyfeirio at fy nghofrestr buddiannau, os gwelwch yn dda. Tan fis Mai, roeddwn i'n arfer gweithio mewn prifysgol yng Nghymru, ac mae gennyf i aelodau o'r teulu sy'n gweithio yn y sector AU yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Weinidog, daw’r adolygiad hwn ar adeg hollbwysig i addysg uwch yng Nghymru. Mae cylch gorchwyl yr adolygiad yn gyffrous ac yn rhoi cyfle i ni feddwl yn feiddgar ac yn greadigol am sut rydyn ni am i addysg uwch weithredu ac, yn y pen draw, gyflawni ar gyfer Cymru.

Un o'r materion rydyn ni wedi'u hwynebu ers peth amser bellach yw cyflogadwyedd graddedigion ac, yn benodol, sut rydym yn sicrhau bod y sgiliau a'r cyfleoedd sydd yn cael eu datblygu drwy ein system addysg uwch yn arwain at yrfaoedd llwyddiannus yng Nghymru. Rwy'n credu bydd yr adolygiad hwn yn dwyn yr agweddau hynny ynghyd.

Yn aml, mae busnesau bach a chanolig yn wynebu mwy o heriau o ran denu a recriwtio talent graddedig. Sut mae'r Gweinidog yn gweld yr adolygiad yn ein helpu ni i gysylltu ein graddedigion yn well ag anghenion a chyfleoedd busnesau Cymru, yn enwedig busnesau bach a chanolig, fel y gallwn gadw mwy o dalent graddedig yma yng Nghymru, tra hefyd yn cefnogi twf ein heconomi? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Minister, this review comes at a vital time for higher education in Wales. The remit of the review is exciting and provides an opportunity to think boldly and creatively about how we want higher education to operate and, ultimately, deliver for Wales.

One of the issues that we have faced for some time now is the employability of graduates and, specifically, how we ensure that the skills and opportunities that are developed through our higher education system lead to successful careers in Wales. I believe that this review will bring those aspects together.

Often, SMEs face more challenges in terms of attracting and recruiting graduate talent. How does the Minister see the review helping us to better connect our graduates with the needs and opportunities of Welsh businesses, particularly SMEs, so that we can retain more graduate talent here in Wales, while also supporting the growth of our economy? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn, Sera. Mae rôl busnesau bach yn gwbl hanfodol. Rwy'n credu bod rhyw 95 y cant o holl fusnesau Cymru yn fusnesau bach a chanolig. A digwydd bod, yn y cyfarfod ges i gyda chynrychiolwyr o gyflogwyr mwyaf Cymru yn gynharach y prynhawn yma, roedd hwn yn fater oedd wedi codi: sut y gall yr arolwg yma a'n prifysgolion a cholegau gefnogi SMEs drwy gynnig gwaith i raddedigion a phobl sydd wedi cymhwyso mewn ffordd wahanol i raddau. Yn glir i fi, mae, er enghraifft, y syniad o sefydlu corff datblygu fel y WDA newydd—y corff datblygu economaidd newydd yma—yn mynd i roi cefnogaeth i fusnesau bach a chanolig i dyfu, a phan maen nhw'n cael y cyfle i dyfu, maen nhw'n edrych i gyflogi mwy o bobl. Dyna lle mae'r cyfle wedyn i raddedigion i gael cyfle am waith. Ond y peth pwysig, dwi'n meddwl, yw gwneud y cysylltiad rhwng cyflogwyr a phrifysgolion yn arbennig, i wneud yn siŵr eu bod nhw'n deall beth yw'r angen o ran pa sgiliau sydd eisiau ar gyfer y dyfodol, a'u bod nhw'n deall wedyn ar lefel ranbarthol pa gyfleoedd sydd gan bobl i fynd i swyddi yn yr ardal arbennig yna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Sera. The role of SMEs and small businesses is entirely crucial. I think around 95 per cent of all businesses in Wales are small and medium-sized enterprises. As it happens, in the meeting that I had with representatives from Wales's largest employers earlier this afternoon, this was an issue that was raised: how can this review, and how can our universities and colleges support SMEs by providing employment for graduates and those who have qualified in other ways too. What was clear to me was that, for example, the idea of establishing a development body such as a new WDA here in Wales will provide support for SMEs to grow, and when they have that opportunity to grow, they will look to employ more people. That's where the opportunity arises for graduates to access work. But I think the important thing is to make that link between employers and universities in particular to ensure that they understand what the needs are in terms of future skills, and that they then understand at a regional level what opportunities are available for people to access employment in that particular area.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'd like to thank the Deputy Minister for sight of his statement. Deputy Minister, you quite correctly referred to prosperity a few times in the economy, and indeed there's a lot of evidence that the success of the economy is linked to education. We've had well-rehearsed arguments about PISA results at secondary level, but at a higher education level, I'll point to some evidence from around the world. We know that, for example, in terms of the top 100 universities, we have between nine and 14 from England, two in Scotland, with one just outside of the top 100, but alas none in Wales, and none close to being in the top 100 in Wales. Our top university comes in just above 200. Professor Prendergast has successfully run a top 100 university in Ireland, and I'm wondering whether you'd be prepared to ask this group to look at a strategy for creating a top 100 university in Wales, because we should have a top 100 university in Wales, and we need a top 100 university in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Hoffwn i ddiolch i'r Dirprwy Weinidog am gael gweld ei ddatganiad. Ddirprwy Weinidog, fe wnaethoch chi gyfeirio'n gywir at ffyniant sawl gwaith yn yr economi, ac yn wir mae yna lawer o dystiolaeth bod llwyddiant yr economi yn gysylltiedig ag addysg. Rydyn ni wedi dadlau droeon am ganlyniadau PISA ar lefel uwchradd, ond ar lefel addysg uwch, fe wnaf i dynnu sylw at rywfaint o dystiolaeth o bob cwr o'r byd. Gwyddom, er enghraifft, o ran y 100 prifysgol uchaf, fod gennym ni rhwng naw a 14 o Loegr, dwy yn yr Alban, gydag un ychydig y tu allan i'r 100 uchaf, ond yn anffodus dim un yng Nghymru, a dim yn agos at fod yn y 100 uchaf, yng Nghymru. Mae ein prifysgol orau ychydig dros safle 200. Mae'r Athro Prendergast wedi llwyddo i gynnal un o'r 100 prifysgol orau yn Iwerddon, a meddwl ydw i tybed a fyddech chi'n barod i ofyn i'r grŵp hwn ystyried strategaeth ar gyfer creu prifysgol yng Nghymru sydd ymhlith y 100 orau, oherwydd dylai fod gennym ni un brifysgol ymhlith y 100 orau yng Nghymru, ac mae angen prifysgol ymhlith y 100 orau arnon ni yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I couldn't agree more. We only have one of the eight universities as part of the Russell Group of universities, and I would want all of our universities to develop in terms of their offer and their standing in the United Kingdom and across the world. That is why the panel is being set up, to look at ways of making them more viable and sustainable, while also trying to support our students as best we can. We can't kill the goose that lays the golden egg. Without students, universities don't exist, so we have to get that balance right, which is why we're asking the panel to undertake this important work. But I absolutely understand where you're coming from. We need all of our universities to succeed and to improve as well.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ni allwn ni gytuno mwy. Dim ond un o'r wyth prifysgol sydd gennym ni sy'n rhan o brifysgolion Grŵp Russell, a byddwn i eisiau i'n holl brifysgolion ddatblygu o ran eu cynnig a'u safle yn y Deyrnas Unedig ac ar draws y byd. Dyna pam mae'r panel yn cael ei sefydlu, i ystyried ffyrdd o'u gwneud yn fwy hyfyw a chynaliadwy, wrth hefyd geisio cefnogi ein myfyrwyr gorau y gallwn ni. Ni allwn ladd yr iâr a cholli'i chywion. Heb fyfyrwyr, nid yw prifysgolion yn bodoli, felly mae'n rhaid i ni gael y cydbwysedd hwnnw'n iawn, a dyna pam ein bod ni'n gofyn i'r panel ymgymryd â'r gwaith pwysig hwn. Ond rwy'n deall yn llwyr eich safbwynt. Mae angen i'n holl brifysgolion lwyddo a gwella hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Deputy Minister, fear of debt is a growing reason for many young people opting out of studying for a degree. I recall the days as recently as two years ago when the money-saving expert Martin Lewis advised students who were eligible for plan 2 loans to take them even if they didn't need them, and invest them, because the interest rates in those days were so low. All of that has changed very quickly with the hiking of interest rates on plan 2 loans and the UK Government's education Secretary calling these egregious and at the top of her in-tray. That's why, in our manifesto for the Senedd election as Welsh Labour, we included a plan to decouple our plan 2 loans from the English system so that Wales can set fair and affordable interest rates, ensuring all young people who may wish to go to university do not feel cost is a barrier. That's also why when I held your position I rejected the freezing of the repayment threshold, ensuring graduates on lower incomes were not drawn into repayments at a time when they might not be able to afford it. In your review, will you commit to working with the UK Government on the issue of plan 2 student interest rates, exploring the importance of continuing to reject a freeze of that repayment threshold, and, perhaps most importantly, exploring the decoupling of plan 2 to create a Wales-only fair system that students and graduates can have faith in over the long term?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ddirprwy Weinidog, mae ofn dyled yn rheswm cynyddol i lawer o bobl ifanc ddewis peidio ag astudio am radd. Rwy'n cofio'r amser mor ddiweddar â dwy flynedd yn ôl pan gynghorodd yr arbenigwr arbed arian Martin Lewis fyfyrwyr a oedd yn gymwys i gael benthyciadau cynllun 2 i'w cymryd hyd yn oed os nad eu hangen arnyn nhw, a'u buddsoddi, oherwydd bod y cyfraddau llog y dyddiau hynny mor isel. Mae hynny i gyd wedi newid yn gyflym iawn gyda'r cynnydd mewn cyfraddau llog ar fenthyciadau cynllun 2 ac Ysgrifennydd Addysg Llywodraeth y DU yn galw'r rhain yn ddybryd ac ar frig ei mewnflwch. Dyna pam, yn ein maniffesto ar gyfer etholiad y Senedd fel Llafur Cymru, fe wnaethon ni gynnwys cynllun i ddatgysylltu ein benthyciadau cynllun 2 o system Lloegr fel bod Cymru yn gallu gosod cyfraddau llog teg a fforddiadwy, gan sicrhau nad yw'r un person ifanc sy'n dymuno mynd i'r brifysgol yn teimlo bod y gost yn rhwystr. Dyna pam, pan yr oeddwn i yn eich swydd chi, y gwnes i wrthod rhewi'r trothwy ad-dalu, gan sicrhau nad oedd graddedigion ar incwm is yn cael eu tynnu i ad-daliadau ar adeg pan efallai na fydden nhw'n gallu'i fforddio. Yn eich adolygiad, a wnewch chi ymrwymo i weithio gyda Llywodraeth y DU ar fater cyfraddau llog myfyrwyr cynllun 2, archwilio pwysigrwydd parhau i wrthod rhewi'r trothwy ad-dalu hwnnw, ac, efallai'n bwysicaf oll, archwilio datgysylltu cynllun 2 i greu system deg yng Nghymru yn unig, y gall myfyrwyr a graddedigion fod â ffydd ynddi dros y tymor hir?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Vikki. You've hit upon one of the most difficult decisions we will have to make as a Welsh Government. You will know the UK Government has indicated its intention to proceed with a freeze to the plan 2 repayment threshold at the current rate of £29,385 in England for the next three financial years. You, as a previous Government, decided to put that on hold, and it's a decision we now have to make. Again, it comes back to the balance between what we expect our students to repay in terms of loans and the burden on them over most of their working life, but also the finances that come from tuition fees as well.

You will have heard a lot of noise in the press across the UK over recent days—the weekend in particular—putting pressure on the Prime Minister to rethink this freeze. I think it's wise for us in Wales to wait to see what the UK Government does first, because many of the regulations around UK Treasury involvement with our plan 2 tie in very closely indeed. I think we will wait to see what the UK Government does before we come to a final position.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Vikki. Rydych chi wedi taro ar un o'r penderfyniadau anoddaf y bydd yn rhaid i ni ei wneud fel Llywodraeth Cymru. Byddwch chi'n gwybod bod Llywodraeth y DU wedi nodi'i bwriad i fwrw ymlaen â rhewi trothwy ad-dalu cynllun 2 ar y gyfradd bresennol sef £29,385 yn Lloegr ar gyfer y tair blynedd ariannol nesaf. Rydych chi, fel Llywodraeth flaenorol, wedi penderfynu gohirio hynny, ac mae'n benderfyniad y mae'n rhaid i ni ei wneud nawr. Unwaith eto, mae'n dod yn ôl at y cydbwysedd rhwng yr hyn yr ydyn ni'n disgwyl i'n myfyrwyr ei ad-dalu o ran benthyciadau a'r baich arnyn nhw dros y rhan fwyaf o'u bywyd gwaith, ond hefyd y cyllid sy'n dod o ffioedd dysgu hefyd.

Byddwch chi wedi clywed llawer o sôn yn y wasg ledled y DU dros y dyddiau diwethaf—y penwythnos yn arbennig—yn rhoi pwysau ar y Prif Weinidog i ailystyried y rhewi hwn. Rwy'n credu'i bod yn ddoeth i ni yng Nghymru aros i weld beth mae Llywodraeth y DU yn ei wneud yn gyntaf, oherwydd mae llawer o'r rheoliadau ynglŷn ag ymwneud Trysorlys y DU â'n cynllun 2 yn cyd-fynd yn agos iawn mewn gwirionedd. Rwy'n credu y gwnawn ni aros i weld beth mae Llywodraeth y DU yn ei wneud cyn i ni ddod i benderfyniad terfynol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Ac yn olaf, Kiera Marshall.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. And finally, Kiera Marshall.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog, for the update today. I want to see more opportunities for learners—not only in Cardiff, but across Wales—who are from the most disadvantaged backgrounds. Since 2020, we haven't seen any meaningful movement in closing the gap between the amount of young people from the most affluent areas going to university compared to those from the most disadvantaged areas. Growing up in Townhill in Swansea, I saw the impact of this gap first-hand on my friends and my neighbours and I'm really keen to support the Government to ensure that the next generation from similar areas across the whole of Wales are given fair opportunities into education. We must have more ambition in providing opportunities to communities that need it most, and at the same time tackling the widening inequality that's happening across the UK. What will this review do to support widening participation across higher education? I think one way we'll agree that we could do this is through degree apprenticeships, but the pathways and the general awareness of degree apprenticeships haven't helped close this gap as of yet. So, how could this review look at furthering the use of degree apprenticeships to help close the widening participation gaps?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog, am y diweddariad heddiw. Rwyf am weld mwy o gyfleoedd i ddysgwyr—nid yn unig yng Nghaerdydd, ond ledled Cymru—sy'n dod o'r cefndiroedd mwyaf difreintiedig. Ers 2020, dydyn ni ddim wedi gweld unrhyw symudiad ystyrlon wrth gau'r bwlch rhwng nifer y bobl ifanc o'r ardaloedd mwyaf cyfoethog sy'n mynd i'r brifysgol o'i gymharu â'r rhai o'r ardaloedd mwyaf difreintiedig. Wrth dyfu i fyny yn Townhill yn Abertawe, gwelais effaith y bwlch hwn yn uniongyrchol ar fy ffrindiau a fy nghymdogion ac rwy'n awyddus iawn i gefnogi'r Llywodraeth i sicrhau bod y genhedlaeth nesaf o ardaloedd tebyg ledled Cymru gyfan yn cael cyfleoedd teg i mewn i addysg. Mae'n rhaid i ni fod â mwy o uchelgais wrth ddarparu cyfleoedd i gymunedau sydd eu hangen fwyaf, ac ar yr un pryd mynd i'r afael â'r anghydraddoldeb sy'n cynyddu sy'n digwydd ledled y DU. Beth fydd yr adolygiad hwn yn ei wneud i gefnogi cyfranogiad ar draws addysg uwch? Rwy'n credu mai un ffordd y byddwn ni'n cytuno y gallem wneud hyn yw trwy brentisiaethau gradd, ond nid yw'r llwybrau a'r ymwybyddiaeth gyffredinol o brentisiaethau gradd wedi helpu i gau'r bwlch hwn eto. Felly, sut allai'r adolygiad hwn edrych ar hybu'r defnydd o brentisiaethau gradd i helpu i gau'r bylchau cyfranogiad sy'n ehangu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol: Adolygiad o Addysg Uwch
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education: Review of Higher Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. That's a really good question to finish off with. It relates to some of the answers I've given previously, but this Welsh Government is absolutely committed to widening participation. The fact that we have, as I mentioned earlier on, a lower number of our Welsh young people going to university than any other part of the United Kingdom is disappointing. We need to raise their ambitions, work closely with schools in those kinds of areas, to make university a destination for those young people.

But I also want to make it known that going to university isn't the only pathway available to our young people. There is a degree apprenticeship scheme that we are happy to support—and I would like to see more young people going along that pathway—but FE colleges, work-based learning, all of that, give different opportunities and options to our young people. I want to get away from the traditional 'work or university' options; there are so many other options as well. I think it's incumbent on our teaching profession, our careers advice people as well, to give as much information about all the options available to our young people, because we want to upskill them and make them as ready as possible for the world of work. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Mae hwnnw'n gwestiwn da iawn i orffen ag ef. Mae'n ymwneud â rhai o'r atebion rydw i wedi'u rhoi o'r blaen, ond mae'r Llywodraeth Cymru hon wedi ymrwymo'n llwyr i ehangu cyfranogiad. Mae'r ffaith bod gennym ni, fel y soniais i yn gynharach, nifer is o'n pobl ifanc yng Nghymru sy'n mynd i'r brifysgol nag unrhyw ran arall o'r Deyrnas Unedig yn siomedig. Mae angen i ni godi eu huchelgeisiau, gweithio'n agos gydag ysgolion yn y mathau hynny o ardaloedd, i wneud prifysgol yn gyrchfan i'r bobl ifanc hynny.

Ond rwyf hefyd eisiau ei gwneud yn hysbys nad mynd i'r brifysgol yw'r unig lwybr sydd ar gael i'n pobl ifanc. Mae yna gynllun prentisiaeth gradd yr ydym ni'n hapus i'w gefnogi—a hoffwn weld mwy o bobl ifanc yn mynd ar hyd y llwybr hwnnw—ond mae colegau AB, dysgu seiliedig ar waith, i gyd, yn rhoi cyfleoedd ac opsiynau gwahanol i'n pobl ifanc. Rwyf am fynd i ffwrdd o'r opsiynau traddodiadol 'gwaith neu brifysgol'; mae cymaint o opsiynau eraill hefyd. Rwy'n credu ei bod yn ddyletswydd ar ein proffesiwn addysgu, ein pobl cynghori gyrfaoedd hefyd, i roi cymaint o wybodaeth am yr holl opsiynau sydd ar gael i'n pobl ifanc, oherwydd rydym am eu huwchsgilio a'u gwneud mor barod â phosibl ar gyfer y byd gwaith. Diolch.
