XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Deputy Minister.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Symudwn ymlaen, felly, i eitem 6, datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg, y cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol. Galwaf ar y Gweinidog Cabinet, Anna Brychan.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We will move on now to item 6, statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language, the foundational literacy and numeracy plan. I call on the Cabinet Minister, Anna Brychan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Following the results of PISA tests taken last year and reported last week, I am today publishing our foundational literacy and numeracy plan. This plan represents an important first step in the development of an equitable system that works for all. It is integral to our PISA response, but it is not just a response to PISA. Our own data is telling us that we are not where we need to be. Our own teachers, leaders and the wider education system want greater clarity, consistency of expectation and greater support to make a difference in the classroom. We have been here before, and successive PISA rounds have highlighted significant and deep-seated issues that have been many years in the making, and that's precisely why we are taking decisive action now.

In many ways, these results reinforce what we already knew: standards of literacy and numeracy in particular require significant and sustained focus, and we must do more to ensure our highest achieving learners reach their full potential. I'm encouraged that our most disadvantaged learners compare well internationally, but data shows that many of our learners could and should be doing better.

Let me be clear: this is not the fault of schools or teachers or support staff. We have inherited a system that lacks clarity, coherence and direction, and literacy and numeracy have been lost in the noise of significant reform. Schools are also responding to increasingly complex learner needs. Demand for specialist support, intervention and wider services continues to grow. We also recognise continued funding challenges. We see the same picture across all our public services as a consequence of an extremely difficult financial settlement. We know too that many of these concerns are shared across this Chamber. These things don't make our ambition to raise standards any easier, but they do demonstrate that educational change is complex and multifaceted, and one that requires a whole-system response. I have long argued that educators, whether teachers, leaders or support staff, are our strongest asset, and it is our responsibility as a Government to ensure that they have the tools to do the job.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Yn dilyn canlyniadau profion PISA a gymerwyd y llynedd ac a adroddwyd yr wythnos diwethaf, rydw i heddiw yn cyhoeddi ein cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol. Mae'r cynllun hwn yn cynrychioli cam cyntaf pwysig yn natblygiad system deg sy'n gweithio i bawb. Mae'n rhan annatod o'n hymateb i PISA, ond nid dim ond ymateb i PISA yn unig ydyw. Mae ein data ein hunain yn dweud wrthym nad ydym lle y mae angen i ni fod. Mae ein hathrawon, ein harweinwyr a'r system addysg ehangach eisiau mwy o eglurder, cysondeb disgwyliadau a mwy o gefnogaeth i wneud gwahaniaeth yn yr ystafell ddosbarth. Rydym wedi bod yma o'r blaen, ac mae rowndiau PISA olynol wedi tynnu sylw at faterion sylweddol a dwfn sydd wedi bod yn ffurfio dros flynyddoedd lawer, a dyna'n union pam rydym yn cymryd camau penderfynol nawr.

Mewn sawl ffordd, mae'r canlyniadau hyn yn atgyfnerthu'r hyn yr oeddem ni eisoes yn ei wybod: mae safonau llythrennedd a rhifedd yn arbennig yn gofyn am ffocws sylweddol a pharhaus, ac mae'n rhaid i ni wneud mwy i sicrhau bod ein dysgwyr sy'n cyflawni uchaf yn cyrraedd eu potensial llawn. Rwy'n galonogol bod ein dysgwyr mwyaf difreintiedig yn cymharu'n dda yn rhyngwladol, ond mae data'n dangos y gallai llawer o'n dysgwyr fod yn gwneud yn well.

Gadewch i mi fod yn glir: nid bai ysgolion nac athrawon na staff cymorth yw hyn. Rydym wedi etifeddu system sydd heb eglurder, cydlyniant a chyfeiriad, ac mae llythrennedd a rhifedd wedi eu colli yn sŵn diwygio sylweddol. Mae ysgolion hefyd yn ymateb i anghenion cynyddol gymhleth dysgwyr. Mae'r galw am gymorth arbenigol, ymyrraeth a gwasanaethau ehangach yn parhau i dyfu. Rydym hefyd yn cydnabod heriau ariannu parhaus. Rydym yn gweld yr un darlun ar draws ein holl wasanaethau cyhoeddus o ganlyniad i setliad ariannol anodd iawn. Gwyddom hefyd fod llawer o'r pryderon hyn yn cael eu rhannu ar draws y Siambr hon. Nid yw'r pethau hyn yn gwneud ein huchelgais i godi safonau yn hawdd, ond maen nhw'n dangos bod newid addysgol yn gymhleth ac yn amlochrog, ac yn un sy'n gofyn am ymateb system gyfan. Rwyf wedi dadlau ers amser maith mai addysgwyr, boed yn athrawon, arweinwyr neu staff cymorth, yw ein hased cryfaf, ac mae'n gyfrifoldeb arnom ni fel Llywodraeth i sicrhau bod ganddyn nhw yr offer i wneud y gwaith.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae ein cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol yn ymwneud â gosod disgwyliadau clir ar gyfer gweithredu. Mae'n amlinellu'n fanwl beth y byddwn i'n ei wneud, a phryd, ac yn dod â'r holl randdeiliaid allweddol ynghyd o dan yr un weledigaeth ar gyfer newid. Mae'r cynllun yn cydnabod yr amrywiaeth o bartneriaid sydd â rôl yn ein hymdrech ar y cyd i godi safonau. Mae rhieni a gofalwyr, ymarferwyr y blynyddoedd cynnar, athrawon ac ymarferwyr addysg, arweinyddion ysgolion a lleoliadau, a phartneriaid cymorth oll yn chwarae rhan hollbwysig yn natblygiad llythrennedd a rhifedd ar draws yr ystod oedran.

Rŷn ni wedi gweithio'n agos gydag arweinwyr yn ogystal ag awdurdodau lleol, Estyn a'n cyrff cefnogi, Dysgu ac Adnodd, i ddatblygu ffordd glir a chydlynol ymlaen. Mae gan Dysgu rôl hanfodol, fel ein corff dysgu proffesiynol cenedlaethol, wrth ddarparu cymorth darllen a mathemateg o ansawdd uchel, sy'n seiliedig ar dystiolaeth, i athrawon ledled Cymru. Mae hwn yn gymorth arbenigol sy'n seiliedig ar wybodaeth am ein cwricwlwm a'n cyd-destun ni. Disgwyliwn i bob ysgol ac awdurdod lleol ymgysylltu â Dysgu wrth i'w gynnig i athrawon ac arweinwyr ddatblygu. Mae e'n bwysig bod addysgwyr, ble bynnag yng Nghymru y maen nhw, yn gallu cael mynediad at yr un lefel o gymorth ac elwa o hwnnw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Our foundational literacy and numeracy plan is about setting clear expectations for action. It sets out in detail what we will do and when, and it brings together all key stakeholders under the same vision for change. The plan recognises the range of partners that have a role in our shared effort to raise standards. Parents and carers, early years practitioners, teachers and education practitioners, leaders of schools and settings, and support partners all play a pivotal role in literacy and numeracy development across the age range.

We have worked closely with leaders as well as local authorities, Estyn and our supporting bodies, Dysgu and Adnodd, to develop a clear and coherent way forward. Dysgu has a crucial role, as our national professional learning body, in the delivery of high-quality, evidence-based reading and mathematics support to teachers across Wales. This is expert support that is based on a knowledge of our curriculum and our context. We expect all schools and local authorities to engage with Dysgu as its offer to teachers and leaders develops. It is important that educators, wherever in Wales they work, have access to the same level of support and can benefit from that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
None of this means that I am any less committed to the Curriculum for Wales, and I have no intention of moving away from its underlying principles and purpose-driven orientation. I have seen first-hand the difference it can make to learners, but literacy and numeracy are the gateway into the curriculum and the means by which learners can access the full range of opportunities it has to offer. I will also set out in the coming months a targeted review of the Curriculum for Wales, focusing on key areas for refinement and clarification.

Today is about recognising the urgency of the situation and that more immediate action is needed. That's why this plan is so important and sets out the actions, in the short and medium term, to raise standards.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid oes unrhyw beth yma sy'n golygu fy mod yn llai ymrwymedig i'r Cwricwlwm i Gymru, ac nid oes gennyf unrhyw fwriad i symud i ffwrdd o'i egwyddorion sylfaenol a'i gyfeiriadedd pwrpasol. Rwyf wedi gweld yn uniongyrchol y gwahaniaeth y gall ei wneud i ddysgwyr, ond llythrennedd a rhifedd yw'r porth i'r cwricwlwm a'r modd y gall dysgwyr gael mynediad i'r ystod lawn o gyfleoedd sydd ganddo i'w cynnig. Byddaf hefyd yn gosod adolygiad wedi'i dargedu o'r Cwricwlwm i Gymru yn ystod y misoedd nesaf, gan ganolbwyntio ar feysydd allweddol i'w mireinio a'u hegluro.

Mae heddiw yn ymwneud â chydnabod brys y sefyllfa a bod angen gweithredu mwy ar unwaith. Dyna pam mae'r cynllun hwn mor bwysig ac yn nodi'r camau gweithredu yn y tymor byr a chanolig, i godi safonau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yn gyntaf, mae’n sefydlu disgwyliadau o flwyddyn i flwyddyn sy’n rhoi eglurder llwyr ynghylch yr hyn y dylai plant ei ddysgu a phryd, gan sicrhau mwy o gysondeb ledled Cymru. Byddwn ni'n cyhoeddi’r manylion hyn ar gyfer ymgynghori yn fuan, fel eu bod nhw'n gallu dod yn ganllawiau statudol cyn gynted â phosibl.

Byddwn ni hefyd yn gwbl glir yn ein canllawiau ynghylch ffoneg synthetig systematig, sy’n arf hanfodol i athrawon wrth helpu plant i ddarllen, ochr yn ochr â datblygu sgiliau darllen eraill. Byddwn ni'n gweithio gydag Estyn, awdurdodau lleol a Dysgu i sicrhau eu bod nhw'n cael eu defnyddio’n effeithiol ac yn gyson. Ac yn wir, rwy’n croesawu ymrwymiad Estyn i ganolbwyntio’n gryfach ar ddarllen a gwaith partneriaid cymorth, megis y bartneriaeth strategol gyda llywodraeth leol.

Yn ail, bydd y cynllun yn cryfhau asesu a’r defnydd o wybodaeth. Byddwn yn cyflwyno asesiad llinell sylfaen—gwaelodlin, i bob pwrpas—pan fydd plant yn dechrau yn yr ysgol, a dangosydd newydd ym mlwyddyn 6, fel bod gan ysgolion ddealltwriaeth glir o ble mae plant a pha gymorth sydd ei angen arnyn nhw. Ar lefel Llywodraeth, byddwn ni'n sefydlu dangosyddion cenedlaethol i asesu ein cynnydd cyffredinol, wedi’u llywio gan dargedau clir. Bydd hyn yn ein galluogi ni i fonitro cynnydd flwyddyn ar ôl blwyddyn, heb orfod aros i PISA ddweud wrthym ni sut rŷn ni'n perfformio.

Mae’r cynllun hefyd yn tanlinellu ein hymrwymiad i gefnogi ysgolion i osod targedau clir iddyn nhw eu hunain ac i’w dysgwyr. Byddwn ni'n gweithio’n agos gydag ysgolion ac awdurdodau lleol i wireddu hyn. Yn ogystal, disgwyliwn i fwy o ysgolion elwa ar CAL:ON Cymru, ein canolfan ragoriaeth genedlaethol newydd ar gyfer llythrennedd, sydd wedi cael croeso cadarnhaol gan athrawon ac sydd wrth wraidd y cynllun hwn.

Bydd y cynllun hefyd yn cefnogi llythrennedd a rhifedd y tu hwnt i’r ystafell ddosbarth. Byddwn ni'n cryfhau ymgysylltiad gyda rhieni, yn hyrwyddo darllen a datblygiad iaith yn y cartref, yn ehangu mynediad at lyfrau drwy lyfrgelloedd ysgolion, ac yn mynd i’r afael â rhwystrau i ddysgu sy’n gysylltiedig â thlodi.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
First, it establishes year-on-year expectations that give absolute clarity about what children should learn and when, ensuring greater consistency across Wales. We will publish this detail for consultation shortly, so that it becomes statutory guidance as soon as possible.

We will also be unequivocal in our guidance about systematic synthetic phonics, which is an essential tool in teachers’ armoury when helping children to read, alongside developing other reading skills. We will work with Estyn, local authorities and Dysgu to ensure it is used effectively and consistently. And indeed, I welcome Estyn’s commitment to an enhanced focus on reading and the efforts by support partners, such as the strategic partnership with local government.

Secondly, the plan will strengthen assessment and use of information. We will introduce a baseline assessment when children start school and a new indicator in year 6, so that schools have a clear understanding of where children are and of what support they need. At a Government level, we will establish national indicators to assess our progress overall, driven by clear targets. This will mean that we can monitor progress year on year, and not have to wait for PISA to tell us how we’re performing.

The plan also underlines our commitment to supporting schools to set clear targets for themselves and for their learners. We will work closely with schools and local authorities to make this happen. In addition, we expect more schools to benefit from CAL:ON Cymru, our new national centre of excellence in literacy, which has been well received by teachers and which sits front and centre of our plan.

The plan will also support literacy and numeracy beyond the classroom. We will strengthen parental engagement, promote reading and language development at home, increase access to books through school libraries, and address poverty-related barriers to learning.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
By the end of this Senedd term we want to see sustained improvement in literacy and numeracy for all children and young people; more children and young people making good progress from where they start; and more young people leaving education with better qualifications, ready for further study, training or work. 

The next set of PISA results will be focused on learners who will be 15 in 2029, and we will get those results in 2030. Naturally, I’m hoping to see an improvement in Wales’s scores in the next PISA round, but I'm mindful of the need to support learners who are in our system now, and that is precisely why this plan has been developed.

Dirprwy Lywydd, we are a new Government with new ambition and make no apologies for setting the bar high. Wales is a proud educating nation whose rich history has been underpinned by a skillful workforce and a thoughtful civic society.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Erbyn diwedd tymor y Senedd hon rydym eisiau gweld gwelliant parhaus mewn llythrennedd a rhifedd ar gyfer pob plentyn a pherson ifanc; mwy o blant a phobl ifanc yn gwneud cynnydd da o'r man lle maen nhw'n dechrau; a mwy o bobl ifanc yn gadael addysg gyda chymwysterau gwell, yn barod ar gyfer astudio, hyfforddiant neu waith pellach. 

Bydd y set nesaf o ganlyniadau PISA yn canolbwyntio ar ddysgwyr a fydd yn 15 oed yn 2029, a byddwn yn cael y canlyniadau hynny yn 2030. Wrth gwrs, rwy'n gobeithio gweld gwelliant yn sgoriau Cymru yn y rownd PISA nesaf, ond rwy'n ymwybodol o'r angen i gefnogi dysgwyr sydd yn ein system nawr, a dyna'n union pam mae'r cynllun hwn wedi'i ddatblygu.

Ddirprwy Lywydd, rydym yn Llywodraeth newydd gydag uchelgais newydd ac nid ydym yn ymddiheuro am osod y bar yn uchel. Mae Cymru yn genedl addysgol falch y mae ei hanes cyfoethog wedi'i ategu gan weithlu medrus a chymdeithas ddinesig feddylgar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae arnom ni ddyletswydd i gael llythrennedd a rhifedd yn iawn er lles cenedlaethau'r presennol a chenedlaethau'r dyfodol. Mae hyn yn golygu galluogi athrawon, arweinwyr a staff cymorth i ganolbwyntio ar yr hyn sydd bwysicaf: addysgu, dysgu a chefnogi dysgwyr i lwyddo. Ond bydd cyrraedd y fan lle rŷn ni eisiau bod yn gofyn am ymdrech ar y cyd, ac rydyn ni wedi ymrwymo i weithio gyda rhieni, gofalwyr, addysgwyr, ysgolion a phartneriaid cymorth i godi safonau ac, yn sgil hynny, wella cyfleoedd bywyd pob plentyn yng Nghymru. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We owe it to current and future generations to get literacy and numeracy right. This means allowing teachers, leaders and support staff to focus on what matters most: teaching, learning and supporting learners to succeed. But getting us to where we want to be will need to be a team effort, and we are committed to working with parents, carers, educators, schools and support partners to raise standards and, with that, improve the life chances of every child in Wales. Thank you very much.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog. Helen Jenner.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Minister. Helen Jenner.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. I just want to update my register of interests as well. I now tutor overseas students at GCSE level four hours a week.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Dwi ond eisiau diweddaru fy nghofrestr buddiannau hefyd. Rwyf bellach yn tiwtora myfyrwyr tramor ar lefel TGAU bedair awr yr wythnos.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am y datganiad yna, ac a gaf i ddechrau drwy groesawu'r ffocws newydd yma ar lythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol? Er y gwahaniaethau gwleidyddol rhyngoch chi a fi, rydyn ni'n dwy yn cytuno y dylai pob plentyn yng Nghymru adael yr ysgol yn gallu darllen, ysgrifennu a defnyddio rhifau yn hyderus. Mae'n rhaid i'r pethau sylfaenol yma ddod yn gyntaf. Ond, Weinidog, mae ambell gyfaddefiad eithaf arwyddocaol yn eich datganiad heddiw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that statement, and may I start by welcoming this new focus on foundational numeracy and literacy? Despite the political differences between you and I, we both agree that every child in Wales should leave school being able to read, write and use numbers confidently. These fundamentals must come first. But, Minister, there are a few significant admissions in your statement today.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You say that the education system has lacked

'clarity, coherence and direction, and literacy and numeracy have been lost in the noise of significant reform.'

So, parents will quite reasonably ask how we were ever allowed to reach that point in the first place. The latest PISA results show Wales scoring 476 in science, 459 in reading and 456 in mathematics. Welsh learners are behind the other UK nations across all three subjects, as we know. On the headline scores, Wales is now closer to Vietnam than to England in both mathematics and science. Gweinidog, I believe we should recognise this for exactly what it is: it’s a national emergency in Welsh education.

I agree, we do need clearer expectations about what children should know and when, earlier identification of those falling behind, a stronger focus on phonics and better use of assessment data. These are all very sensible suggestions. But you've said today that the national indicators will be driven by clear targets, so I would like to ask, what are those targets? What measurable improvement do you expect to see by when, and will those targets be published so that parents, teachers, this Senedd, can judge whether this plan has actually worked? Because saying that standards must improve is not the same as setting out what success looks like.

I also want to understand what this plan means for teachers on the front line of an education system in distress. You're proposing a new baseline assessment, a year 6 indicator, national indicators and greater target setting. You and I both know that teachers are under enormous pressure. I've raised before that retaining good teachers is every bit as important as recruiting them. So, what additional time, training and resources will schools receive to deliver this plan? And importantly, Minister, what are you taking away? Because if every new initiative simply means more assessments, more data collection and an increase in teacher workload, then we risk adding fuel to the fire by pushing people out of the profession.

I also want to turn to additional learning needs. You acknowledge today that schools are dealing with increasingly complex needs, growing demand for specialist support and, ironically, continued funding pressure. That is exactly why Reform argued in favour of greater funding for ALN here in Wales. But the supplementary budget you published did not provide additional funding specifically for ALN. Only when securing support for that budget became critical did the Government begin making additional offers to local authorities and schools at the coalface of ALN. So, when you say today that children will be identified earlier and receive appropriate intervention, the obvious question is: intervention from whom, and paid for by what? Identifying that a child is struggling is only the first step. Schools and councils then need teaching assistants, specialist teachers, educational psychologists and appropriate provision to actually help that child. So, do you still believe it was the right decision not to direct more money towards ALN in the supplementary budget?

When the pressures you describe in today's statement are already being felt in classrooms across Wales, your Government had the opportunity to do something about it. The funding was there, arising from greater special educational needs and disability spending in England. I'd be interested to know what representations, if any, you made during the broader negotiation stages of that budget.

And finally, Minister, accountability—atebolrwydd. You say in your statement that you are hoping to see an improvement in Wales's scores in the next PISA round. I think we need something firmer than hope. The next cohort will sit PISA, as you said, in 2029, with the results published in 2030. So, will you commit today that, when those results are published, Wales will have improved on its current scores in reading, mathematics and science? That is a straightforward measure against which this Government can be judged. Parents, teachers and indeed the children themselves deserve clarity. What does success look like? When will we see it? And who will take responsibility if it's not delivered? Will it be you, Gweinidog? Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rydych chi'n dweud bod y system addysg heb

'eglurder, cydlyniant a chyfeiriad, ac mae llythrennedd a rhifedd wedi eu colli yn sŵn diwygio sylweddol.'

Felly, yn rhesymol, bydd rhieni yn gofyn sut y caniatawyd i ni gyrraedd y fan honno yn y lle cyntaf. Mae canlyniadau diweddaraf PISA yn dangos bod Cymru yn sgorio 476 mewn gwyddoniaeth, 459 mewn darllen a 456 mewn mathemateg. Mae dysgwyr Cymraeg y tu ôl i genhedloedd eraill y DU ar draws y tri phwnc, fel y gwyddom. Ar y prif sgoriau, mae Cymru bellach yn agosach at Fietnam nag at Loegr mewn mathemateg a gwyddoniaeth. Weinidog, rwy'n credu y dylem gydnabod hyn am yr hyn ydyw yn union: mae'n argyfwng cenedlaethol mewn addysg yng Nghymru.

Rwy'n cytuno, mae angen disgwyliadau cliriach ynglŷn â'r hyn y dylai plant ei wybod a phryd, adnabod y rhai sydd ar ei hôl hi, mwy o bwyslais ar ffoneg a gwell defnydd o ddata asesu. Mae'r rhain i gyd yn awgrymiadau synhwyrol iawn. Ond rydych chi wedi dweud heddiw y bydd y dangosyddion cenedlaethol yn cael eu hysgogi gan dargedau clir, felly hoffwn ofyn, beth yw'r targedau hynny? Pa welliant mesuradwy ydych chi'n disgwyl ei weld ac erbyn pryd, ac a fydd y targedau hynny'n cael eu cyhoeddi fel y gall rhieni, athrawon, y Senedd hon, farnu a yw'r cynllun hwn wedi gweithio mewn gwirionedd? Oherwydd nid yw dweud bod yn rhaid i safonau wella yr un peth â nodi sut olwg sydd ar lwyddiant.

Rwyf hefyd eisiau deall beth mae'r cynllun hwn yn ei olygu i athrawon ar y rheng flaen o system addysg mewn trallod. Rydych chi'n cynnig asesiad sylfaenol newydd, dangosydd blwyddyn 6, dangosyddion cenedlaethol a mwy o osod targedau. Rydych chi a minnau'n gwybod bod athrawon o dan bwysau enfawr. Rwyf wedi crybwyll o'r blaen bod cadw athrawon da yr un mor bwysig â'u recriwtio. Felly, pa amser, hyfforddiant ac adnoddau ychwanegol y bydd ysgolion yn eu derbyn i gyflawni'r cynllun hwn? Ac yn bwysig, Weinidog, beth ydych chi'n ei dynnu i ffwrdd? Oherwydd os yw pob menter newydd yn golygu mwy o asesiadau, mwy o gasglu data a chynnydd mewn llwyth gwaith athrawon, yna rydym mewn perygl o roi tanwydd ar y tân trwy wthio pobl allan o'r proffesiwn.

Rwyf hefyd eisiau troi at anghenion dysgu ychwanegol. Rydych chi'n cydnabod heddiw bod ysgolion yn ymdrin ag anghenion cynyddol gymhleth, galw cynyddol am gymorth arbenigol ac, yn eironig, pwysau ariannu parhaus. Dyna'n union pam y dadleuodd Reform o blaid mwy o gyllid ar gyfer ADY yma yng Nghymru. Ond nid oedd y gyllideb atodol a gyhoeddwyd gennych yn darparu cyllid ychwanegol yn benodol ar gyfer ADY. Felly, pan fyddwch chi'n dweud heddiw y bydd plant yn cael eu nodi yn gynharach ac yn derbyn ymyrraeth briodol, y cwestiwn amlwg yw: ymyrraeth gan bwy, a'i ariannu gan beth? Dim ond y cam cyntaf yw nodi bod plentyn yn cael trafferth. Yna mae angen cynorthwywyr addysgu, athrawon arbenigol, seicolegwyr addysgol a darpariaeth briodol ar ysgolion a chynghorau i helpu'r plentyn hwnnw. Felly, ydych chi'n dal i gredu mai dyma'r penderfyniad cywir sef peidio â chyfeirio mwy o arian tuag at ADY yn y gyllideb atodol?

Pan fydd y pwysau rydych chi'n eu disgrifio yn y datganiad heddiw eisoes yn cael eu teimlo mewn ystafelloedd dosbarth ledled Cymru, cafodd eich Llywodraeth gyfle i wneud rhywbeth am y peth. Roedd y cyllid yno, yn deillio o fwy o wariant ar anghenion addysgol arbennig ac anabledd yn Lloegr. Byddai gen i ddiddordeb gwybod pa sylwadau, os o gwbl, wnaethoch chi yn ystod camau trafod ehangach y gyllideb honno.

Ac yn olaf, Weinidog, atebolrwydd. Rydych chi'n dweud yn eich datganiad eich bod yn gobeithio gweld gwelliant yn sgoriau Cymru yn y rownd PISA nesaf. Rwy'n credu bod angen rhywbeth mwy cadarn na gobaith. Bydd y garfan nesaf yn sefyll PISA, fel y dywedoch chi, yn 2029, gyda'r canlyniadau yn cael eu cyhoeddi yn 2030. Felly, a wnewch chi ymrwymo heddiw y bydd Cymru, pan fydd y canlyniadau hynny'n cael eu cyhoeddi, wedi gwella ar ei sgoriau presennol mewn darllen, mathemateg a gwyddoniaeth? Mae hynny'n fesur syml y gellir barnu'r Llywodraeth hon yn ei erbyn. Mae rhieni, athrawon ac yn wir y plant eu hunain yn haeddu eglurder. Sut olwg sydd ar lwyddiant? Pryd fyddwn ni'n ei weld? A phwy fydd yn cymryd cyfrifoldeb os na chaiff ei gyflawni? Ai chi Weinidog? Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. I will try and answer as many of those questions as I can. In terms of the delivery, I want this to demonstrate progress in Wales before the end of this Senedd term. In order to do that, I think we need to be clear what delivery means, and that's why I've undertaken to set up a delivery board that will be expressly responsible for this. It will bring together all the key partners who have a stake and a responsibility in relation to this plan. I intend to chair it myself, and it will meet in the autumn term for the first time. So, I expect you to be asking me for the progress that has been made well before the next PISA round.

The workload question you raised is obviously a pertinent one, and we've discussed this before. We have undertaken a workload assessment against this plan, and I'm very keen to keep an eye on whether this is adding, because my hope and intention is that the increased clarity around the expectations will actually be helpful in that regard. Because some of the feedback—well, quite a lot of the feedback, in fact—that I regularly have from teachers and headteachers is that that lack of clarity is in itself problematic in terms of workload. But workload, as you will know too, is part of a separate piece of work that we are doing, looking in detail at that and linked to behaviour and other issues in schools that are making that engagement with learners difficult. So, that is a discrete piece of work that I'm happy to update on at another time, but I am still considering these things in the round.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
In terms of identifying early intervention, I've already had conversations with the Deputy Prime Minister—First Minister, sorry—[Laughter.]—I translated in my head, didn't I—the Deputy First Minister, and the health Minister as well, because the key thing about this is that our childcare offer and health services, health visitors, and all the people who have key information about families and learners already exist in our system. The bringing together of that data and information to inform schools is a piece of work that we are doing. And interestingly—sorry, I've been waiting to share this all day—interestingly, one of the things we will need to identify is that baseline when learners are entering school, because a lot of the feedback from school is a concern around this. We are dealing with issues and needs that perhaps we haven't seen before. So, a clear understanding of that is a priority for us. So, we are looking to establish that baseline now for piloting then next year, as you will see in the planned timeline.

I have, following PISA last week, also had conversations with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. And this one is of particular interest for jurisdictions across the world, because doing this well, in a way that isn't too onerous for the professionals that have to engage at a school level, but does give you an early insight into the support that that child needs and from whom—. But also it's a method, particularly in our primary schools, for them to be able to demonstrate, across that school, that pupil's journey, the value they have added. And the start—. It's important to understand the starting point if you have expectations of the end point. So, that will be key, and there's a clear timeline around that, as there is about the national indicator at year 6, for, essentially, the same reason: where are we now at the end of primary school education? These, though, are going to—. It brings us back to the workload point in a way. I want to develop these measures using data and information that is in the system already. We have a lot of data. Teachers are used to the personalised assessments, for example. These are familiar structures, familiar data that we can use and draw down to inform these baselines. That means no new things, because that was a key consideration as well, because these have been developed with our system in mind and with a workforce that is familiar with them in mind.

You mentioned local authorities as well, and I have deliberately built this plan around five foundations. This is a way of bringing together, for the first time for nought to 16, all those who have a responsibility and knowledge of these children: families, parents and carers, local authorities, schools, support services—all those people who are part of our system, working together through a delivery board to show that we can make a difference to the learners in our system now. We can use data better. We will have targets that show us that our system is going in the right direction.

I've already had many conversations, even before I started in this new role, with leaders and teachers in our education system. This will be not unfamiliar for them, but it will also give them the clarity that they seek and that they are asking for increasingly, for them to have the confidence and for us to have the confidence, that there is a consistent understanding of what our expectations are across all local authorities across Wales.

When the detailed statutory guidance on those expectations is published later this term, you will see the level of detail in there, which I trust that people will find helpful. We will consult on that, because I intend it to be statutory guidance, but that is a significant piece of work that has been undertaken over the last four months, with the intention that it gives us as a system an understanding of the direction we're going in, what we need to see in classrooms across Wales, how do we give ourselves, all of us, confidence that we are going in the right direction, and bring teachers with us too. Diolch yn fawr.

O ran nodi ymyrraeth gynnar, rydw i eisoes wedi cael sgyrsiau gyda'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog—Prif Weinidog, mae'n ddrwg gen i—[Chwerthin.]—Cyfieithais yn fy mhen—y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog, a'r Gweinidog dros iechyd hefyd, oherwydd y peth allweddol am hyn yw bod ein cynnig gofal plant a'n gwasanaethau iechyd, ymwelwyr iechyd, a'r holl bobl sydd â gwybodaeth allweddol am deuluoedd a dysgwyr eisoes yn bodoli yn ein system. Mae dod â'r data a'r wybodaeth honno at ei gilydd i hysbysu ysgolion yn ddarn o waith yr ydym yn ei wneud. Ac yn ddiddorol—mae'n ddrwg gen oi, rydw i wedi bod yn aros i rannu hyn trwy'r dydd—yn ddiddorol, un o'r pethau y bydd angen i ni eu nodi yw'r llinell sylfaen honno pan fydd dysgwyr yn mynd i'r ysgol, oherwydd mae llawer o'r adborth o'r ysgol yn cynnwys pryder ynghylch hyn. Rydym yn ymdrin â materion ac anghenion nad ydym efallai wedi'u gweld o'r blaen. Felly, mae dealltwriaeth glir o hynny yn flaenoriaeth i ni. Felly, rydym yn bwriadu sefydlu'r llinell sylfaen honno nawr ar gyfer treialu wedyn y flwyddyn nesaf, fel y gwelwch yn yr amserlen arfaethedig.

Ar ôl PISA yr wythnos diwethaf, rwyf hefyd wedi cael sgyrsiau gyda'r Sefydliad ar gyfer Cydweithrediad a Datblygiad Economaidd. Ac mae hwn o ddiddordeb arbennig i awdurdodaethau ledled y byd, oherwydd bydd gwneud hyn yn dda, mewn ffordd nad yw'n rhy feichus i'r gweithwyr proffesiynol sy'n gorfod ymgysylltu ar lefel ysgol, ond sy'n rhoi cipolwg cynnar i chi ar y gefnogaeth sydd ei hangen ar y plentyn hwnnw a gan bwy—. Ond hefyd mae'n ddull iddyn nhw allu dangos, ar draws yr ysgol honno, daith y disgybl, y gwerth maen nhw wedi'i ychwanegu. A'r cychwyn—. Mae'n bwysig deall y man cychwyn os oes gennych ddisgwyliadau ynghylch y man terfynol. Felly, bydd hynny'n allweddol, ac mae amserlen glir ar gyfer hynny, fel sydd ar gyfer y dangosydd cenedlaethol ym mlwyddyn 6, am yr un rheswm: ble ydym ni nawr ar ddiwedd addysg ysgol gynradd? Mae'r rhain, fodd bynnag, yn mynd i—. Mae'n dod â ni yn ôl at y pwynt llwyth gwaith mewn ffordd. Rwyf eisiau datblygu'r mesurau hyn gan ddefnyddio data a gwybodaeth sydd eisoes yn y system. Mae gennym lawer o ddata. Mae athrawon wedi arfer â'r asesiadau personol, er enghraifft. Mae'r rhain yn strwythurau cyfarwydd, data cyfarwydd y gallwn eu defnyddio a'u tynnu i lawr i lywio'r llinellau sylfaen hyn. Mae hynny'n golygu na fydd pethau newydd, oherwydd roedd hynny'n ystyriaeth allweddol hefyd, oherwydd mae'r rhain wedi'u datblygu gyda'n system mewn golwg a gyda gweithlu sy'n gyfarwydd â nhw mewn golwg.

Fe wnaethoch chi sôn am awdurdodau lleol hefyd, ac rwyf wedi adeiladu'r cynllun hwn yn fwriadol o amgylch pum sylfaen. Mae hon yn ffordd o ddwyn ynghyd unrhyw un sydd â chyfrifoldeb a gwybodaeth am y plant hyn: teuluoedd, rhieni a gofalwyr, awdurdodau lleol, ysgolion, gwasanaethau cymorth—yr holl bobl hynny sy'n rhan o'n system, sy'n gweithio gyda'i gilydd trwy fwrdd cyflawni i ddangos y gallwn wneud gwahaniaeth i'r dysgwyr yn ein system nawr. Gallwn ddefnyddio data'n well. Bydd gennym dargedau sy'n dangos i ni fod ein system yn mynd i'r cyfeiriad cywir.

Rwyf eisoes wedi cael llawer o sgyrsiau, hyd yn oed cyn i mi ddechrau yn y rôl newydd hon, gydag arweinwyr ac athrawon yn ein system addysg. Ni fydd hyn yn anghyfarwydd iddyn nhw, ond bydd hefyd yn rhoi'r eglurder y maen nhw'n ceisio ac y maen nhw'n gofyn amdano yn gynyddol, er mwyn iddynt gael yr hyder ac i ni gael yr hyder, bod yna ddealltwriaeth gyson am beth yw ein disgwyliadau ar draws pob awdurdod lleol ledled Cymru.

Pan gyhoeddir y canllawiau statudol manwl ar y disgwyliadau hynny yn ddiweddarach y tymor hwn, fe welwch y lefel o fanylion yno, yr wyf yn hyderus y bydd pobl yn eu hystyried yn ddefnyddiol. Byddwn yn ymgynghori ar hynny, oherwydd y bwriad yw eu bod yn ganllawiau statudol, ond mae hynny'n ddarn sylweddol o waith sydd wedi'i wneud dros y pedwar mis diwethaf, gyda'r bwriad ei fod yn rhoi dealltwriaeth i ni fel system am y cyfeiriad rydym ni'n mynd iddo, beth sydd angen i ni ei weld mewn ystafelloedd dosbarth ledled Cymru, sut ydyn ni'n rhoi hyder i ni'n hunain, pob un ohonom, ein bod ni'n mynd i'r cyfeiriad cywir, a dod ag athrawon gyda ni hefyd. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I thank the Cabinet Minister for her statement today? I was very keen to be positive this afternoon, which I think is a good thing, because I can see many things in this plan that were begun during my time in Government under the last Labour Government: for example, the changes to personalised assessments, the development of age-related expectations, the clear prioritisation of literacy and numeracy, and the £20 million that we invested in grants for literacy and numeracy, including the CAL:ON programme, which I see you are remaining committed to in your plan. I'm very happy to see some of these initiatives repackaged into a plan under the new Government. What matters is that the work happens to benefit children and young people.

I do have some questions. My first is on the targeted review of Curriculum for Wales. I just wanted to ask if you could say a little bit more about what 'targeted review' means. I'm obviously very conscious that, towards the end of our time in Government, one of the areas Estyn flagged up as being a concern was the humanities. Is it your plan to pick off certain areas in order to review the curriculum in relation to that?

I took the decision to take Wales into TIMSS, the trends in international mathematics and science study, and PIRLS, the progress in international reading literacy study, the international primary school tests. I thought that that was the right thing to do, to do that international benchmarking. There was some resistance from some trade unions, but I was very clear that these would be a test of the Government rather than of schools. So, I just wanted to ask where TIMSS and PIRLS fit into this. Is it your intention to remain committed to TIMSS and PIRLS, and how will they inform the work that you are doing?

You've talked about setting targets for schools, and that's fine. Is it your intention to set a target for the Government? The statement refers to 'sustained improvement'. What is that going to look like? Are you going to be more concrete than that? Obviously, I'm conscious that you are discussing targets at a time when industrial relations are quite difficult with the teaching unions. As we know, the NAHT is out to ballot at the moment. What discussions have you had with trade union partners on these measures?

I wanted to ask specifically about mental health. As you know, it's something I'm particularly passionate about. Your plan includes a commitment to roll out the wraparound mental health support, starting from autumn 2026. I'm not at all opposed to new ways of supporting learners and families, but I do want to point out again that the school counselling toolkit, which was commissioned previously from the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy and which was designed to improve our counselling offering in Wales, which we already invest a huge sum of money in, and make that more consistent, has not been published. Is there an update on that? Because we really have to get the basics right in schools in terms of school counselling before looking to build on those.

And then my final point: in the plan, it says you've made a commitment to review the pupil development grant policy to improve how we allocate and fund it, monitor its use and impact and how we evaluate the success of grant funding, and the work on that starts in autumn 2026. That did come as a bit of a surprise to me, because I announced a review of the pupil development grant in December 2025, and the work on that was proceeding. So, is this a departure from that work? Is it a continuation of this work? And can I have an assurance that this work is not new, because it was meant to be under way from 2025? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf i ddiolch i'r Gweinidog Cabinet am ei datganiad heddiw? Roeddwn i'n awyddus iawn i fod yn gadarnhaol y prynhawn yma, sy'n beth da, oherwydd gallaf weld llawer o bethau yn y cynllun hwn a ddechreuwyd yn ystod fy nghyfnod yn y Llywodraeth o dan y Llywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf: er enghraifft, y newidiadau i asesiadau personol, datblygu disgwyliadau sy'n gysylltiedig ag oedran, blaenoriaethu llythrennedd a rhifedd yn glir, a'r £20 miliwn a fuddsoddwyd gennym mewn grantiau ar gyfer llythrennedd a rhifedd, gan gynnwys y rhaglen CAL:ON, yr wyf yn gweld eich bod yn parhau i ymrwymo iddi yn eich cynllun. Rwy'n hapus iawn i weld rhai o'r mentrau hyn yn cael eu hailbecynnu i greu cynllun o dan y Llywodraeth newydd. Yr hyn sy'n bwysig yw bod y gwaith yn digwydd er budd plant a phobl ifanc.

Mae gen i rai cwestiynau. Mae'r un cyntaf ar yr adolygiad wedi'i dargedu o'r Cwricwlwm i Gymru. Roeddwn i eisiau gofyn a allech chi ddweud ychydig mwy am yr hyn y mae 'adolygiad wedi'i dargedu' yn ei olygu. Rwy'n amlwg yn ymwybodol iawn, tua diwedd ein hamser yn y Llywodraeth, mai un o'r meysydd a oedd Estyn yn ei nodi fel pryder oedd y dyniaethau. Ai eich cynllun chi yw dewis rhai meysydd er mwyn adolygu'r cwricwlwm mewn perthynas â hynny?

Fe wnes i benderfynu mynd â Chymru i mewn i TIMSS, yr astudiaeth ryngwladol o dueddiadau mewn mathemateg a gwyddoniaeth, a PIRLS, yr astudiaeth cynnydd mewn llythrennedd darllen rhyngwladol, y profion ysgolion cynradd rhyngwladol. Roeddwn i'n meddwl mai dyna'r peth iawn i'w wneud, i gyflawni'r meincnodi rhyngwladol hwnnw. Roedd rhywfaint o wrthwynebiad gan rai undebau llafur, ond roeddwn i'n glir iawn y byddai'r rhain yn brawf i'r Llywodraeth yn hytrach nag i ysgolion. Felly, roeddwn i eisiau gofyn pa ran sydd gan TIMSS a PIRLS yn hyn. Ai eich bwriad yw parhau i fod yn ymrwymedig i TIMSS a PIRLS, a sut y byddant yn llywio'r gwaith rydych chi'n ei wneud?

Rydych chi wedi sôn am osod targedau ar gyfer ysgolion, ac mae hynny'n iawn. Ai eich bwriad yw gosod targed i'r Llywodraeth? Mae'r datganiad yn cyfeirio at 'welliant parhaus'. Sut olwg fydd ar hynny? Ydych chi'n mynd i fod yn fwy cadarn na hynny? Yn amlwg, rwy'n ymwybodol eich bod chi'n trafod targedau ar adeg pan fo cysylltiadau diwydiannol yn eithaf anodd gyda'r undebau addysgu. Fel y gwyddom, mae'r NAHT yn pleidleisio ar hyn o bryd. Pa drafodaethau ydych chi wedi'u cael gyda phartneriaid undebau llafur ar y mesurau hyn?

Roeddwn i eisiau gofyn yn benodol am iechyd meddwl. Fel y gwyddoch, mae'n rhywbeth rydw i'n arbennig o angerddol amdano. Mae eich cynllun yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i gyflwyno'r cymorth iechyd meddwl cofleidiol, gan ddechrau o hydref 2026. Nid wyf yn gwrthwynebu ffyrdd newydd o gefnogi dysgwyr a theuluoedd, ond rwyf eisiau nodi eto nad yw'r pecyn cymorth cwnsela ysgolion, a gomisiynwyd yn flaenorol gan Gymdeithas Cwnsela a Seicotherapi Prydain ac a gynlluniwyd i wella ein cynnig cwnsela yng Nghymru, yr ydym eisoes yn buddsoddi swm enfawr o arian ynddo, ac yn gwneud hynny'n fwy cyson, wedi'i gyhoeddi. Oes diweddariad ynghylch hynny? Oherwydd mae'n rhaid i ni gael y pethau sylfaenol yn iawn mewn ysgolion o ran cwnsela mewn ysgol cyn ystyried adeiladu ar y rheini.

Ac yna fy mhwynt olaf: yn y cynllun, mae'n dweud eich bod wedi gwneud ymrwymiad i adolygu'r polisi grant datblygu disgyblion i wella sut rydym yn ei ddyrannu a'i ariannu, monitro ei ddefnydd a'i effaith a sut rydym yn gwerthuso llwyddiant cyllid grant, ac mae'r gwaith ar hynny yn dechrau yn hydref 2026. Roedd hynny'n dipyn o syndod i mi, oherwydd cyhoeddais adolygiad o'r grant datblygu disgyblion ym mis Rhagfyr 2025, ac roedd y gwaith ar hynny yn mynd rhagddo. Felly, a yw hyn yn golygu gadael y gwaith hwnnw? A yw'n barhad o'r gwaith hwn? Ac a gaf i sicrwydd nad yw'r gwaith hwn yn newydd, oherwydd roedd i fod ar y gweill o 2025? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you very much. Yes, a target for Government, that is what my intention is in establishing some of these expectations around, particularly, the year 6 indicator—that it is for us as a Government to assume the responsibility of Government around leadership of that improvement and be able—. We need to establish that baseline and then plot from there what a trajectory of progress will look like. And yes, I will be very happy to share that.

On a school level, what I expect to happen is professional conversations between the schools and local authorities and that they draw as well on support by organisations like CAL:ON, using this plan to understand how the learners in their care are improving their skills. I'm not returning to standard assessment tests or league tables or any—. I know some people find them deeply attractive; I find them replete with unintended consequences. What we want is to make a genuine difference in classrooms across Wales and hold ourselves as a Government to account for the progress we are making.

On TIMSS and PIRLS, yes, we are remaining in TIMSS and PIRLS at this point, and I'm looking forward to seeing what they show us when we have data from that. Because, obviously, if there is any data anywhere that will usefully inform us to do this better, then I'm very keen to interrogate that and use it. But I am also keen on intelligent accountability in our system and I'm sure that will resonate with a lot of the partners we have worked with over the years. Saying a thing doesn't make it so—you need to make it work at school level, you need to make it intelligently accountable, from their point of view and also from ours. We are trying to address issues in the Welsh system; importing things and applying them without thought does not work in that context. We need to make improvements here in our own context with our own learners.

You asked about mental health, and I will have to come back to you on the update, because I can't quite remember. But mental health is a key priority, because we know this is one of the reasons that impacts, for example, attendance. So, if we are to make a difference to these learners around literacy and numeracy, they will need to be in school to be able to access that. They will need the support to be able to engage with the curriculum. So that remains, we know, a pressing priority. And particularly post COVID, some of these issues are very—what's the word—profound for a lot of learners and that support will need to be there, if they are to be well supported and benefit from the plans we have.

There was a question then about reviewing the pupil development grant. I have made no decisions about that. But I am looking that everything we do supports the aims of this plan, and supports our workforce and every part of our education system to effect these improvements and to support them as individuals in it as well. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Ie, targed i'r Llywodraeth, dyna beth yw fy mwriad wrth sefydlu rhai o'r disgwyliadau hyn ynghylch, yn enwedig, y dangosydd blwyddyn 6—ein bod ni fel Llywodraeth yn cymryd cyfrifoldeb Llywodraeth dros arweinyddiaeth y gwelliant hwnnw a gallu—. Mae angen i ni sefydlu'r llinell sylfaen honno ac yna plotio o'r fan hon sut olwg fydd ar lwybr cynnydd. A byddaf yn hapus iawn i rannu hynny.

Ar lefel ysgol, yr hyn rwy'n disgwyl y bydd yn digwydd yw sgyrsiau proffesiynol rhwng yr ysgolion ac awdurdodau lleol a'u bod yn tynnu hefyd ar gefnogaeth sefydliadau fel CAL:ON, gan ddefnyddio'r cynllun hwn i ddeall sut mae'r dysgwyr yn eu gofal yn gwella eu sgiliau. Nid wyf yn dychwelyd at brofion asesu safonol neu dablau cynghrair neu unrhyw—. Rwy'n gwybod bod rhai pobl yn eu gweld yn ddeniadol iawn; rwy'n eu gweld yn llawn canlyniadau anfwriadol. Yr hyn yr ydym yn dymuno yw gwneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol mewn ystafelloedd dosbarth ledled Cymru a dal ein hunain fel Llywodraeth i gyfrif am y cynnydd rydym ni'n ei wneud.

Ar TIMSS a PIRLS, ydym, rydym ni'n aros yn TIMSS a PIRLS ar hyn o bryd, ac rwy'n edrych ymlaen at weld beth maen nhw'n ei ddangos i ni pan fydd gennym ddata o hynny. Oherwydd, yn amlwg, os oes unrhyw ddata yn unrhyw le a fydd yn ddefnyddiol i ni wneud hyn yn well, yna rwy'n awyddus iawn i archwilio hynny a'i ddefnyddio. Ond rydw i hefyd yn awyddus bod atebolrwydd deallus yn ein system ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd hynny'n taro tant ymhlith llawer o'r partneriaid rydym ni wedi gweithio gyda nhw dros y blynyddoedd. Nid yw dweud rhywbeth yn golygu ei fod yn cael ei wneud—mae angen i chi wneud iddo weithio ar lefel ysgol, mae angen i chi ei wneud yn atebol yn ddeallus, o'u safbwynt nhw a hefyd o'n safbwynt ni. Rydym yn ceisio mynd i'r afael â materion yn y system yng Nghymru; nid yw mewnforio pethau a'u cymhwyso heb feddwl yn gweithio yn y cyd-destun hwnnw. Mae angen i ni wneud gwelliannau yma yn ein cyd-destun ni ein hunain gyda'n dysgwyr ein hunain.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn am iechyd meddwl, a bydd yn rhaid i mi ddod yn ôl atoch chi o ran y diweddariad, oherwydd ni allaf gofio'n iawn. Ond mae iechyd meddwl yn flaenoriaeth allweddol, oherwydd rydym ni'n gwybod mai dyma un o'r rhesymau sy'n effeithio, er enghraifft, ar bresenoldeb. Felly, os ydym am wneud gwahaniaeth i'r dysgwyr hyn o ran llythrennedd a rhifedd, bydd angen iddynt fod yn yr ysgol i allu cael mynediad at hynny. Bydd angen y gefnogaeth arnynt i allu ymgysylltu â'r cwricwlwm. Felly mae hynny'n parhau, rydym ni'n gwybod, yn flaenoriaeth frys. Ac yn enwedig ar ôl COVID, mae rhai o'r materion hyn yn—beth yw'r gair—yn ddwys i lawer o ddysgwyr a bydd angen i'r gefnogaeth honno fod yno, os ydynt am gael eu cefnogi'n dda ac elwa ar y cynlluniau sydd gennym.

Roedd cwestiwn wedyn ynglŷn ag adolygu'r grant datblygu disgyblion. Nid wyf wedi gwneud unrhyw benderfyniadau ynghylch hwnnw. Ond rwy'n ceisio sicrhau bod popeth a wnawn yn cefnogi nodau'r cynllun hwn, ac yn cefnogi ein gweithlu a phob rhan o'n system addysg i weithredu'r gwelliannau hyn a'u cefnogi fel unigolion ynddo hefyd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Oh, targeted review. Sorry, I knew there was something else. Sorry. It was the curriculum review. It will be targeted. I am very keen that nobody in the system hears any intent on my part to depart from Curriculum for Wales and start with a new clean sheet of paper and involve us in another 15 years of a new curriculum. I don't think we need that. I have seen Curriculum for Wales make a genuine difference. It's an engaging curriculum, it's appropriate in that it values the widest possible range of educational competencies. Including putting the same value on humanities and expressive arts and numeracy is important, I think, particularly now. Somebody mentioned AI earlier on; the human development aspect of education is important, and we want to preserve that. Having said that, literacy and numeracy is the gateway into doing well in all of these areas and I think there is a genuine call for a greater element of clarity around some aspects of the curriculum, and that's what I'm discussing, as I'm going to put together a group of experts—I've spoken to 12 so far and I'm going to select a smaller group than 12, otherwise we'll be at it for five years—to look at a targeted review that will be helpful in the system without breaking the intent of Curriculum for Wales, and that's what I'm asking them to undertake. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: O, adolygiad wedi'i dargedu. Mae'n ddrwg gen i, roeddwn i'n gwybod bod rhywbeth arall. Mae'n ddrwg gen i. Adolygiad y cwricwlwm oedd hwn. Bydd yn cael ei dargedu. Rwy'n awyddus iawn nad oes neb yn y system yn clywed unrhyw fwriad ar fy rhan i i ymadael â'r Cwricwlwm i Gymru a dechrau â thaflen bapur lân, newydd gan achosi i ni wynebu 15 mlynedd arall o gwricwlwm newydd. Nid wyf yn credu bod angen hynny. Rwyf wedi gweld y Cwricwlwm i Gymru yn gwneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol. Mae'n gwricwlwm diddorol, mae'n briodol gan ei fod yn gwerthfawrogi'r ystod ehangaf posibl o gymwyseddau addysgol. Mae cynnwys rhoi'r un gwerth ar y dyniaethau a'r celfyddydau mynegiannol a rhifedd yn bwysig, rwy'n credu, yn enwedig nawr. Soniodd rhywun am AI yn gynharach; mae'r agwedd datblygiad dynol ar addysg yn bwysig, ac rydym eisiau cadw hynny. Wedi dweud hynny, llythrennedd a rhifedd yw'r porth ar gyfer gwneud yn dda ym mhob un o'r meysydd hyn ac rwy'n credu bod galwad gwirioneddol am fwy o eglurder ynghylch rhai agweddau ar y cwricwlwm, a dyna beth rwy'n ei drafod, gan fy mod i'n mynd i greu grŵp o arbenigwyr—rydw i wedi siarad â 12 hyd yma ac rydw i'n mynd i ddewis grŵp sy'n llai na 12, fel arall byddwn wrthi am bum mlynedd—i edrych ar adolygiad wedi'i dargedu a fydd yn ddefnyddiol yn y system heb dorri bwriad Cwricwlwm i Gymru, a dyna beth rwy'n gofyn iddyn nhw ymgymryd ag ef. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cabinet Minister, I'm sure you'd be fascinated to hear that I had a very interesting start to my day today, because I had the privilege of formally welcoming Logos Hope to Cardiff Bay, the ship that's docked here for three weeks. I would encourage all Members of the Chamber to take a visit, if you get a chance. It's the world's largest floating book fair. Now, I'm not sure how many floating book fairs there are, but this is the biggest one in the world. On that ship, there are around 350 volunteers of 50 different nationalities going around the world supporting children particularly with their literacy and education, and they do an incredible job.

But the reason I mention it now is that, in one of the contributions by the managing director on the ship today, he invoked the spirit of Griffith Jones and pointed out the literacy heritage that we have here in Wales and, of course, his work on the circulating schools in the eighteenth century, and the global reputation. There are over 50 nationalities on this ship and they recognise the heritage we have here in Wales around literacy in particular. It struck me, as I sat there, where we, sadly, find ourselves at the moment. You opened your statement by pointing to the fact that it's not all about PISA, but clearly the OECD are pointing to our downward trend at the moment in particular on reading and maths, and I know it's a wake-up call for you, but, in particular, it's a concern that parents have of children in schools and they recognise that far too many children are leaving school without the strong foundations that they need.

So, I wonder, as my first question to you, after years of promises to raise standards—and parents have heard this before and teachers have heard this before—what confidence can you give to parents and teachers that this plan will finally deliver the improvement that they've been waiting for? And let me point out, Cabinet Minister, the things that I am really supportive of on this here, in particular the focus on the nought-16 approach, I think that's very helpful; literacy and numeracy don't suddenly start when a child walks through the school gates, and we need to understand where children are starting from, track that progress and identify where support is needed before problems become entrenched. That goes back to that point around the parental involvement. I was really pleased to see, in your actual plan, foundation 1, which is the role of parents and carers, and let me encourage you to push as strongly as possible in that area, because we know the huge difference that good parenting and support at home can make to those children in their first few years. I also welcome the proposed year 6 indicator. If a child is struggling with reading and numeracy at the end of primary school, the secondary school needs to know that as best as possible, but good information sharing can make a real difference to that transition and to the support that children receive. So, I wonder if you would outline more clearly how the Welsh Government will ensure that this information actually leads to earlier and better support.

I do have some concerns, as I'm sure you'd expect, and some of those are around how this works in practice. I think colleagues have already mentioned the existing workload that teachers have, and I know you've responded to some of that. They don't want more paperwork, they don't want more bureaucracy, they don't want more sand in the system; they want this to work as smoothly as possible. So, I wonder, in your response to me, if you can give those reassurances that you recognise that again, and that, whilst we're asking schools to set ambitious targets, they'll be given the resources, training and support to be able to achieve this.

I also noticed in the opening of your plan document, Cabinet Minister, that you point out, and I'll quote here, that:

'A sustained period of reform has taken its toll, and literacy and numeracy have been lost in the noise.'

You go on, though, to say that the new plan is deliberate—I can't say the word; my literacy skills need to be improved—

'deliberately iterative and will be subject to ongoing review and evaluation'.

Now, those two things, perhaps, seem to fight each other, and I wonder what assurances you can give to our schools that—. You pointed out that all this reform has taken a lot of energy in the system, but then go on to say that they'll be subject to ongoing review and evaluation. So, I think schools would want to know how are you going to get that tension right. How are you going to ensure that, whilst those reviews are important, actually, they need to be getting on with the job in hand?

I believe time is up, Deputy Presiding Officer, so I look forward to the response, but perhaps I have one moment. We cannot, of course, decouple literacy and numeracy outcomes from some basic expectations in schools. I questioned the First Minister earlier around how we're going to address classroom behaviours, because, for children to gain those literacy and numeracy skills, they need to be in the best place possible in the classroom around behaviours as well. So, I'd appreciate any response on that as well. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Weinidog Cabinet, rwy'n siŵr y byddech wrth eich bodd yn clywed fy mod wedi cael dechrau diddorol iawn i'm diwrnod heddiw, oherwydd cefais y fraint o groesawu Logos Hope yn ffurfiol i Fae Caerdydd, y llong sydd wedi docio yma am dair wythnos. Byddwn yn annog holl Aelodau'r Siambr i ymweld â hi, os cewch gyfle. Dyma'r ffair lyfrau arnofiol fwyaf yn y byd. Nawr, nid wyf yn siŵr faint o ffeiriau llyfrau arnofiol sydd yna, ond dyma'r un fwyaf yn y byd. Ar y llong honno, mae tua 350 o wirfoddolwyr o 50 o wahanol genhedloedd yn mynd o gwmpas y byd yn cefnogi plant yn enwedig gyda'u llythrennedd a'u haddysg, ac maen nhw'n gwneud gwaith anhygoel.

Ond y rheswm yr wyf yn sôn amdano nawr yw hyn, yn un o gyfraniadau y rheolwr gyfarwyddwr ar y llong heddiw, fe gyfeiriodd at ysbryd Griffith Jones a thynnu sylw at y dreftadaeth llythrennedd sydd gennym yma yng Nghymru ac, wrth gwrs, ei waith ar yr ysgolion cylchynol yn y ddeunawfed ganrif, a'r enw da byd-eang. Mae dros 50 o genhedloedd ar y llong hon ac maen nhw'n cydnabod y dreftadaeth sydd gennym yma yng Nghymru o ran llythrennedd yn arbennig. Fe wnaeth fy nharo i, wrth i mi eistedd yno, lle rydym ni, yn anffodus, yn cael ein hunain ar hyn o bryd. Fe wnaethoch chi agor eich datganiad trwy dynnu sylw at y ffaith nad yw e i gyd yn ymwneud â PISA, ond yn amlwg mae'r Sefydliad ar gyfer Cydweithrediad a Datblygiad Economaidd yn cyfeirio at ein tuedd tuag at i lawr ar hyn o bryd yn arbennig o ran darllen a mathemateg, ac rwy'n gwybod ei fod yn rhybudd i chi, ond, yn arbennig, mae'n bryder sydd gan rieni ynghylch eu plant blant mewn ysgolion ac maen nhw'n cydnabod bod llawer gormod o blant yn gadael yr ysgol heb y sylfeini cadarn sydd eu hangen arnynt.

Felly, tybed, fel fy nghwestiwn cyntaf i chi, ar ôl blynyddoedd o addewidion i godi safonau—ac mae rhieni wedi clywed hyn o'r blaen ac mae athrawon wedi clywed hyn o'r blaen—pa hyder allwch chi ei gynnig i rieni ac athrawon y bydd y cynllun hwn o'r diwedd yn cyflawni'r gwelliant y maen nhw wedi bod yn aros amdano? A gadewch i mi nodi, Weinidog Cabinet, y pethau rydw i'n wirioneddol gefnogol ohonyn nhw yma, yn enwedig y ffocws ar y dull gweithredu 0-16, rwy'n credu bod hynny'n ddefnyddiol iawn; nid yw llythrennedd a rhifedd yn dechrau yn sydyn pan fydd plentyn yn cerdded trwy gatiau'r ysgol, ac mae angen i ni ddeall o ble mae plant yn dechrau, olrhain y cynnydd hwnnw a nodi lle mae angen cefnogaeth cyn i broblemau ymwreiddio. Mae hynny'n mynd yn ôl i'r pwynt hwnnw ynghylch cyfranogiad rhieni. Roeddwn i'n falch iawn o weld, yn eich cynllun gwirioneddol, sylfaen 1, sef rôl rhieni a gofalwyr, a gadewch imi eich annog i wthio mor gryf â phosibl yn y maes hwnnw, oherwydd rydym yn gwybod y gwahaniaeth enfawr y gall rhianta a chefnogaeth dda gartref ei wneud i'r plant hynny yn eu blynyddoedd cyntaf. Rwyf hefyd yn croesawu'r dangosydd blwyddyn 6 arfaethedig. Os yw plentyn yn cael trafferth gyda darllen a rhifedd ar ddiwedd cyfnod yr ysgol gynradd, mae angen i'r ysgol uwchradd wybod hynny cystal â phosibl, ond gall rhannu gwybodaeth dda wneud gwahaniaeth gwirioneddol i'r trawsnewidiad hwnnw ac i'r gefnogaeth y mae plant yn ei derbyn. Felly, tybed a fyddech chi'n amlinellu'n gliriach sut y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau bod yr wybodaeth hon mewn gwirionedd yn arwain at gefnogaeth gynharach a gwell.

Mae gen i rai pryderon, fel rwy'n siŵr y byddech chi'n ei ddisgwyl, ac mae rhai o'r rheiny yn ymwneud â sut mae hyn yn gweithio yn ymarferol. Rwy'n credu bod cyd-Aelodau eisoes wedi sôn am y llwyth gwaith presennol sydd gan athrawon, ac rwy'n gwybod eich bod wedi ymateb i rywfaint o hynny. Nid ydynt eisiau mwy o waith papur, nid ydynt eisiau mwy o fiwrocratiaeth, nid ydynt eisiau mwy o dywod yn y system; maen nhw eisiau i hyn weithio mor ddidrafferth â phosibl. Felly, tybed, yn eich ymateb i mi, a allwch chi roi'r sicrwydd hynny eich bod chi'n cydnabod hynny eto, ac y byddant yn cael yr adnoddau, yr hyfforddiant a'r gefnogaeth i allu cyflawni hyn.

Sylwais hefyd yn agoriad eich dogfen gynllun, Weinidog Cabinet, eich bod chi'n nodi, ac fe ddyfynnaf:

'Mae cyfnod estynedig o ddiwygio wedi gadael ei ôl, ac mae'r ffocws ar lythrennedd a rhifedd wedi pylu.'

Rydych chi'n dweud drachefn fodd bynnag bod y cynllun newydd yn fwriadol—ni allaf ddweud y gair; mae angen gwella fy sgiliau llythrennedd—yn

'fwriadol ailadroddus a bydd yn cael ei adolygu a'i werthuso'n barhaus'.

Nawr, mae'n ymddangos bod y ddau beth hynny, efallai, yn ymladd yn erbyn ei gilydd, a meddwl ydw i tybed pa sicrwydd y gallwch chi ei roi i'n hysgolion bod—. Fe wnaethoch chi nodi bod yr holl ddiwygiad hwn wedi cymryd llawer o egni yn y system, ond yna fe ddywedwch y byddan nhw'n destun adolygiad a gwerthuso parhaus. Felly, rwy'n credu y byddai ysgolion eisiau gwybod sut ydych chi'n mynd i gael y tensiwn hwnnw'n iawn. Sut ydych chi'n mynd i sicrhau, er bod yr adolygiadau hynny'n bwysig, mewn gwirionedd, y bydd angen iddynt barhau â'r gwaith hwnnw?

Rwy'n credu bod fy amser ar ben, Ddirprwy Lywydd, felly edrychaf ymlaen at yr ymateb, ond efallai bod gen i un eiliad. Ni allwn, wrth gwrs, ddatgysylltu canlyniadau llythrennedd a rhifedd oddi wrth rhai disgwyliadau sylfaenol mewn ysgolion. Holais y Prif Weinidog yn gynharach ynglŷn â sut rydym ni'n mynd i fynd i'r afael ag ymddygiadau yn yr ystafell ddosbarth, oherwydd er mwyn i blant ennill y sgiliau llythrennedd a rhifedd hynny, mae angen iddyn nhw fod yn y lle gorau posibl yn yr ystafell ddosbarth o ran ymddygiadau hefyd. Felly, byddwn yn gwerthfawrogi unrhyw ymateb ar hynny hefyd. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a'r Gymraeg: Y Cynllun Llythrennedd a Rhifedd Sylfaenol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language: The Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Plan
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. I put 'deliberately iterative' in there just to trip people, probably including myself. It comes back to an earlier point that you made. It is important to keep an eye on the data that feeds our system. That's not quite the same thing as introducing new, big policy areas and the scale of reform, perhaps, we've had over the last 15 years. 

The previous education Minister mentioned PIRLS and TIMSS. We would be missing an opportunity if, as, say, a delivery board, we didn't, when they came, think about whether they might inform what we are doing. But to give us more information and more data, rather, because the planning itself, the expectations year-on-year—I think that has already been drafted with our literacy expert panel, for example—will be quite clear. But we want to keep an eye on this as time goes on and feed information into the system appropriately and well in order that we can make the progress we want to during this Senedd term. Education is a complex field, and we need to keep that conversation going. But I do think that understanding data, gleaning information from the system to inform our plan will be helpful rather than otherwise. If it proves unhelpful, I'm sure somebody will ask me about it at a later date, but that's certainly my intention.

Behaviour was touched on previously as well. Behaviour and support for learners are a key part of what we, as a Government, have prioritised in education. There is continued work that I can return to at a later date, perhaps, on the behaviour framework that seeks to bring services together to support schools as well, because some of those challenges can be difficult when you are also trying to focus on literacy and numeracy. So, that certainly will go hand in hand with this work as well.

Parents, yes, I agree, are part of this as well. Education, the schools system, cannot do this on its own. But I think it's also important to support parents with teaching reading and reading with their children. People are very pressurised. It can be difficult to find the time, but giving parents support around that is a key part of this plan as well. I think, frankly, I and others probably could do a better job at modelling our own reading. I'm very conscious that I read now less than I did, perhaps, 10 years ago—well, I know I do—so, I think there is a social element to this as well and how we model to other parents, but also to children that we too can read a book and put our phones aside occasionally.

Griffith Jones—coming back to Griffith Jones—is always a good thing. Catherine the Great, I think, took up his plans, didn't she, and exported them to Russia. A repeat of that would be really quite unsettling now. But I think this is an attempt as well to recharge. This is a social thing too. Everybody in our society needs to put a value on education if we're going to make a real difference. And I think allocating this responsibility just to schools, or just to parents, or any part of this system, is not going to be as powerful as everybody accepting that education is important—it is the thing that makes the difference to everybody in our society in Wales, and we all have a part to play in that. And we can thank Griffith Jones for showing us the way. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr. Rhoddais yn 'fwriadol ailadroddus' yno dim ond i faglu pobl, gan gynnwys fi fy hun yn ôl pob tebyg. Mae'n dod yn ôl at bwynt cynharach a wnaethoch chi. Mae'n bwysig cadw llygad ar y data sy'n bwydo ein system. Nid yw hynny'n hollol yr un peth â chyflwyno meysydd polisi newydd, mawr a graddfa'r diwygio, efallai, rydym ni wedi'i gael dros y 15 mlynedd diwethaf. 

Soniodd y Gweinidog dros addysg blaenorol am PIRLS a TIMSS. Byddwn yn colli cyfle pe bai, dyweder, o ran bwrdd cyflawni, pe bai ni ddim, pan ddaw, yn meddwl a allent lywio'r hyn yr ydym yn ei wneud. Ond i roi mwy o wybodaeth a mwy o ddata i ni, yn hytrach, oherwydd bydd y cynllunio ei hun, y disgwyliadau flwyddyn ar ôl blwyddyn—rwy'n credu bod hynny eisoes wedi'i ddrafftio gyda'n panel arbenigol llythrennedd, er enghraifft—yn eithaf clir. Ond rydym ni eisiau cadw llygad ar hyn wrth i amser fynd ymlaen a bwydo gwybodaeth i'r system yn briodol ac yn dda er mwyn i ni allu gwneud y cynnydd rydyn ni eisiau ei wneud yn ystod tymor y Senedd hon. Mae addysg yn faes cymhleth, ac mae angen i ni gadw'r sgwrs honno i fynd. Ond rwy'n credu y bydd deall data, casglu gwybodaeth o'r system i lywio ein cynllun yn ddefnyddiol yn hytrach nag fel arall. Os nad yw'n ddefnyddiol, rwy'n siŵr y bydd rhywun yn gofyn i mi amdano yn nes ymlaen, ond dyna fy mwriad yn sicr.

Cyfeiriwyd at ymddygiad o'r blaen hefyd. Mae ymddygiad a chefnogaeth i ddysgwyr yn rhan allweddol o'r hyn rydym ni, fel Llywodraeth, wedi'i flaenoriaethu mewn addysg. Mae gwaith parhaus y gallaf ddychwelyd ato yn nes ymlaen, efallai, ar y fframwaith ymddygiad sy'n ceisio dod â gwasanaethau at ei gilydd i gefnogi ysgolion hefyd, oherwydd gall rhai o'r heriau hynny fod yn anodd pan fyddwch hefyd yn ceisio canolbwyntio ar lythrennedd a rhifedd. Felly, bydd hynny'n sicr yn mynd law yn llaw â'r gwaith hwn hefyd.

Mae rhieni, ydynt, rwy'n cytuno, yn rhan o hyn hefyd. Ni all addysg, y system ysgolion, wneud hyn ar ei phen ei hun. Ond rwy'n credu ei bod hefyd yn bwysig cefnogi rhieni gydag addysgu darllen a darllen gyda'u plant. Mae pobl dan bwysau mawr. Gall fod yn anodd dod o hyd i'r amser, ond mae rhoi cefnogaeth i rieni ynghylch hynny yn rhan allweddol o'r cynllun hwn hefyd. Rwy'n credu, i fod yn onest, y gallwn i ac eraill wneud yn well wrth fodelu ein darllen ein hunain. Rwy'n ymwybodol iawn fy mod i'n darllen llai nawr nag yr oeddwn i, efallai, 10 mlynedd yn ôl—wel, rwy'n gwybod fy mod i'n gwneud hynny—felly, rwy'n credu bod elfen gymdeithasol i hyn hefyd a sut rydym ni'n modelu i rieni eraill, ond hefyd i blant y gallwn ni hefyd ddarllen llyfr a rhoi ein ffonau o'r neilltu o bryd i'w gilydd.

Mae Griffith Jones—gan ddod yn ôl at Griffith Jones—bob amser yn beth da. Cymerodd Catrin Fawr, rwy'n credu, ei gynlluniau a'u hallforio nhw i Rwsia. Byddai ailadrodd hynny yn eithaf annifyr nawr. Ond rwy'n credu bod hwn yn ymgais hefyd i atgyfnerthu. Mae hyn yn beth cymdeithasol hefyd. Mae angen i bawb yn ein cymdeithas roi gwerth ar addysg os ydym am wneud gwahaniaeth go iawn. Ac rwy'n credu nad yw dyrannu'r cyfrifoldeb hwn i ysgolion yn unig, neu i rieni yn unig, neu unrhyw ran o'r system hon, yn mynd i fod mor bwerus â phawb yn derbyn bod addysg yn bwysig—dyma'r peth sy'n gwneud y gwahaniaeth i bawb yn ein cymdeithas yng Nghymru, ac mae gan bob un ohonom ran i'w chwarae yn hynny. A gallwn ddiolch i Griffith Jones am ddangos y ffordd i ni. Diolch yn fawr.
