XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Jayne. I agree with the point that you made in opening there, about the first few weeks of a baby's life being of essential importance in terms of not just their welfare, but the welfare of everyone around that baby, about the entire family. I know, from the role that you previously played, this is something very close to your heart as well, and I commend you for everything that you did in that role. I know it's something that is still really important to you.

In terms of the assurance assessment of neonatal services that women helped shape, as you're saying, yes, I'm very happy to confirm that the recommendations of 'The path to safer beginnings' are indeed going to be implemented. I'm very happy to confirm that. Again, I know that there will be people who will be watching this who will say, 'Oh, yes, but they have reports and they have recommendations and they're accepted, but not enough changes'. We cannot get this wrong. This is something that transcends politics. This is about ensuring that more babies get the care that they need when they need it, and making sure that we learn from when things have gone so horrifically wrong. So, yes, that is something of absolute essentialness, if that's a word.

In terms of midwifery—and of course, the point you make is absolutely true—none of this will be possible without the fantastic staff who are helping women and families every day. I do recognise the pressures on the midwifery workforce with maternity services. They play that vital role in delivering safe and sustainable maternity care, of course. The Welsh Government does continue to invest in the education, the training, the retention of the workforce. As I've said, we are committed to delivering the recommendations on that as well from 'The path to safer beginnings', and that includes developing a workforce acuity tool that reflects the current requirements in maternity services and a workforce model that's fit for the future. In the meantime, health boards have to plan, they have to deploy their workforce effectively using the current Birthrate Plus workforce planning tool, to ensure that those services are staffed safely and sustainably.

On the situation of midwifery graduates, I recognise the ongoing uncertainty that's facing so many of our newly qualified midwives. That, of course, is a situation that we inherited. But from the graduate summit that my colleague the health Minister had convened earlier in the summer, we're making sure that we are maximising employment opportunities, that we're working with Health Education and Improvement Wales and with NHS Wales to make sure that we are providing that practical support, that we're ensuring the lessons from this year's recruitment cycle can inform future workforce planning. But crucially, that every opportunity is maximised for those young people, and my thoughts are with them, absolutely.

Finally, the workforce plan is being developed. This will be part of the consideration in terms of perinatal mental health. This was something that was really important to my predecessor in this role, Steffan Lewis. I know, again, it's something that is really important to you. If ever it would be helpful—and I'd extend this to Members, to spokespeople, across the Chamber—to have a further meeting to discuss that in greater depth, I'd be really happy to do that. Diolch, Jayne. Thank you for that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Jayne. Rwy'n cytuno â'ch sylwad agoriadol chi yn y fan yna, ynghylch bod wythnosau cyntaf bywyd babi yn hanfodol bwysig nid yn unig o ran eu lles, ond lles pawb sy'n ymwneud â'r babi hwnnw, am y teulu cyfan. Rwy'n gwybod, o'ch swyddogaeth flaenorol, fod hwn yn rhywbeth sy'n agos iawn at eich calon chi hefyd, ac rwy'n eich canmol am bopeth a wnaethoch chi yn y swyddogaeth honno. Rwy'n gwybod ei fod yn rhywbeth sy'n dal i fod yn bwysig iawn i chi.

O ran yr asesiad sicrwydd o wasanaethau newyddenedigol y mae menywod wedi helpu i'w llunio, fel rydych chi'n dweud, ydw, rwy'n hapus iawn i gadarnhau bod argymhellion 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel' yn mynd i gael eu gweithredu. Rwy'n hapus iawn i gadarnhau hynny. Unwaith eto, rwy'n gwybod y bydd yna bobl a fydd yn gwylio hyn a fydd yn dweud, 'O, ie, ond mae ganddyn nhw adroddiadau ac mae ganddyn nhw argymhellion ac maen nhw'n cael eu derbyn, ond dim digon o newidiadau'. Ni allwn ni gael hyn yn anghywir. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n uwch na gwleidyddiaeth. Mae hyn yn ymwneud â sicrhau bod mwy o fabanod yn cael y gofal sydd ei angen arnyn nhw pan fydd ei angen arnyn nhw fwyaf, a gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn dysgu o'r adegau pan fydd pethau wedi mynd mor ofnadwy o anghywir. Felly, ydy, mae hynny'n rhywbeth o hanfodolwrydd mawr, os yw hynny'n air.

O ran bydwreigiaeth—ac wrth gwrs, mae'r pwynt rydych chi'n ei wneud yn hollol wir—ni fydd unrhyw elfen o hyn yn bosibl heb y staff gwych sy'n helpu menywod a theuluoedd bob dydd. Rwyf yn cydnabod y pwysau ar y gweithlu bydwreigiaeth gyda gwasanaethau mamolaeth. Maen nhw'n gwneud y gwaith hanfodol hwnnw o ddarparu gofal mamolaeth diogel a chynaliadwy, wrth gwrs. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn parhau i fuddsoddi mewn addysg, hyfforddiant, dal gafael ar y gweithlu. Fel y dywedais i, rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i gyflawni'r argymhellion ar hynny hefyd o 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel', ac mae hynny'n cynnwys datblygu offeryn aciwtedd gweithlu sy'n adlewyrchu'r gofynion presennol mewn gwasanaethau mamolaeth a model gweithlu sy'n addas ar gyfer y dyfodol. Yn y cyfamser, mae'n rhaid i fyrddau iechyd gynllunio, mae'n rhaid iddyn nhw ddefnyddio'u gweithlu yn effeithiol gan ddefnyddio'r offeryn cynllunio gweithlu Birthrate Plus presennol, i sicrhau bod y gwasanaethau hynny'n cael eu staffio'n ddiogel ac yn gynaliadwy.

O ran sefyllfa graddedigion bydwreigiaeth, rwy'n cydnabod yr ansicrwydd parhaus sy'n wynebu cymaint o'n bydwragedd sydd newydd gymhwyso. Mae hynny, wrth gwrs, yn sefyllfa a etifeddwyd gennym ni. Ond o'r uwchgynhadledd graddedigion yr oedd fy nghyd-Aelod y Gweinidog iechyd wedi'i chynnull yn gynharach yn yr haf, rydym ni'n gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn gwneud y mwyaf o gyfleoedd cyflogaeth, ein bod yn gweithio gydag Addysg a Gwella Iechyd Cymru a gyda Gwasanaeth Iechyd Gwladol Cymru i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn darparu'r cymorth ymarferol hwnnw, ein bod yn sicrhau y gall y gwersi o'r cylch recriwtio eleni lywio cynllunio'r gweithlu yn y dyfodol. Ond yn hollbwysig, y rhoddir pob cyfle posibl i'r bobl ifanc hynny, ac rwy'n cydymdeimlo gyda nhw, yn llwyr.

Yn olaf, mae'r cynllun gweithlu yn cael ei ddatblygu. Bydd hyn yn rhan o'r ystyriaeth o ran iechyd meddwl amenedigol. Roedd hyn yn rhywbeth a oedd yn bwysig iawn i'm rhagflaenydd yn y swydd hon, Steffan Lewis. Rwy'n gwybod, unwaith eto, ei fod yn rhywbeth sy'n bwysig iawn i chi. Os byddai'n ddefnyddiol—ac rwy'n dweud hyn wrth Aelodau, wrth lefarwyr, ar draws y Siambr—i gael cyfarfod pellach i drafod hynny yn fanylach, byddwn yn hapus iawn i wneud hynny. Diolch, Jayne. Diolch am hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I thank you, Minister, for bringing forward this statement? Your passion about this subject is clearly evident, and it's something that is important to all of us. Every family has the right to expect that if they raise concerns at any stage, those concerns will be listened to, they'll be taken seriously and acted upon. The principle behind Call for Concern is therefore one that I think every Member in this Chamber can support.

However, with so many of these NHS initiatives, success will ultimately depend on the practical reality of implementation, hence the various similar questions we're all going to be asking of you. Minister, you have set out plans to roll out Call for Concern across Wales, and outlined work already under way across a number of health boards. That is a welcome ambition, but families expect the same standards of care regardless of where they live. Now, I wonder, Minister, can you explain how the Welsh Government will independently assess whether women and families are receiving that same experience of Call for Concern in every health board? I think you've partly answered that in an earlier question. It's so important that there is access to that same level of care, and it's important that there is a process put in place to measure that.

Minister, you've spoken about empowering women and families to raise concerns when they believe something is wrong, and that's absolutely the correct approach. But empowerment only exists if people know that the system is there in the first place. Too often, families have spoken about not knowing how to escalate concerns or challenge decisions at the time they were most worried. Simply creating a process does not guarantee that it will be used. Minister, you have acknowledged the importance of ensuring women and families are aware of the system and feel confident enough to use it. Can you therefore tell us how the Government intends to measure awareness amongst patients and families, rather than simply assume that the information has been provided?

Whilst I recognise your emphasis on culture change, culture alone does not provide rapid clinical reviews. If concerns are escalated and additional assessments are required, who will undertake those reviews? What additional workforce capacity has been made available to support this programme and what specific funding has accompanied its implementation? Staff across our maternity and neonatal services already work under considerable pressure, as we know. They continue to do an outstanding job in difficult circumstances, but patient safety initiatives cannot operate on goodwill alone.

Llywydd, whilst I welcome the introduction of Call for Concern, it is important that we do not lose sight of the wider context. The reason such measures are necessary is because recent reviews have revealed serious concerns about maternity services across Wales. The review into services in Swansea bay identified repeated failings in care, governance and culture, while the national maternity assessment found that further improvements remain necessary across Wales. The Welsh Conservatives support measures that strengthen patient safety and amplify the voices of women and families. However, today's announcement will ultimately be judged not by its intentions, but by its outcomes. Families from across Wales deserve to know that, wherever they give birth, whoever is providing their care and whatever concerns they have, their voice will be heard, their concerns will be acted on and their safety and that of their baby will always come first. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
A gaf i ddiolch i chi, Weinidog, am gyflwyno'r datganiad hwn? Mae eich angerdd am y pwnc hwn yn amlwg, ac mae'n rhywbeth sy'n bwysig i bob un ohonom ni. Mae gan bob teulu yr hawl i ddisgwyl, os ydyn nhw'n codi pryderon ar unrhyw adeg, y gwrandewir ar y pryderon hynny, y byddan nhw'n cael eu cymryd o ddifrif ac y gweithredir arnyn nhw. Felly, mae'r egwyddor y tu ôl i Galwad am Bryder yn un y credaf y gall pob Aelod yn y Siambr hon ei gefnogi.

Fodd bynnag, gyda chymaint o'r mentrau Gwasanaeth Iechyd hyn, bydd llwyddiant yn y pen draw yn dibynnu ar realiti ymarferol gweithredu, sy'n esbonio'r gwahanol gwestiynau tebyg rydym ni i gyd yn mynd i'w gofyn i chi. Weinidog, rydych chi wedi nodi cynlluniau i gyflwyno Galwad am Bryder ledled Cymru, ac wedi amlinellu'r gwaith sydd eisoes yn cael ei wneud ar draws nifer o fyrddau iechyd. Mae hynny'n uchelgais i'w groesawu, ond mae teuluoedd yn disgwyl yr un safonau gofal waeth ble maen nhw'n byw. Nawr, tybed, Weinidog, a allwch chi esbonio sut y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn asesu yn annibynnol a yw menywod a theuluoedd yn cael yr un profiad o Galwad am Bryder ym mhob bwrdd iechyd? Rwy'n credu eich bod wedi ateb hynny'n rhannol mewn cwestiwn cynharach. Mae mor bwysig bod gofal o'r un safon ar gael, ac mae'n bwysig bod proses wedi'i sefydlu i fesur hynny.

Weinidog, rydych chi wedi siarad am rymuso menywod a theuluoedd i godi pryderon pan fyddan nhw'n credu bod rhywbeth o'i le, a dyna'n wir y ffordd gywir o fynd ati. Ond mae grymuso ond yn bosib dim ond os yw pobl yn gwybod bod y system yn bodoli yn y lle cyntaf. Yn rhy aml, mae teuluoedd wedi dweud nad oedden nhw'n gwybod sut i uwchgyfeirio pryderon neu herio penderfyniadau ar yr adeg roedden nhw'n poeni fwyaf. Nid yw creu proses yn gwarantu y bydd yn cael ei defnyddio. Weinidog, rydych chi wedi cydnabod pwysigrwydd sicrhau bod menywod a theuluoedd yn ymwybodol o'r system ac yn teimlo'n ddigon hyderus i'w defnyddio. Allwch chi felly ddweud wrthym ni sut mae'r Llywodraeth yn bwriadu mesur ymwybyddiaeth ymhlith cleifion a theuluoedd, yn hytrach na chymryd yn ganiataol bod yr wybodaeth wedi'i darparu?

Er fy mod i'n cydnabod eich pwyslais ar newid diwylliant, nid yw diwylliant ar ei ben ei hun yn darparu adolygiadau clinigol cyflym. Os caiff pryderon eu huwchgyfeirio ac mae angen asesiadau ychwanegol, pwy fydd yn ymgymryd â'r adolygiadau hynny? Pa gapasiti gweithlu ychwanegol sydd ar gael i gefnogi'r rhaglen hon a pha gyllid penodol sydd yna i'w gweithredu? Mae staff ar draws ein gwasanaethau mamolaeth a newyddenedigol eisoes yn gweithio o dan bwysau sylweddol, fel y gwyddom ni. Maen nhw'n parhau i wneud gwaith rhagorol mewn amgylchiadau anodd, ond ni all mentrau diogelu cleifion weithredu ar ewyllys da yn unig.

Lywydd, er fy mod i'n croesawu cyflwyno Galwad am Bryder, mae'n bwysig nad ydym yn colli golwg ar y cyd-destun ehangach. Y rheswm pam mae angen mesurau o'r fath yw oherwydd bod adolygiadau diweddar wedi datgelu pryderon difrifol am wasanaethau mamolaeth ledled Cymru. Mae'r adolygiad i wasanaethau ym Mae Abertawe wedi nodi methiannau dro ar ôl tro mewn gofal, llywodraethu a diwylliant, tra bod yr asesiad mamolaeth cenedlaethol wedi canfod bod angen gwelliannau pellach ledled Cymru. Mae'r Ceidwadwyr Cymreig yn cefnogi mesurau sy'n cryfhau diogelwch cleifion ac sy'n rhoi llais cryfach i fenywod a theuluoedd. Fodd bynnag, bydd y cyhoeddiad heddiw yn cael ei farnu yn y pen draw nid yn ôl ei fwriadau, ond yn ôl ei ganlyniadau. Mae teuluoedd o bob cwr o Gymru yn haeddu gwybod, lle bynnag maen nhw'n rhoi geni, pwy bynnag sy'n darparu eu gofal, a pha bynnag bryderon sydd ganddyn nhw, y gwrandewir ar eu llais, y gweithredir ar eu pryderon, ac y bydd eu diogelwch nhw a'u babi bob amser yn dod yn gyntaf. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Peter. I think that there is an awful lot where there will be, I would hope, agreement across the Chamber on this, and that's come out in the fact that I think that it does no harm to be reinforcing those same questions, because it is something so important for us to be repeating things like this, in terms of the point you made that success is, again, in the implementation. It isn't about whether a system exists, it's about whether the system works, whether it is going to lead to further empowerment and improvements in safety, which, again, could even mean lives being saved. So, it's something of fundamental importance.

You asked about ensuring that we need to make sure that there isn't a postcode lottery. Absolutely. In terms of how we stop that from happening, the Welsh health circular sets out that clear national expectation for health boards and trusts. Of course local arrangements will need to reflect individual services, but that core requirement has to be the same across Wales. And in terms of how we monitor that progress, it's going to be supported through national improvement networks. It's going to be monitored through established NHS governance and assurance arrangements as well.

You talked about empowering women, and, again, I agree entirely with you. In terms of—and it's an interesting point—how we can make sure that they know that this is available, which is something that Claire raised as well, so, practically, the things that we can do, there's going to be information provided by health boards during care—information leaflets, posters, bedside information, discussions with staff. Because, again, we can't just put a poster on the wall and think, 'Oh, well, it's there now, people will have to read it.' This is a very stressful time in someone's life, and they're not necessarily going to be looking at the poster on the wall. That's why it has to be embedded in the culture of the NHS. And that's something that, again, we're going to have to keep under continual review to see how well that is working.

In terms of how we assess how well it's working, I've laid that out. But in terms of the question that you raised, which is a really good question: how can we measure awareness levels? Of course, to a certain extent, how often it is used will be that, but that's a very crude way of looking at it. I'm going to speak to officials about what else could be possible, because I think that's a really good question.

And you mentioned staff pressures. Now, I do recognise, and this is something that Jayne alluded to as well, that there are huge pressures facing staff. Of course, and I'm sure that they would agree, patient safety has to be the priority. And so that's why it's intended to strengthen existing deterioration escalation arrangements; it's not meant to create a separate service that runs alongside them. Health boards will have to ensure, of course, that those local pathways are practical, that they're understood clearly, that they're supported by appropriate clinical leadership. But again, we need to keep this under review.

And finally, Llywydd, Peter, you asked, I suppose, why this is happening now, in a way, in terms of the wider context that we need to be aware of. Call for Concern isn't a response to any single review or investigation. It forms part of a wider programme to improve maternity and neonatal safety. But, of course, this doesn't exist in a vacuum. This is very timely today with the news that's coming out from England. We have to learn from reviews. We have to learn from inspections, investigations. Most importantly, we have to learn from the experiences of women and the experiences of families and make sure that, as you say, outcomes and making sure that people's lives are better—. That's the ultimate test.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Peter. Rwy'n credu bod yna gryn gytuno, rwy'n gobeithio, ar draws y Siambr ar hyn, ac mae hynny wedi ei weld yn y ffaith fy mod i'n credu nad yw'n gwneud unrhyw niwed i fod yn holi'r un cwestiynau hynny, oherwydd mae'n rhywbeth mor bwysig i ni fod yn ailadrodd pethau fel hyn, o ran y sylw a wnaethoch chi fod llwyddiant, eto, yn ymwneud â'r gweithredu. Nid yw'n ymwneud ag a yw system yn bodoli, mae'n ymwneud ag a yw'r system yn gweithio, a yw'n mynd i arwain at rymuso pellach a gwelliannau mewn diogelwch, a allai, unwaith eto, hyd yn oed olygu bod bywydau yn cael eu hachub. Felly, mae'n rhywbeth o bwysigrwydd sylfaenol.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn am sicrhau bod angen i ni wneud yn siŵr nad oes loteri cod post. Yn hollol. O ran sut rydym ni'n atal hynny rhag digwydd, mae cylchlythyr iechyd Cymru yn nodi'r disgwyliad cenedlaethol clir hwnnw ar gyfer byrddau ac ymddiriedolaethau iechyd. Wrth gwrs, bydd angen i drefniadau lleol adlewyrchu gwasanaethau unigol, ond mae'n rhaid i'r gofyniad craidd hwnnw fod yr un fath ledled Cymru. Ac o ran sut rydym ni'n monitro'r cynnydd hwnnw, bydd yn cael ei gefnogi trwy rwydweithiau gwella cenedlaethol. Bydd yn cael ei fonitro trwy drefniadau llywodraethu a sicrwydd sefydledig y Gwasanaeth Iechyd hefyd.

Fe wnaethoch chi siarad am rymuso menywod, ac, unwaith eto, rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr â chi. O ran—ac mae'n bwynt diddorol—sut y gallwn ni wneud yn siŵr eu bod yn gwybod bod hyn ar gael, sy'n rhywbeth a gododd Claire hefyd, felly, yn ymarferol, y pethau y gallwn ni eu gwneud, bydd gwybodaeth yn cael ei ddarparu gan fyrddau iechyd yn ystod gofal—taflenni gwybodaeth, posteri, gwybodaeth wrth ochr y gwely, trafodaethau gyda staff. Oherwydd, eto, ni allwn ni roi poster ar y wal a meddwl, 'O, wel, mae e yna nawr, bydd yn rhaid i bobl ei ddarllen.' Mae hwn yn gyfnod o straen mawr ym mywyd rhywun, ac nid ydyn nhw o reidrwydd yn mynd i fod yn edrych ar y poster ar y wal. Dyna pam mae'n rhaid iddo gael ei ymgorffori yn niwylliant y Gwasanaeth Iechyd. Ac mae hynny'n rhywbeth y bydd yn rhaid i ni ei adolygu'n barhaus i weld pa mor dda mae hynny'n gweithio.

O ran sut rydym ni'n asesu pa mor dda mae'n gweithio, rydw i wedi amlinellu hynny. Ond o ran y cwestiwn a godwyd gennych chi, sy'n gwestiwn da iawn: sut allwn ni fesur lefelau ymwybyddiaeth? Wrth gwrs, i ryw raddau, pa mor aml y mae'n cael ei ddefnyddio fydd hynny, ond mae hynny'n ffordd amrwd iawn o edrych arno. Rydw i'n mynd i siarad â swyddogion am beth arall allai fod yn bosibl, oherwydd rwy'n credu bod hynny'n gwestiwn da iawn.

Ac fe wnaethoch chi sôn am bwysau staff. Nawr, rwy'n cydnabod, ac mae hyn yn rhywbeth y cyfeiriodd Jayne ato hefyd, bod pwysau enfawr ar staff. Wrth gwrs, ac rwy'n siŵr y bydden nhw'n cytuno, mae'n rhaid i ddiogelwch cleifion fod y flaenoriaeth. Ac felly dyna pam mai'r bwriad yw cryfhau'r trefniadau presennol o ran uwchgyfeirio dirywiad; nid yw'n bwriadu creu gwasanaeth ar wahân sy'n rhedeg ochr yn ochr â nhw. Bydd yn rhaid i fyrddau iechyd sicrhau, wrth gwrs, bod y llwybrau lleol hynny'n ymarferol, eu bod yn cael eu deall yn glir, eu bod yn cael eu cefnogi gan arweinyddiaeth glinigol briodol. Ond eto, mae angen i ni adolygu hyn.

Ac yn olaf, Lywydd, Peter, fe wnaethoch chi ofyn, mae'n debyg, pam mae hyn yn digwydd nawr, mewn ffordd, o ran y cyd-destun ehangach y mae angen i ni fod yn ymwybodol ohono. Nid yw Galwad am Bryder yn ymateb i unrhyw adolygiad neu ymchwiliad unigol. Mae'n rhan o raglen ehangach i wella diogelwch mamolaeth a newyddenedigol. Ond, wrth gwrs, nid yw hyn yn bodoli mewn gwagle. Mae hyn yn amserol iawn heddiw gyda'r newyddion sydd i'w gweld yn Lloegr. Mae'n rhaid i ni ddysgu o adolygiadau. Mae'n rhaid i ni ddysgu o arolygiadau, ymchwiliadau. Yn bwysicaf oll, mae'n rhaid i ni ddysgu o brofiadau menywod a phrofiadau teuluoedd a gwneud yn siŵr bod bywydau pobl yn well—. Dyna'r prawf eithaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I really welcome today's statement on the expansion of the Call for Concern into maternity and neonatal services. And since being elected, I've heard from far too many families who have raised concerns about their own health or their partner's health, as well as that of their baby, but felt that they weren't listened to or taken seriously, as we've heard multiple times, and, as we know, sometimes with devastating consequences.

In preparation for today's statement, I've been made aware of staff working in adult in-patient wards in Cwm Taf Morgannwg, where Call for Concern is already in place, who have never heard of it. And I'm concerned that if staff aren't aware of the service, patients and families may not be either. So, I wonder if I could ask how the Welsh Government is working with health boards, and have a little bit more detail on that, to make sure that everybody involved, from the patient, families and staff, know about Call for Concern and have the information and training, and also how we make sure that families feel able to escalate those concerns without worrying that they're being difficult, or that it will affect their care. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n croesawu'n fawr y datganiad heddiw ar ehangu Galwad am Bryder i wasanaethau mamolaeth a newyddenedigol. Ac ers cael fy ethol, rwyf wedi clywed gan lawer gormod o deuluoedd sydd wedi codi pryderon am eu hiechyd eu hunain neu iechyd eu partner, yn ogystal â'u babi, ond yn teimlo na wrandawyd arnyn nhw na'u cymryd o ddifrif, fel yr ydym ni wedi clywed sawl gwaith, ac, fel y gwyddom ni, weithiau gyda chanlyniadau trychinebus.

Wrth baratoi ar gyfer y datganiad heddiw, rwyf wedi cael gwybod am staff sy'n gweithio mewn wardiau cleifion mewnol oedolion yng Nghwm Taf Morgannwg, lle mae Galwad am Bryder eisoes ar waith, nad ydyn nhw erioed wedi clywed amdano. Ac rwy'n pryderu, os nad yw staff yn ymwybodol o'r gwasanaeth, efallai na fydd cleifion a theuluoedd chwaith. Felly, tybed ga i ofyn sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gyda byrddau iechyd, a chael ychydig mwy o fanylion ar hynny, i wneud yn siŵr bod pawb sy'n gysylltiedig, o'r claf, teuluoedd a staff, yn gwybod am Galwad am Bryder ac yn cael yr wybodaeth a'r hyfforddiant, a hefyd sut rydym ni'n sicrhau bod teuluoedd yn teimlo eu bod yn gallu uwchgyfeirio'r pryderon hynny heb boeni eu bod yn drafferthus, neu y bydd yn effeithio ar eu gofal. Diolch.

—that women feel that they are truly empowered to be able to use their voice, and to feel more certain that their voice is going to be listened to.

I am concerned—. Okay, I will take that away, the point that you said about the lack of awareness among some members of the workforce. As I say, this is being rolled out at different timetables slightly over a period of weeks with different health boards, but would you mind writing to me with some of those specifics so I can look into that? XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thanks, Deputy Minister. It's a really serious thing that you've brought to our attention with postpartum. The maternity and birth statistics for 2025 show that 35 per cent of pregnant women in Wales report a mental health condition at initial assessment. Cwm Taf Morgannwg health board had the highest rate in Wales at 39 per cent. Deterioration in mental health during pregnancy or the postnatal period can be extremely rapid. One of the main clinical messages from MBRRACE-UK, in the report last year, was that it's important to recognise and act on red flags in maternal mental health, including significant change in mental state, thoughts or acts of violent self-harm, expression of incompetence as a mother, or estrangement from the infant. Could a call for concern in maternity services be made where the concern is psychiatric deterioration, including postpartum psychosis, acute suicide ideation, or a sudden change in behaviour?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Dirprwy Weinidog. Mae'n beth difrifol iawn rydych chi wedi'i ddwyn i'n sylw gyda gofal ôl-enedigol. Mae'r ystadegau mamolaeth a genedigaeth ar gyfer 2025 yn dangos bod 35 y cant o fenywod beichiog yng Nghymru yn adrodd cyflwr iechyd meddwl ar yr asesiad cychwynnol. Bwrdd iechyd Cwm Taf Morgannwg oedd â'r gyfradd uchaf yng Nghymru ar 39 y cant. Gall dirywiad mewn iechyd meddwl yn ystod beichiogrwydd neu'r cyfnod ôl-enedigol fod yn gyflym iawn. Un o'r prif negeseuon clinigol gan MBRRACE-UK, yn yr adroddiad y llynedd, oedd ei bod yn bwysig cydnabod a gweithredu ar iechyd meddwl mamau os oedd yna arwyddion pryderus, gan gynnwys newid sylweddol mewn cyflwr meddwl, meddyliau neu weithredoedd o hunan-niweidio treisgar, mynegiant o analluogrwydd fel mam, neu ymddieithrio oddi wrth y baban. A ellid codi pryder mewn gwasanaethau mamolaeth lle mae'r pryder yn ddirywiad seiciatrig, gan gynnwys seicosis ôl-enedigol, meddyliau dwys am hunanladdiad, neu newid sydyn mewn ymddygiad?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Gareth. I know the expertise that you bring to this area as well, so thank you for sharing that. Certainly we need to be learning from MBRRACE-UK on this. My understanding is that acute psychiatric problems, like what you've set out, would be covered by this. Again, it's making sure that this supplements and complements the support that is already there, that it doesn't look to sit alongside it. If a family member in the kind of situation that you are outlining notices something about the mother, that their mental health is deteriorating, they will be with them possibly every day, they will be with them hour after hour. They will see that deterioration in a way that a clinician might not, because they haven't seen them for as long. So, this is vitally important and this is something that I'm really passionate about. And I know that you're not just passionate about this, but you have an awful lot of expertise in this area as well. I really appreciate the fact that you've raised this because, absolutely, we can't afford to get this wrong. This is about women's lives. So, thank you for raising that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Gareth. Rwy'n gwybod am eich arbenigedd yn y maes yma hefyd, felly diolch am rannu hynny. Yn bendant, mae angen i ni ddysgu gan MBRRACE-UK yn hyn o beth. Fy nealltwriaeth i yw y byddai problemau seiciatrig acíwt, fel y rhai rydych chi wedi'u disgrifio, yn cael eu cynnwys yn hyn. Unwaith eto, mae'n bwysig sicrhau bod hyn yn ategu ac yn cyd-fynd â'r gefnogaeth sydd eisoes ar gael, yn hytrach na dim ond eistedd ochr yn ochr â hi. Os bydd aelod o'r teulu yn y math o sefyllfa rydych chi'n ei disgrifio yn sylwi ar rywbeth ynglŷn â'r fam, fel bod ei hiechyd meddwl yn dirywio, byddant gyda hi o bosibl bob dydd, awr ar ôl awr. Byddant yn gweld y dirywiad hwnnw mewn ffordd na fyddai clinigwr o bosibl yn ei weld, gan nad ydyn nhw wedi bod yn eu gweld am gyfnod mor hir. Felly, mae hyn yn hollbwysig ac yn rhywbeth rwy'n angerddol iawn yn ei gylch. Ac rwy'n gwybod nad ydych chi nid yn unig yn angerddol, ond bod gennych chi lawer iawn o arbenigedd yn y maes hwn hefyd. Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi'n fawr eich bod wedi codi'r mater hwn oherwydd, yn bendant, ni allwn ni fforddio gwneud camgymeriad yma. Mae hyn yn ymwneud â bywydau menywod. Felly, diolch i chi am wneud y sylw yna.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr to the Deputy Minister for her statement today. I'd like to start by sharing a constituent's experience. Megan Lewis is a recent midwifery graduate from the University of South Wales, and despite graduating with a first-class honours degree, Megan and 62 other graduates have been told that there are no band 5 vacancies for them. In her own words, Megan says, ‘We are being told we are not needed, but we are needed. I see it with my own eyes. The staff see it, the women and the families—we all see it.’

Safe staffing is not optional. I recently wrote to Cardiff and Vale health board who told me that they do not anticipate any vacancies in the near future, and are currently over-established by around 20 whole-time equivalent midwives. It feels like there's a disconnect between the experience on the ground and the staffing levels that health boards are required to maintain. The upcoming national workforce plan announced by the Government does present a valuable opportunity to shape the future of the workforce, so I wondered if the Deputy Minister could just give some clarity on how this will improve the way staffing demand and the commissioning of training courses will be aligned with each other.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr i'r Dirprwy Weinidog am ei datganiad heddiw. Fe hoffwn i ddechrau trwy rannu profiad etholwr. Mae Megan Lewis wedi graddio mewn bydwreigiaeth yn ddiweddar o Brifysgol De Cymru, ac er iddi raddio gyda gradd anrhydedd dosbarth cyntaf, dywedwyd wrth Megan a 62 o raddedigion eraill nad oes unrhyw swyddi gwag band 5 ar eu cyfer. Yn ei geiriau ei hun, dywed Megan, 'Rydym ni'n cael gwybod nad oes ein hangen ni, ond mae ein hangen ni. Rwy'n ei weld gyda fy llygaid fy hun. Mae'r staff yn ei weld, y menywod a'r teuluoedd—rydyn ni i gyd yn ei weld.'

Nid dewis yw staffio diogel. Ysgrifennais at fwrdd iechyd Caerdydd a'r Fro yn ddiweddar a ddywedodd wrthyf i nad ydyn nhw'n rhagweld unrhyw swyddi gwag yn y dyfodol agos, ac ar hyn o bryd bod ganddyn nhw ormod o staff, o oddeutu 20 o fydwragedd cyfwerth ag amser llawn. Mae'n teimlo fel bod datgysylltiad rhwng y profiad ar lawr gwlad a'r lefelau staffio y mae'n ofynnol i fyrddau iechyd eu cynnal. Mae'r cynllun gweithlu cenedlaethol sydd ar ddod a gyhoeddwyd gan y Llywodraeth yn cyflwyno cyfle gwerthfawr i lunio dyfodol y gweithlu, felly tybed a allai'r Dirprwy Weinidog roi rhywfaint o eglurder ynghylch sut y bydd hyn yn gwella'r ffordd y bydd y galw am staff a chomisiynu cyrsiau hyfforddi yn asio.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Zaynub, and thank you for your advocacy with this issue as well. This has come up already and I'll say again that I know that there are concerns about how reported staffing levels don't always reflect the pressures that are being experienced on the ground, and as you've alluded to, the 2026 student streamlining process has highlighted how vitally important it is that we ensure workforce planning, education commissioning and service requirements are closely aligned. Now, of course we need to learn lessons from that for future cohorts, but we vitally need to be supporting those graduates today—Megan and her fellow graduates. They are needed. Of course they are needed, and as a Government, we are doing everything that we can to maximise those employment opportunities, working again with HEIW and NHS Wales. I can only begin to imagine how difficult this time will be for Megan and for her fellow graduates. It is something that we absolutely are taking incredibly seriously. And, of course, this is feeding into the workforce plan.

In terms of our response to ‘The path to safer beginnings in Wales’ report, we're already working with NHS organisations to develop the future maternity workforce security tool that I mentioned earlier, which reflects better the complexity of care, where the future service demands are going to be, workforce requirements. And in that meantime period, health boards have to, of course, deploy their workforce effectively with the existing mandated planning tool Birthrate Plus. But, look, this is something that is hugely, hugely important, and the thoughts of everyone in this Chamber are going to be with that cohort, and I thank you, and other Members as well, for raising their concerns. They are needed. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Zaynub, a diolch am eich eiriolaeth gyda'r mater hwn hefyd. Mae hyn wedi codi eisoes, ac fe hoffwn i ail-ddweud fy mod i'n ymwybodol o'r pryderon ynghylch sut nad yw lefelau staffio a adroddir bob amser yn adlewyrchu'r pwysau a brofir ar lawr gwlad; ac fel y sonioch chi, mae'r broses symleiddio ar gyfer myfyrwyr yn 2026 wedi amlygu pa mor hanfodol bwysig yw hi i ni sicrhau bod cynllunio'r gweithlu, comisiynu addysg a gofynion gwasanaeth yn cyd-fynd yn agos. Wrth gwrs, mae angen i ni ddysgu gwersi o hynny ar gyfer carfanau'r dyfodol, ond mae angen dybryd arnom ni i gefnogi'r graddedigion hynny heddiw—Megan a'i chyd-raddedigion. Mae eu hangen nhw. Wrth gwrs bod eu hangen nhw, ac fel Llywodraeth, rydym ni'n gwneud popeth o fewn ein gallu i wneud y mwyaf o'r cyfleoedd cyflogaeth hynny, gan weithio unwaith eto gydag Addysg a Gwella Iechyd Cymru a Gwasanaeth Iechyd Gwladol Cymru. Prin y gallaf i ddychmygu pa mor anodd fydd y cyfnod hwn i Megan ac i'w chyd-raddedigion. Mae'n rhywbeth rydym ni'n ei gymryd yn gwbl o ddifrif. Ac wrth gwrs, mae hyn yn cyfrannu at y cynllun gweithlu.

O ran ein hymateb i'r adroddiad 'Y llwybr tuag at ddechrau mwy diogel yng Nghymru', rydym ni eisoes yn gweithio gyda sefydliadau'r Gwasanaeth Iechyd i ddatblygu'r offeryn diogelwch ar gyfer gweithlu gwasanaethau mamolaeth y dyfodol y soniais i amdano yn gynharach, sy'n adlewyrchu'n well cymhlethdod gofal, beth fydd gofynion gwasanaeth yn y dyfodol, gofynion y gweithlu. Ac yn y cyfamser, mae'n rhaid i fyrddau iechyd, wrth gwrs, ddefnyddio eu gweithlu yn effeithiol gyda'r offeryn cynllunio gorfodol presennol Birthrate Plus. Ond, edrychwch, mae hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n hynod o bwysig, a bydd meddyliau pawb yn y Siambr hon gyda'r garfan honno, ac rwy'n diolch i chi, ac Aelodau eraill hefyd, am godi eu pryderon. Mae eu hangen nhw. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. And thank you, Deputy Minister, for your statement. I have to give my own personal experience, which is somewhat a little bit different to many families. It was a really positive one and a really precious one, the way it should be. I gave birth in Singleton Hospital to two healthy boys in what they describe as a giant hot tub, but I have reminded them that it's not quite as relaxing as they do make out. But that to one side, I wish all mums and families had that same experience, but I can't ignore what other families do go through.

In May last year, Llais found that 76 per cent of women and families who used the same maternity services as I did at Singleton reported a negative experience or failures in their care. Two months later, families published their own review because, in their words, their trust in the health board had broken down completely. They identified failures in escalation, which we've discussed this afternoon. The independent review, published the very next day, found repeated failures in care, and complaints handling that simply wasn't good enough. Those services are still in level 4 intervention. So, Deputy Minister, what specific actions will you take to ensure escalation routes will work, when the last one failed? Because I'd love more women, families and babies to have the same experience as I did—maybe not always in the hot tub, but a better experience. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. A diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog, am eich datganiad. Mae'n rhaid i mi sôn am fy mhrofiad personol fy hun, sydd ychydig yn wahanol i lawer o deuluoedd. Roedd yn un cadarnhaol iawn ac yn un gwerthfawr iawn, fel y dylai fod. Fe wnes i roi genedigaeth yn Ysbyty Singleton i ddau fachgen iach yn yr hyn maen nhw'n ei ddisgrifio fel twba twym enfawr, ond rwyf wedi eu hatgoffa nad yw mor ymlaciol ag y maen nhw'n ei ddisgrifio. Ond rwy'n dweud hynny wrth fynd heibio, ac yn dymuno i bob mam a theulu gael yr un profiad, ond ni allaf anwybyddu'r hyn y mae teuluoedd eraill yn ei wynebu.

Ym mis Mai y llynedd, canfu Llais fod 76 y cant o fenywod a theuluoedd a ddefnyddiodd yr un gwasanaethau mamolaeth ag y gwnes i yn Singleton wedi adrodd profiad negyddol neu fethiannau yn eu gofal. Ddau fis yn ddiweddarach, cyhoeddodd teuluoedd eu hadolygiad eu hunain oherwydd, yn eu geiriau nhw, roedd eu hymddiriedaeth yn y bwrdd iechyd wedi chwalu'n llwyr. Fe wnaethon nhw nodi methiannau mewn uwchgyfeirio, yr ydym ni wedi eu trafod y prynhawn yma. Canfu'r adolygiad annibynnol, a gyhoeddwyd y diwrnod canlynol, fod methiannau dro ar ôl tro mewn gofal, ac nad oedd ymdrin â chwynion yn ddigon da. Mae'r gwasanaethau hynny yn dal i fod mewn ymyrraeth lefel 4. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, pa gamau penodol y byddwch chi'n eu cymryd i sicrhau bod llwybrau uwchgyfeirio yn gweithio, pan fethodd yr un diwethaf? Oherwydd byddwn i wrth fy modd i fwy o fenywod, teuluoedd a babanod gael yr un profiad â mi—efallai nid bob amser yn y twba twym, ond profiad gwell. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Sicrhau bod Menywod, Babanod a Theuluoedd yn Ganolog i Ddiogelwch: Gweithredu Call for Concern mewn Gwasanaethau Mamolaeth a Newyddenedigol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women's Health: Putting Women, Babies and Families at the Heart of Safety: The implementation of Call for Concern in Maternity and Neonatal Services
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for raising that. Look, I'm really glad that you had that positive experience. It should, like you say, be a precious experience for every family or every individual, and, too often, it isn't, of course, and I feel that we need to keep repeating that, for the vast majority of families, they will have a wonderful experience and life-changing in a fantastic way. For too many families, they have a life-changing experience in another way, and not just our thoughts, our action here has to be making sure that we are helping them. We have to learn from every investigation, whether that's in our own health boards, whether that's from investigations that are happening that are commissioned on a greater level, nationally, sometimes in other countries as well.

In terms of, as I've said, how we make sure that the escalation processes are followed, this has to sit alongside the tools that already exist, to complement them as that safeguard, so that it is yet another check and balance, and, crucially, it's a platform to make sure that women get their voice heard, that families get their concerns raised. As I've said, existing governance assurance arrangements are going to be used to make sure that we are monitoring this properly. But if I could say finally, Dirprwy—. Forgive me, I downgraded you then, sorry. If I can say finally, Llywydd—it's the first day back—that every family, every woman deserves to have the fantastic care that you've just set out. I can only imagine that this will have been a difficult statement for many families to listen to, and you are going to be in our thoughts as well. We have to get this right. And I really welcome the tone that everyone in the Chamber has taken this afternoon. Diolch. Diolch, Lywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am grybwyll hynny. Edrychwch, rwy'n falch iawn eich bod wedi cael y profiad cadarnhaol hwnnw. Dylai, fel rydych chi'n ei ddweud, fod yn brofiad gwerthfawr i bob teulu neu bob unigolyn, ac, yn rhy aml, dydy e ddim, wrth gwrs, ac rwy'n teimlo bod angen i ni barhau i ailadrodd hynny, i'r mwyafrif helaeth o deuluoedd, y byddan nhw'n cael profiad gwych sy'n newid eu bywydau mewn ffordd wych. I ormod o deuluoedd, maen nhw'n cael profiad sy'n newid eu bywydau mewn ffordd arall, ac nid dim ond ein meddyliau, rhaid i'n gweithredu yn hyn o beth wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n eu helpu. Mae'n rhaid i ni ddysgu o bob ymchwiliad, boed hynny yn ein byrddau iechyd ein hunain, boed hynny'n dod o ymchwiliadau a gomisiynir ar lefel uwch, yn genedlaethol, weithiau mewn gwledydd eraill hefyd.

O ran sut rydym ni'n gwneud yn siŵr bod y prosesau uwchgyfeirio yn cael eu dilyn, mae'n rhaid i hyn ddigwydd ochr yn ochr â'r prosesau sy'n bodoli eisoes, i'w hategu fel y broses ddiogelu honno, fel ei bod yn broses ddiogelu arall, ac, yn hollbwysig, mae'n llwyfan i wneud yn siŵr y clywir llais menywod, y codir pryderon teuluoedd. Fel y dywedais i, caiff y trefniadau sicrwydd llywodraethu presennol eu defnyddio i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn cadw golwg iawn ar hyn. Ond os gaf i ddweud yn olaf, Ddirprwy—. Maddeuwch i mi, fe wnes i eich israddio yn y fan yna, mae'n ddrwg gen i. Ond os ga i ddweud yn olaf, Lywydd—dyma'r diwrnod cyntaf yn ôl—bod pob teulu, pob menyw, yn haeddu cael y gofal gwych rydych chi newydd ei amlinellu. Allaf i ond dychmygu y bu hwn yn ddatganiad anodd i lawer o deuluoedd ei glywed, a byddwn yn meddwl amdanoch chi hefyd. Mae'n rhaid i ni wneud hyn yn iawn. Ac rwy'n croesawu'n fawr natur foneddigaidd pawb yn y Siambr y prynhawn yma. Diolch. Diolch, Lywydd.
